# Pietro Galatino’s Work on the Secrets 
# of Catholic Truth.

->That is,<-

## A most complete commentary on all the difficult passages of the Old Testament,
## drawn from the Talmud and other Hebrew books, written both before 
## the birth of CHRIST and after, against the stubborn lack of faith 
## <note>original: "perfidiam." In the 16th century, this term was used by Christian polemicists to describe the Jewish rejection of Christ as the Messiah, emphasizing a "lack of faith" rather than the modern sense of "treachery."</note> of the Jews.

->To this is added,<-

## ❧ Three books by Johann Reuchlin of Pforzheim,
## Doctor of Laws, on the Art of the Kabbalah <term>Kabbalah: An ancient Jewish tradition of mystical interpretation of the Bible; Reuchlin was a pioneer in introducing these ideas to a Christian audience.</term>, 
## full of all kinds of learning.

->Moreover,<-

->WE HAVE ADDED a double Index: the first contains the subjects themselves, the other<-
->encompasses the explained obscure passages of Scripture.<-

## To the Reader.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial N in a square border with foliate and floral decorations.</image-desc>

**I**N OUR AGE, which is both unjust and polluted by unspeakable crimes, it is no wonder that all those old heresies—once put to rest and condemned by the Catholic <note>Here meaning the "universal" or "orthodox" Christian Church as it saw itself in the 16th century.</note> Church, in which alone the writings of the New and Old Testaments are held in esteem—should rightly sprout up again. For today, nearly everyone is permitted to propose to others whatever they have dreamed up at night or pondered during the day, following Satanic suggestions. And what is most astonishing is that these heresies always find followers and supporters who are so bold, so frivolous, and so shameless that they dare to thrust whatever comes into their mouths as a Divine oracle upon the simple-minded, who are easily led astray. The cautious are deceived and beautifully persuaded by the charm of words, so that they think everything these men babble was uttered as if from the tripod of Apollo <note>A reference to the Oracle at Delphi; the author is comparing heretical claims to pagan prophecies.</note> or spoken by **CHRIST** himself, the Son of God. Therefore, we are not warned in vain by **CHRIST** himself not to believe all those who say, "Behold, here is **CHRIST**, behold, there he is." <note>original: "Ecce, hîc est CHRISTVS, ecce illic." A reference to Matthew 24:23.</note> They are seduced, and they seduce others, so that they do not seem to wander in error alone. This, however, is the consolation of the Church: that God always raises up some from the elect to oppose these impious seducers, to refute the false dogmas being spread, and to bring forth the Truth from the <term>panoply</term> <note>From the Greek 'panoplia,' referring to a full suit of armor or a complete defensive set.</note> of the divine Scriptures, so that the false prophets have no escape, neither for answering nor for defending their own views. 

Professors of Theology ought to diligently drag this troop of impious men out from their hiding places using sound doctrine. Did not the Satanic progeny of Arius <note>Arius (c. 250–336 AD) taught that Christ was a created being, a view condemned as the Arian heresy.</note> cause much trouble for the pious, only to be finally destroyed by the word of **CHRIST**? Did not Samosatenus <note>Paul of Samosata, a 3rd-century bishop who held controversial views on the nature of Christ.</note> destroy himself with his own blade? Have not also the Anabaptists, Storch, Servetus, <note>Nicholas Storch and Michael Servetus were 16th-century radical reformers; Servetus was famously executed for his views on the Trinity.</note> and countless others been exposed to the mockery of the whole world because of the madnesses they devised without the authority of God's word? The same happens to all heretics. 

When, therefore, **PETRUS GALATINUS** <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), a Franciscan friar and scholar of Hebrew and the Kabbalah.</note> observed the arrogance, pride, and insolence of the Jews toward the Christian religion, he considered it his duty—since he had made no small progress in Hebrew letters—to finally bring something forward into the light. And indeed, he set his hand to the task successfully. He composed these Twelve Books, filled with every kind of erudition and learning, for the benefit of the Church of **CHRIST** (which is currently tossed about by various opinions) against that perfidious crowd which not only denies both the divinity and humanity of **CHRIST** even when convinced by the Scriptures, but also attacks all the Scriptures, especially those of Moses and the Prophets...

<summary>This preface introduces a defense of Christian doctrine against both Protestant "heretics" and Jewish scholarship, framing the work of Petrus Galatinus as a necessary academic and spiritual correction.</summary>

-> E P I S T L E <-

<meta>The text begins mid-sentence, continuing the thought that these heretics might</meta> ...invert [the truth], fashioning false interpretations, as much against the genuine sense of Scripture as against the Rabbis, whom he <note>Likely referring to the author or a specific opponent mentioned previously.</note> holds in the highest esteem. These are the same Rabbis who described the times of **CHRIST** so clearly that, among men of sound mind, the testimonies which the Talmudists <note>Scholars of the Talmud, the central text of Jewish civil and ceremonial law.</note> bring forward concerning the Kingdom of **CHRIST**, His Passion, and His Resurrection, are irrefutable.

**GALATINUS** <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), a Franciscan friar and scholar who wrote 'De Arcanis Catholicae Veritatis'.</note> is certainly a prudent man, absolutely learned in Hebrew, Chaldean <term>A historical term used here to refer to Aramaic.</term>, Greek, and Latin literature. He directs his writings toward a single goal (leaving the life of the Jews—which he views as devoted to greed, deceptive, and contaminated by various crimes—to God the judge). No one could more clearly hand down the promises made to the Fathers concerning **CHRIST**, namely to Adam, Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to Moses, the Prophets, David, and countless other faithful servants of God. To these, he describes the times in which the scepter was taken from the Jews, and their Judges—whom they called the **Sanhedrin** <term>The supreme council and tribunal of the Jewish people during the Second Temple period.</term>—were either driven out or killed. They have lost the use of their Sacrifices; they are without a Priesthood, without the multitude of Levites, and without a King, ever since the Temple was destroyed and all things were reduced to desolation. The miracles which once occurred both within and without the Temple have vanished, and these wretched people have been cast into every corner of the earth. These are certain signs that **CHRIST**, whom the holy Fathers expected, has come and has purged the world of sins.

Furthermore, their own Rabbis, whom they dare not deny, described those final times in beautiful words; so that, if they were not driven to madness against the religion of **CHRIST**, they could easily grasp the Truth. Yet this blinded nation proceeds with an obstinate mind, defending [their views] against their own conscience, devising false interpretations, and imagining an external Kingdom of **CHRIST** and a most splendid pageantry with which their Messiah is to enter.

I tell you, fair Reader, our Author treats all these matters so skillfully, in the manner of a dialogue, that you could desire nothing more in this regard. Whoever reads this book with an attentive mind will find great benefit when they wish to study <note>original: "euoluere," literally 'to unroll,' referring to the way one reads a scroll or a volume.</note> the Bible. The Author has focused his efforts especially on obscure and little-known passages, so that one can navigate the **Old Testament** without hesitation. Everything is divided into Chapters. Passages of Scripture are cited throughout, so that the reader’s mind does not waver for long in searching for the referenced locations. Moreover, he brings forward whatever has been said of **CHRIST** anywhere, using interpretations not gathered from common sources <note>original: "ex triuio," literally 'from the crossroads' or 'commonplace.'</note>, but from the Jewish Rabbis who wrote before the birth of **CHRIST** concerning the Messiah’s kingdom, as well as from Christian Doctors. You have here (to summarize much in a few words) a Commentary on all the difficult places of the entire **Old Testament**. Is there not a great treasure offered here, which a student of Theology cannot be without, except to his own greatest loss? As for the diligence which Dr. **Franciscus Stancarus** <note>Francesco Stancaro (1501–1574), an Italian Hebraist and theologian who likely edited or promoted this work.</note>, who is most highly skilled in Hebrew literature, [has applied...]

# TO THE READER.

...the effort employed in correcting these books, the Kind Reader will easily discover if he compares the old edition with this new one. No one believes how easily copies, even those accurately transcribed, are corrupted. 

The Kabbalistic <term>Kabbalah: a traditional Jewish system of mystical interpretation of the Scriptures.</term> writings of **Capnio** <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a prominent German humanist and Hebrew scholar; "Capnio" is the Greek version of his name, meaning "smoky."</note> have also been added—material well-suited to this work. In these, much mention is made of the ancient Fathers who awaited **CHRIST** the Redeemer with the deepest longing, and who knew perfectly well that lost salvation was to be recovered upon the wood <note>original: "in ligno"; a common theological shorthand for the wood of the Cross.</note>. 

But truly, good wine needs no hanging ivy <note>original: "uino uendibili non opus est suspensa hedera"; an ancient proverb meaning that a high-quality product needs no advertisement or "signpost" to attract people.</note>. All these things, however, are aimed at this: that the Church founded by the Apostles may be rebuilt, setting aside those sects and opinions which have never failed to bring in a sea of evils, and which have either altered or utterly overthrown all well-ordered states. 

->The Jews are a daily example to us,<-
->lest we fall into the wrath<-
->of God through unrepentance, after<-
->the Truth has been acknowledged. Farewell.<-

<meta>This page transitions from the introductory Hebrew testimonials found on the previous pages to the formal Latin dedication of the work. # To the most invincible Maximilian
## Caesar, Emperor of the Romans, ever August,
### An Epistle from Pietro Galatino of the Order of Friars Minor.

<image-desc>A large ornate woodcut initial letter "N" featuring a classical or mythological scene with two figures (possibly Hercules wrestling) in a landscape with trees.</image-desc>

For a long time now, I have been distressed by no small anxiety of mind, O Emperor **Maximilian**, ever August, as I witnessed the multifaceted and exceptional learning of **Capnio** <note>original: "Capnionis"; the Latinized name for Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous German humanist. The name is a Greek pun: *kapnos* means "smoke," just as the German *Rauch* does.</note> being so unworthily torn apart by the pestilential and poisonous bites of envious men. I saw that some even dared to falsely slander many of his sayings—which are in total agreement with the Orthodox faith—with the mark of heresy. I realized that this was being done as a poor, or rather a most wretched, example to all learned men: that after exhausting so much labor and so many sleepless nights, he should be repaid with such unjust treatment. 

Yet, I did not dare to write anything, nor even to open my mouth, to attempt to defend a man so learned and so outstanding in every kind of virtue against the reckless ignorance of the wicked. I feared that it might be attributed to me as a vice of rashness or arrogance if I—endowed with only mediocre talent and not sufficiently equipped with great erudition—should choose to act as an uninvited patron to a man so skilled and excellent in the <term>triple-tongued learning: the mastery of the three "sacred" languages: Latin, Greek, and Hebrew.</term> For such a man is more than capable of defending himself along with the truth itself.

However, my most reverend lord, Lord **Lorenzo Pucci**, Cardinal of the Four Crowned Saints <note>Lorenzo Pucci (1458–1531), an influential Italian cardinal and patron of the arts and sciences.</note>—a most sharp investigator of the Christian faith and most observant of Your Majesty (as is his duty)—urged me quite sharply to undertake this defense with a spirited mind. He did so because he believed Your Majesty’s own honor was at stake if even the suspicion of a crime were to touch your counselor. Thus, he compelled me to necessarily undergo the heavy burden of this task, which is far beyond my shoulders. 

In addition, the will of the Most Holy **Leo X**, the Supreme Pontiff, was a further factor that greatly impelled me to do this. For I was well aware that the Pope himself, as a singular cultivator of truth and wisdom, desired above all else that **Capnio** be freed from these slanders. He also wished to gratify Your Majesty in this matter, as he hoped to satisfy your wishes most vehemently. 

While I was uniquely intent upon this matter—sweating with all my strength to dig out the secrets found in the **Talmud** <note>original: "in Talmud"; Galatino argues that ancient Jewish texts contains hidden proofs for Christian doctrines.</note> which serve both the confirmation of the Catholic faith and the protection of **Capnio’s** cause—Your Majesty’s letters suddenly arrived. In them, you most kindly encouraged me to complete this work as quickly as possible, along with many other letters sent to the Supreme Pontiff...

<summary>Pietro Galatino dedicates his work to Emperor Maximilian I, explaining that he was moved by Cardinal Pucci and Pope Leo X to defend the scholar Johannes Reuchlin (Capnio) against charges of heresy by using evidence from the Talmud.</summary>

<keywords>Maximilian I, Johannes Reuchlin, Capnio, Pietro Galatino, Lorenzo Pucci, Pope Leo X, Talmud, heresy, Christian Hebraism, triple-tongued learning</keywords>

Having previously expressed his hesitation to defend Johannes Reuchlin (Capnio) due to his own perceived lack of talent, Galatinus now explains that the support of high-ranking church and state officials—including the "Catholic King" and various Cardinals—has emboldened him to finish and dedicate this work to the Emperor.</meta>

# TO MAXIMILIAN

...[and the Catholic] King <note>original: "Regemq[ue] Catholicum"; likely referring to Ferdinand II of Aragon or his successor Charles V, who held the title 'Catholic King.'</note>, and several Cardinal Fathers of the Christian aristocracy, who wrote most kindly in my favor. Moved by this extraordinary and almost incredible kindness, I began to urge my unfinished "vigils" <note>A common scholarly metaphor for works written late into the night.</note> more pressingly and ardently so they might hasten toward their conclusion. Furthermore, I decided to consecrate whatever these efforts might become to your divine majesty, so that they might come forth into the light under more favorable omens; and that, having shaken off the darkness of errors, they might reveal the light of **Truth** with much greater confidence. 

For it was not fitting that the **WORK ON THE SECRETS OF CATHOLIC TRUTH** <note>original: "OPVS DE ARCANIS CATHOLICÆ VERITATIS"; the title of the present volume by Pietro Galatino, first published in 1518.</note>, completed for the benefit of the <term>Christian Commonwealth: the unified political and spiritual community of Christian nations</term>, should be dedicated to any other than the finest preserver, defender, and promoter of both Catholic Truth itself and the entire Christian Commonwealth. If this dedication of mine should in no way prove equal to your Imperial Highness, I hope you will deign to consider it well and receive it with a peaceful countenance (as is your custom), knowing that it proceeded from a most devoted heart. 

->Receive it now, therefore, Most Sacred Emperor: and as I<-
->labor constantly in the vineyard of the Lord,<-
->receive, protect, and cherish me among the<-
->least of your Majesty’s servants (though<-
->unworthy) according to your clemency.<-

# Pietro Galatino’s Work on the Secrets of Catholic Truth.

->The participants of the entire work,<-
->GALATINUS, CAPNIO, HOOGSTRATEN.<-
<note>Galatinus is the author, Pietro Galatino; Capnio is the Greek-style pseudonym for the famous humanist Johannes Reuchlin; Hoogstraten refers to Jacob van Hoogstraten, a Dominican inquisitor and Reuchlin’s chief opponent.</note>

->GALATINUS,<-

<image-desc>Decorative historiated initial 'Q' containing a woodcut of a putto struggling within the circular frame of the letter.</image-desc>

As much as I am able to perceive from those things which have been said back and forth by you in my presence until now, a great debate is being waged between you concerning the **Talmud**, from which your entire controversy takes its origin. For one of you [Hoogstraten] endeavors to condemn the Talmud as entirely evil and utterly repugnant to the Christian religion; he contends to prove this with many articles formulated against the other’s little book, which is titled **THE EYEGLASS** <note>original: "OCVLARE SPECVLVM"; Reuchlin's 1511 defense of Jewish books, which sparked a massive legal and intellectual battle.</note>. The other [Reuchlin], truly, strives with the greatest zeal to defend the Talmud itself as being good in many parts, and extremely profitable, convenient, and necessary for the Catholic truth to crush the very stubborn "neck" <note>A biblical metaphor for stubbornness or pride.</note> of the Jews. 

Therefore, since both of you seem to seek nothing other than the truth—for (as I believe) you have both met with me for no other reason than for the sake of searching out that very Truth—and since I also shall say nothing except what savors of Christian truth in order to define the articles to be discussed, I believe I shall perform a worthwhile task for the <term>Christian Commonwealth: the collective body of Christian nations and peoples</term> if, before we come to those articles themselves, I do not neglect to unlock the secrets of the Catholic faith lying hidden in the Talmud itself. It is by these secrets that the "perfidy" <note>original: "perfidia"; in this historical context, the term specifically referred to the "unbelief" or "lack of faith" attributed to the Jews from a Christian perspective.</note> of the Jews of our time is most strongly refuted. For through the Talmudic scriptures of the ancient Jews, not only are all the quibbles of the more recent Jews (who strive with every effort to pervert the prophecies of the Prophets) utterly rebuffed, but the **Truth** of the Orthodox doctrine also shines forth most clearly.

<meta>This page begins the first dialogue of the preface. Johannes Reuchlin (Capnio) encourages Pietro Galatino to use the original Hebrew and Aramaic texts to prove Christian doctrines, and Galatino outlines his methodological commitment to the "Hebrew Truth" over existing Latin or Greek translations.</meta>

# PREFACE

->**CAPNIO**<-

You will do very well indeed, my **Galatino**. For in this way, the errors of the Jews of our age will be most effectively disproved, and the strongest testimonies against them will be brought forth from their very own writings in support of the Christian truth, which they never cease to attack. But so that they are less able to resist such great truth, it is necessary that you record the oracles of the holy prophets <note>original: "uatum"; Galatino uses a classical term for the biblical prophets.</note> and the sayings of the ancient **Talmudists**—which you are about to bring against the Jews themselves—exactly as they were written, namely in **Chaldaic** <note>In the 16th century, "Chaldaic" typically referred to Aramaic.</note> and in **Hebrew**.

->**GALATINUS**<-

I will indeed do what you urge most willingly, my **Capnio**: both for the reasons you have stated, and especially so that when the Jews see themselves defeated by their own weapons, they may be compelled to acknowledge the truth they never cease to deny. Once acknowledged, if they wish to look out for their own welfare, they might not neglect to confess and preserve it; lest, at last, having been cast out from the Heavenly kingdom into the outer darkness, they suffer eternal evils. 

But since it would be both very difficult and unpleasant to maintain this for every single thing, I will take care to recount in **Hebrew** or **Chaldaic**, just as they have them, only those passages which, above all others, express and attest to the truth against them. Everything else which I must bring forward from their Scriptures, I shall endeavor to translate into our language <note>i.e., Latin in the original, now English.</note> as faithfully as the language allows, so that they will neither be able to deny the truth nor dare to say that it is not so in their own books. 

Therefore, in translating the sayings of the **Sacred Page** <note>A traditional term for the Bible.</note>, wherever I find that our manuscripts have deviated from the Hebrew, I shall follow neither the **Septuagint** <note>The ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note> nor any other interpreter; instead, I shall turn them into our speech exactly as the **Hebrew Truth** <note>original: "Hebraica ueritas"; a principle famously championed by St. Jerome, asserting that the original Hebrew text is the ultimate authority for the Old Testament.</note> holds. For by this means, every path of escape will be blocked for the deceitful-speaking Jews; and many, indeed nearly infinite, passages of Holy Scripture—which are found to be vitiated and corrupted among both the Latins and the Greeks, partly due to the length of time and partly by the fault of scribes—will be truly and excellently corrected for the sake of our faith. 

In these Hebrew texts, the Christian truth shines far more clearly and perfectly than in our own Latin or Greek editions. Because of this, I have no doubt that I will be criticized by many—especially by those who are accustomed to find fault with whatever they have not done themselves, and who disparage everything they do not know. Truth surely has many enemies, and those who constantly profess it have never lacked rivals. For **Athanasius** and **Chrysostom** suffered such things among the Greeks, as did **Augustine** and **Jerome** among the Latins, and finally all those who have uniquely embraced Truth. Against these critics, I invoke nothing other than Truth herself, who I hope (with Divine aid favoring me) will be a shield for me on every side. Especially since I [submit] myself and all my [assertions] to the determination of the most holy **LEO X**, Supreme Pontiff, the best cultivator of Truth itself, and of the sacrosanct Roman Church, which is both the lady and teacher of all Churches...

<meta>This page continues the introductory dialogue between the scholar Johannes Reuchlin (Capnio), the inquisitor Jacob van Hoogstraten (Hogostratus), and the author Pietro Galatino. ### OF THE AUTHOR.

I submit and subject my assertions, both in these matters and in all others.

->**HOGOSTRATUS**<-
<note>Jacob van Hoogstraten (c. 1460–1527) was a Dominican inquisitor and a leading opponent of Reuchlin in the controversy over Jewish books.</note>

Since I see that you are about to say wondrous and unheard-of things to reveal the Truth, I would wish that we might (with you as our guide) obtain that Truth itself which we seek so greatly more quickly and easily. Therefore, if it would not be a burden, I would ask that you satisfy my inquiry should any doubt enter my mind.

->**GALATINUS**<-

That will indeed be very pleasant for me, and not at all unwelcome. For that reason, I would first of all ask this of you—who possess no small skill in Divine and human Philosophy—as well as of **Capnio** <note>The Greek-style pseudonym of Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and Hebraist.</note> himself—who is not only exceptionally gifted in every kind of literature, but is also a most eloquent interpreter of the three languages <note>The "three sacred languages" are Latin, Greek, and Hebrew.</note> in which the Divine secrets are revealed: that whatever doubts may arise, they should by no means pass by undiscussed. Rather, let them be brought forward for us to examine in turn. For I too will consider that whatever my opinion might bring to those same doubts, according to the capacity of my small wit, should by no means be kept silent. 

But because it is very difficult, and almost impossible, for a weak man (such as I know myself to be) to walk confidently along that path in which even the strongest have been known to stumble—for I confess that I must necessarily undertake many things far beyond my strength and of much greater weight to track down Truth of this kind—I have therefore decided that I must first implore Divine aid. Thus, while prayer itself to God serves as my staff, and His word becomes a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths <note>A reference to Psalm 119:105.</note>, I may walk secure and safe through the ranks of the enemy. By conquering them with their own weapons, I hope to take away from them—as if from unjust possessors—the truth which they hold but do not know, which they neglect and attack. 

So that finally, once the truth itself is found in the **Talmudic Books**, it may be clearer than light what should rightly be thought about the **Talmud** itself, concerning which there is a war among you <note>Galatino refers to the contemporary "Reuchlin Affair," a massive legal and intellectual battle over whether the Talmud should be confiscated and burned.</note>. So that this may be done more rightly and better, it will be necessary for our entire discourse to revolve around twelve main points. From these, twelve individual Books shall be composed, in each of which many mysteries of our faith can be unlocked.

# Book One concerning the Talmud.

## On the ancient and authentic scriptures of the Jews. Chapter One.

->GALATINUS,<-

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'A' featuring intricate floral scrollwork and foliage.</image-desc>

TO convince the Jews of their <term>perfidy</term> <note>original: "perfidiam" — in this historical context, the author refers to the Jewish rejection of Christian doctrine, often translated as 'faithlessness' or 'unbelief' rather than modern treachery.</note> through their own Talmudic scriptures, it is necessary above all else to know that there are two kinds of teachings among them, upon which their <term>Synagogue</term> <note>original: "Synagoga" — used here to refer to the Jewish religious institution and community as a whole.</note> has never ceased to rely, both now and in the past. One of these they call the <term>Written Torah</term> <note>original: "תורה שבכתב" (Torah she-bi-khtav) — the Hebrew Bible, specifically the first five books.</note>, that is, the law which is in writing, or which was delivered in writing. The other, however, they call the <term>Oral Torah</term> <note>original: "תורה שבעל פה" (Torah she-be-al peh) — the oral tradition or interpretation of the law.</note>, that is, the law which is in the mouth, or which was delivered by word of mouth. They claim this is nothing other than the explanation of the law itself, which they assert was handed down to Moses together with the law. For as the ancient <term>Talmudists</term> <note>original: "Talmudistae" — scholars and compilers of the Talmud, the central text of Rabbinic Judaism.</note> testify in the first chapter of that book called <term>Berakhot</term> <note>original: "ברכות" — meaning 'Blessings', the first tractate of the Talmud.</note>, Moses received both the law and the exposition of the law on Mount Sinai by the same spirit. Furthermore, the explanation of the law points toward a double sense: namely, the literal and the spiritual or mystical. They affirm that Moses wrote down neither of these, but delivered both by word of mouth. And they say this law is the one concerning which it is read in <term>Pirkei Avot</term> <note>original: "בפרקי אבות" — 'Chapters of the Fathers', a collection of ethical teachings and the historical chain of tradition.</note>, that is, in the chapters of the fathers, as follows: "Moses received the Torah from Sinai and handed it down to Joshua; and Joshua to the elders; and the elders to the prophets; and the prophets handed it down to the men of the Great Assembly." 

This kind of tradition (as is gathered from various volumes of the Talmudists, and as is reported by Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>original: "Rabbi Mose Ægyptio" — referring to Maimonides, also known as Rambam (1138–1204), a preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and jurist.</note> in the beginning of his <term>Mishneh Torah</term> <note>original: "Deuteronomij" — Maimonides' code of law is often referred to as a "Second Law" or Deuteronomy.</note>) happened to occur in this order: For when Joshua had received this exposition of the law from Moses, he delivered it to Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, who was the grandson of Aaron; and by us, his name is <insert>frequently</insert> corruptly called Phinees. Then Phinehas delivered it to Eli the priest. Eli to Samuel the prophet and priest. Samuel to King David. David to Ahijah the prophet. Ahijah to Elijah the prophet. Elijah to Elisha the prophet. Elisha to Jehoiada the High Priest. Jehoiada to Zechariah the prophet. Zechariah to Hosea the prophet. Hosea to Amos the prophet. Amos to Isaiah the prophet. Isaiah to Micah the prophet. Micah...

...to Joel the prophet. Joel, moreover, [handed it down] to Nahum the prophet. Nahum to Habakkuk the prophet. Habakkuk to Zephaniah the prophet. Zephaniah to Jeremiah the prophet. Jeremiah to Baruch the scribe. Baruch to Ezra the priest and scribe. Up to this point, we do not read that the Jews possessed any other scripture besides the Bible, which they call <term>Macdesciya</term> <note>original: "מקדשיא" (*Mikdashya*) — an Aramaic term meaning "The Sanctuary" or "The Holy Thing of God".</note>, that is, the holy thing of God. Indeed, until those times, no one is found to have committed anything concerning the explanation of the Law to writing.

->CAPITO<-

In order that none of our people remain unaware of which books the Jews receive as sacred and divine, please tell me: in what manner is the *Macdesciya*—that is, the Bible itself—distinguished among them?

<margin>The division of the Bible according to the Hebrews.</margin> ->GALATINUS<-

The Jews (as you yourself know) call the Bible <term>Arbaa ve-Esrim</term> <note>original: "ארבעה ועשרים"</note>, that is, the Twenty-four, because it contains that many books. For they divide it into four parts. The first of these, which they call <term>Torah</term> <note>original: "תורה"</note>, that is, the Law, or <term>Humas</term> <note>original: "חומש" (*Chumash*)</note>, that is, the <margin>Humas.</margin> Fivefold, and which the Greeks name the Pentateuch, contains five books. They name these according to their opening words. Indeed, they call the book of Genesis <term>Berescith</term> <note>original: "בראשית"</note>, <margin>Berescith.</margin> which is the same as "In the beginning." Exodus they call <term>Ve-elleh shemot</term> <note>original: "ואלה שמות"</note>, that is, "And these are the names." Leviticus they call <term>Vayikra</term> <note>original: "ויקרא"</note>, that is, "And he called." Numbers they call <term>Bemidbar Sinai</term> <note>original: "במדבר סיני"</note>, that is, "In the desert of Sinai." Deuteronomy, however, they call <term>Elleh ha-devarim</term> <note>original: "אלה הדברים"</note>, that is, "These are the words."

<margin>The second part.</margin> The second part comprises four books, which they call <term>Nevi'im Rishonim</term> <note>original: "נביאים ראשונים"</note>, that is, the Former Prophets. These are <term>Yehoshua</term> <note>original: "יהושע"</note>, whom we call Joshua; <term>Shophtim</term> <note>original: "שופטים"</note>, that is, Judges; <term>Shemuel</term> <note>original: "שמואל"</note>, which among us contains the first and second books of Kings; and <term>Melachim</term> <note>original: "מלכים"</note>, that is, Kings, which among us embraces the third and fourth books of Kings.

<margin>The third part.</margin> The third part also contains four books. These they call <term>Nevi'im Acharonim</term> <note>original: "נביאים אחרונים"</note>, that is, the Latter Prophets. These are Isaiah, Jeremiah, <term>Yehezkel</term> <note>original: "יחזקאל"</note>, whom we call Ezekiel, and the book of the Twelve Prophets, whom we call the Minor Prophets.

<margin>The fourth part.</margin> Finally, the fourth part, which they call <term>Ketuvim</term> <note>original: "כתובים"</note>, that is, the Hagiographa <note>Greek for "Holy Writings"</note>, contains eleven books. The first of these is titled <term>Dibre ha-yamim</term> <note>original: "דברי הימים"</note>, that is, "The words of the days," which we call by the Greek word <term>Paralipomenon</term> <note>Meaning "The things omitted," referring to the Books of Chronicles.</note>. The second is <term>Tehilloth</term> <note>original: "תהלות"</note> or <term>Tehillim</term> <note>original: "תהילים"</note>, or by a shortened form <term>Tillim</term> <note>original: "תלים"</note>, that is, "Hymns." Although *tillim* can also mean "heaps" or "mounds," the singular of which is <term>tel</term> <note>original: "תל"</note>, which is the same as a heap. This second meaning is not out of place, since the Psalms are, as it were, heaps of collected thoughts. This book we call the Psalter, from the Greek. The third is <term>Mishle Shelomo</term> <note>original: "משלי שלמה"</note>, that is, the Proverbs, or rather, the Parables of Solomon. The fourth is <term>Iyov</term> <note>original: "איוב"</note>, whom we call by the corrupted name Job. The fifth is Ruth. The sixth is <term>Koheleth</term> <note>original: "קהלת"</note>, that is, the assembly or the preacher, whom we call Ecclesiastes. The seventh is <term>Eichah</term> <note>original: "איכה"</note>, that is, "How," which is called by us the book of Lamentations or Dirges...

# BOOK ONE

the book is inscribed. The eighth is <term>Scir hascirim</term> <note>original: "שיר השירים" (*Shir HaShirim*)</note>, that is, the Song of Songs. The ninth is **Esther** <note>original: "אסתר"</note>. The tenth is **Daniel** <note>original: "דניאל"</note>. Finally, the eleventh is **Ezra** <note>original: "עזרא"</note>, which they count as one book along with Nehemiah. Therefore, the Jews hold only these twenty-four books, which we have enumerated, as sacred and divine. For although they possess the book of Joshua ben Sirach <note>also known as Ecclesiasticus</note>, Judith, Tobit, and the first book of Maccabees, they do not include them among the twenty-four. As for the third and fourth books of Ezra, I myself have not yet seen them in Hebrew; however, some of them say that they have recently been found and are to be discovered in Constantinople. But the second book of Maccabees and the book of Philo the Hebrew, which is called the Wisdom of Solomon, I have never found among the Hebrews, but have only seen them in Greek. Furthermore, the Hymn of the Three Children, and the stories of Susanna, Bel, and the Dragon—which we have in our book of Daniel—they do not possess at all. I have mentioned these things so that we may know which books the Jews approve as authentic. Therefore, it is certain that besides the aforementioned twenty-four books, no other scripture existed among the Jews until the time of Ezra. Indeed, the commentaries on the Law themselves—both literal and spiritual or mystical—were spread among the prophets and sages from the time of Moses the lawgiver until the Babylonian captivity only through a certain successive order <note>meaning an oral transmission from teacher to student</note>, as has been said. After the Babylonian captivity, however, when Ezra himself rewrote the Law (which had been burned during the destruction of the city of Jerusalem and the Temple), the other sages began to write down the exposition of that same Law. This was done lest, if another destruction of the city should happen to occur in which all the wise men might perish, the explanation of the Law itself would perish along with them. Because of this, it happened that all those sages who lived from the Babylonian exile until the first writing of the Talmudic codex—who are also called the "Men of the Great Synagogue" in the <term>Pirke auoth</term> <note>original: "פרקי אבות" (*Pirke Avot*), or "Chapters of the Fathers"</note>—and who are known to have taught the Law, handed down the exposition of that Law to their students through both speech and writing. Their authority among the Jews is so great that their writings, from which the Talmud was later composed, hold the first place after the prophets. This is not without merit, since their doctrine was handed down to them directly by the prophets themselves, whose disciples and successors they were. Therefore, it is no wonder if those who preceded the coming of Christ, in explaining the Law and the prophets, handed down in writing almost infinite and truly marvelous things concerning Christ and the truths of the Christian faith, all of which are inserted scatteringly throughout the Talmudic books.

<margin>Alexander the Great worshipped the High Priest of the Jews.</margin>
...ptius <note>likely a fragment of the name Eupolemus, an ancient historian</note> relates in the beginning of his commentary on Deuteronomy that Ezra himself, the teacher of the Law, handed down the explanation of the Law to Simon the Priest, who was also called Jaddua. This is the same Jaddua who, upon hearing that Alexander the Macedonian had captured Gaza and set out on a journey toward Jerusalem, began to be seized by no small dread and fear. For on account of a prior stubbornness, he greatly feared the King's indignation. Therefore, he was warned by a divine oracle through a vision in the night that some should meet the angry Emperor in white garments, while he and the rest of the priests, dressed in their lawful robes, should go out when Alexander was not far from the city itself.

When they had done this, and Alexander saw the High Priest himself wearing a robe of hyacinth blue and gold, and bearing upon his head both the mitre and the golden plate on which the <term>tetragrammaton</term> <note>original: "τετραγράμματον"; the sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>—the name of God—was written, he immediately approached him alone and worshipped the name of God, and first paid reverence to the High Priest himself. When the kings of Syria and all the others who were with him saw this, they were profoundly struck with amazement. Yet no one dared to ask him why he, whom all others worshipped, had himself worshipped only the High Priest, except for Parmenio <note>Alexander's high-ranking general</note>. 

Alexander answered him: "I did not," he said, "worship this man, but the God whose high priesthood he exercises. For I saw a figure in this very dress in a dream while I was still in Macedonia, when I was wondering how I might be able to conquer Asia. He warned me not to hesitate in any way, but to cross over confidently; he promised that he would lead my army and would deliver the power of the Persians to me. Therefore, I have prostrated myself to worship Him. From that time on, I believe that I have been guided by divine help, have conquered Darius, and have broken the power of the Persians. Therefore, I trust that all things which turn in my heart and all that I hope for shall come to pass."

Furthermore, this Jaddua or Simon (to return to the point from which I digressed) handed down the explanation of the Law to Antigonus of Soho <note>original: "Sichæo"</note>. They also call this a **Targum** <note>term: A Targum is an ancient Aramaic translation or paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible, used when Aramaic became the common spoken language.</note>, because it is also in Aramaic, just like the other, even if both are written with Hebrew letters. The edition by Jonathan on the Psalter is in the possession of very few. Those who have it hide it to the best of their ability because of the mysteries of the Christian faith which it contains. Finally, Simeon, the son of Hillel—whom the Talmudists, because of his exceptional holiness, surname <margin>Simeon the Just.</margin> **The Just** <note>original: "צדיק" (Tzadik).</note>—in whom the scepter of the Academy of the Great Synagogue failed (as is said in the *Chapters of the Fathers* <note>original: "פרקי אבות" (Pirkei Avot), a famous collection of ethical teachings in the Talmud.</note>), spoke many things concerning the Messiah. And at last, when in his extreme old age he had received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death unless his eyes saw the Messiah, the Son of God, he took Christ himself in his arms. He then confirmed in Christ's presence the things he had taught about him, having been instructed by the Holy Spirit. His excellent sayings are found scattered in the books of the Talmud. Therefore, from the sayings of all these men, and of many others who, writing upon the Law and the Prophets at those same times, openly showed that our Lord Jesus Christ would be both the only Son of Almighty God and the true Messiah, almost the entire Talmud is composed.

### *On the Jewish writers who happened to live shortly after the passion of Christ, and what they thought of him. Chapter IV.*

->HOOGSTRATEN,<-

<image-desc>A decorative initial "C" featuring a scholar or religious figure in a circular frame.</image-desc> Since all these men whom you have enumerated preceded the coming of Christ, and many of them were inspired by the Spirit, no one at all would think it should be denied that, by explaining the Law and the Prophets, they wrote correctly concerning the Messiah. But concerning those who happened to write after the passion of Christ, and who remained in Judaism with obstinate minds, it is certainly clear that no one ever correctly explained either the Law or the Prophets speaking of the Messiah, but rather distorted them toward a false sense according to their own perfidy. **GALATINUS:** Although that may be rightly said of the Jews of our own time, who are the most foul dregs of all their race, it does not hold true universally for the ancients. Some of those indeed interpreted the prophecies concerning Christ according to the true sense...

For Philo, in that book which he wrote concerning the life of our own people—that is, concerning Apostolic men <note>Philo’s work *De Vita Contemplativa* describes a group called the Therapeutae, whom early Christian historians like Eusebius mistakenly identified as the first Christian monks.</note>—describes the first Church at Alexandria under Mark the Evangelist. <margin>The book which is titled the Wisdom of Solomon.</margin>
-cellent and certainly divine volume which he called the book of the *Wisdom of Solomon*. **HOG:** <note>Hogstraten, one of the participants in this dialogue.</note> For what reason did he wish this book to be inscribed with such a title? **GAL:** <note>Galatinus, the primary speaker of the treatise.</note> Certainly not without cause. For what Solomon predicted enigmatically and parabolically, and as if in a universal sense, in the book of *Proverbs* concerning the Son of God (who is the Wisdom of the Father), Philo teaches in this book—through the same arts of obscurity and concealment—as having already been fulfilled. And if he does not always remain in universality (as Solomon does), he approaches the very specificity he intends, being unable (as I think) to restrain himself from revealing the truth he pursues. Among other things, this is shown most clearly by this example: Solomon warns that we must be cautious when he says, *My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent to them.* Then follows: *If they say, "Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood,"* along with the rest that follows. <note>original: Proverbs 1:10-11.</note> What is all this other than what Philo reports as having happened in his own time, saying: *The impious said among themselves, thinking not rightly,* with the rest that follows? <note>original: Wisdom of Solomon 2:1.</note> And descending even further into specificity, he says: *Let us put wood into his bread.* <note>original: "Mittamus lignum in panem eius." This is a famous Latin rendering of Jeremiah 11:19, which Galatinus here attributes to the tradition surrounding Philo/Solomon.</note> Where by "wood," he designated the Cross; and by "bread," our Lord Jesus himself—taking the parable of the bread from the parable then (as I believe) made common from the mouth of the Lord himself, saying: *The bread that I shall give is my flesh for the life of the world.* <note>original: John 6:51.</note> From this, he teaches through the words of the same Lord that what Solomon had said would one day happen regarding the same Lord was fulfilled in him. Therefore, since the subject matter for both is the same, as is the art of obscurity and concealment, and no difference occurs other than that of future and past time, this book of Philo is rightly called the *Wisdom of Solomon*. Especially since in it, he most excellently suggests the divinity, innocence, and passion of Christ himself, who is both the Wisdom of the Father and is called the Prince of Peace. Hence, to rebuke the ingratitude and impiety of the Jews, he says in Greek—speaking in the person of those whom he calls "the impious": *Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our deeds; he reproaches us for sins against the law, and charges us with sins against our upbringing. He professes to have knowledge of God and calls himself the child of the Lord.* <note>original Greek: "ἐνεδρεύσωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστὶ, καὶ ἐναντιοῦται τοῖς ἔργοις ἡμῶν, καὶ ὀνειδίζει ἡμῖν ἁμαρτήματα νόμου, καὶ ἐπιφημίζεται ἡμῖν ἁμαρτήματα παιδείας ἡμῶν, ἐπαγγέλλεται γνῶσιν ἔχειν θεοῦ, καὶ παῖδα κυρίου ἑαυτὸν ὀνομάζει." This is a quote from the Wisdom of Solomon 2:12-13.</note>

These excellent men, therefore, Philo and Josephus—who, although they wrote in Greek, were both Jews and fierce followers of the traditions of their fathers—if they had not correctly understood those things which had been foretold by the prophets concerning the Messiah, they would neither have held such a good opinion of Christ, nor would they have reported what they said of him so truthfully. Therefore, there is no doubt that if they wrote these things about him in Greek, they also wrote many more things in Hebrew while explaining the Law and the Prophets, since both were most skilled in both languages and were initiated into the sacred scriptures from their very cradles. Whence it is also fair to believe that many others besides them existed at the same times who felt correctly about the Lord Jesus Christ and, explaining the prophecies of the prophets, wrote the truth about him.

<margin>
The third type of Jews.

Yet even they (see how great is the power of truth!) were not able to deny the truth entirely. It must not be thought that this happened without divine arrangement—so that against the enemies of truth who deny it, we might have testimonies of that very truth from those same people. Nor does it prejudice the truth that they themselves did not believe; rather, it adds more to the testimony, because even as unbelievers and against their will, they did not deny it. From the sayings and writings of these men, and of all the others who handed down anything in writing after the Babylonian captivity, the volume of the <term>Talmud</term> was gathered and compiled.

### Who the author of the Talmud itself was, when it was published, into how many parts it is divided, and what subjects it primarily treats.

Since I have found various opinions concerning the author of the <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, consisting of the Mishnah and the Gemara.</note> itself, and regarding the time when it was published. However, being prevented by death, he was unable to complete it. Soon afterward, his son, together with <term>Maremar</term>, gave the finishing touches to the work. <margin>What the Talmud is.</margin> The Talmud, moreover, is that which is called "doctrine" or "instruction," embracing all previous commentaries, statutes, and certain histories of the times; it is a work truly full on all sides of divine and natural, as well as political and legal wisdom. The sixth, named **מסכת כלאים** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Kil'ayim*</note>, the Treatise of Mixtures, has nine chapters, which treat all kinds of things that were forbidden to be mixed. ...was bound to offer only from certain things, namely from wheat, barley, grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, and dates. <margin>The second part of the Talmud, called the Order of Festivals.</margin> The second part encompasses twelve books. The first of these, which is called **מסכת שבת** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Shabbat*</note>, that is, the Treatise of the Sabbath, contains twenty-four chapters, in which it is treated of the Sabbath, and of those things which were permitted and those which were prohibited on the Sabbath day. The second, which is called **מסכת ערובין** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Eruvin*</note>, that is, the Treatise of Mixtures <note>original: *conversationum*, literally "dealings" or "living together," referring here to the legal "mixing" of domains to allow carrying on the Sabbath</note>, is divided into ten chapters, in which it deals with the communal mixtures which were mutually permitted to the Jews on the Sabbath. The third, which is called **מסכת פסחים** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Pesahim*</note>, that is, the Treatise of Passover, is divided into two parts; in the first part, it deals specifically with unleavened bread and those things which were to be prepared for the solemnity of the Passover; in the second part, however, it deals with the Paschal lamb. The entire book is divided into ten chapters. The fourth, which is denominated **מסכת שקלים** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Shekalim*</note>, that is, the Treatise of Shekels, is partitioned into eight chapters, in which it is treated of the collection of shekels that was required for the purchase of the two lambs that were offered daily in sacrifice—one in the morning and the other in the evening. <margin>What a shekel is.</margin> Although a shekel is properly a certain measure of weight, according to that passage in Leviticus 27: **שקל** <note>Hebrew: *shekel*</note>, that is, a shekel has twenty gerahs <note>original: *obolos*; Galatinus uses the Greco-Roman term for a small coin to explain the Hebrew currency</note>, since it is derived from the Hebrew verb **שקל** <note>Hebrew: *shakal*</note>, which signifies "to weigh." In this context, however, it is a type of currency weighing twenty gerahs. For every person, after having completed their twentieth year of age, was bound to pay a half-shekel every year according to the weight-measure of the sanctuary, for the purchase of the two aforementioned lambs, to be offered in the perpetual sacrifice for the redemption of their souls. The fifth, which is called **מסכת יומא** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Yoma*</note>, that is, the Treatise of Days, contains eight chapters, in which it deals with the Day of Atonement and those things which were required to be done on such a day. The sixth, which is named **מסכת סוכה** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Sukkah*</note>, that is, the Treatise of the Booth or Tabernacle, has five chapters, in which it deals with the Feast of Booths or Tabernacles. The fifth, which is denominated **מסכת סוטה** <note>Hebrew: *Massekhet Sotah*</note>, that is, the Treatise of the Wayward Wife, has nine chapters. These treat all damages and harms that are typically caused by both men and animals. The second, which is named **בבא מציעא** <note>Hebrew: *Bava Metzia*</note>, that is, the Middle Gate, is also divided into ten chapters. These deal with lawsuits, rights, usury, and rentals. These treat sales and purchases, partnerships, and heirs and inheritances. The twelfth, which is called the <term>Treatise of Stems</term> <note>original Hebrew: *Massekhet Okatzin* (מסכת עוקצין)</note>, has three chapters, in which it is declared when the stems to which apples and other fruits adhere were said to be contaminated by contact with impure fruits.

Therefore, of the whole Talmud (as is clear from the preceding), the primary parts are six, the books sixty, and the chapters five hundred and thirty-two. In these are found many and almost infinite <term>concluded traditions</term> <note>original Hebrew: *Gemarot* (גמרות), the plural of *Gemara*</note> scattered throughout, that is, finalized traditions or determined conclusions. These contain almost innumerable secrets concerning the Messiah and are very much in agreement with our faith, having been handed down and written by the ancient Jews through many cycles of years, long before the Talmud was compiled. For it almost never happens in the Talmud itself that any <term>tradition</term> <note>original Hebrew: *Gemara* (גמרא)</note>—that is, a conclusion handed down and determined by those ancient fathers—is found that does not express some secret of the Catholic <note>The author uses "Catholic" here in its original sense of "universal" or "orthodox" Christian truth.</note> truth, either explicitly and openly, or implicitly and through figures.

# BOOK ONE
<header>BOOK</header>

# *That the Talmudists, in seeking the secrets of the Law, chiefly followed the allegorical sense, while the Cabalists followed the anagogical sense; also, what Cabala is, and why our ancestors did not mention Cabala.*

## Chapter VI.

### HOOGSTRATEN <note>Jacob van Hoogstraten (c. 1460–1527) was a Dominican inquisitor and a leading opponent of Johannes Reuchlin in the "Battle of the Books" regarding Jewish literature. Here, he serves as the skeptical interlocutor.</note>

---

**S**ince the Jews understand everything only literally—for they are usually said to consider nothing but the "rind" <note>The "cortex" or rind refers to the outer, literal meaning of scripture, as opposed to the internal, spiritual "nut."</note> of the scripture—how can it be true that the Talmudists followed a spiritual and mystical sense? 

**GALATINUS.** That may indeed be rightly said of the Jews of our current age. To escape the truth, they occupy themselves only with the literal rind of the law, utterly rejecting all allegories and figures. Indeed, the entire assembly of more recent teachers and younger Talmudists, as if blinded in spirit and completely neglecting the light of the mind, embrace nothing of the divine utterances except the historical and literal sense.

<margin>The spiritual and literal senses.</margin>
The ancients, however, were accustomed to seek the secrets of the law only through the spiritual and mystical sense. The Talmudists very often demonstrate how much the spiritual sense exceeds the literal for investigating the secrets of the law. They say that the literal sense is a <term>Davar katan</term> <note>original Hebrew: דבר קטן</note>, which means "a small thing," but the spiritual or mystical sense is a <term>Davar gadol</term> <note>original Hebrew: דבר גדול</note>, which means "a great thing." Furthermore, they call the literal sense a <term>Mashal</term> <note>original Hebrew: משל</note>, meaning an example or parable, as Rabbi Moses <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> relates in the first treatise of his book, the *Moreh* <note>The *Moreh Nevukhim* or *Guide for the Perplexed*.</note>. Moreover, they compare the literal sense to a candle that is bought for a tiny farthing. But the allegorical or figurative sense—which they call the "certainty of the law"—they liken to a dark pearl hidden in a house <note>original: "בורית שחורה" (*burit shechorah*). Galatinus interprets this as a hidden or darkened pearl, following Maimonides' metaphor of finding a jewel in a dark room using a cheap candle.</note>, which is finally found by those searching by means of such a candle—that is, through the literal sense or parable. 

Rabbi Moses declares this same point excellently and most beautifully near the beginning of that same book, saying: "Know that the key to understanding everything the Prophets said is to understand parables, metaphors, figures, and enigmas." For you know it was said in Hosea, chapter 12: <note>Hosea 12:10</note> "And by the hand of the prophets I have used likenesses" <note>original Hebrew: וביד הנביאים אדמה</note>. And again in Ezekiel, chapter 17: <note>Ezekiel 17:2</note> "Son of Adam, pose a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel" <note>original Hebrew: בן אדם חיד חידה ומשול משל אל בית ישראל</note>. "A great eagle with [great] wings..." And a few lines later: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Say now to the rebellious house, do you not know what these things mean? Say: Behold, the king of Babylon has come to Jerusalem and taken its king..." <note>original Hebrew: ויהי דבר יהוה אלי לאמר : אמור נא לבית המרי הלא ידעתם מה אלה אמור הנה בא מלך בבל ירושלם ויקח את מלכה</note>

This is to say: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Say, I pray, to the rebellious house,"

<meta>Catchword: "rebellious," matching the start of the next page.</meta>

<summary>In this chapter, Galatinus distinguishes between the literalism of contemporary Jews and the mystical depth of the ancient Talmudists. He uses Maimonides' metaphors to argue that the literal text is merely a "small thing" or a cheap candle used to find the "great thing"—the hidden spiritual truth.</summary>

# FIRST [BOOK]
<header>FIRST</header>

...rebel, 'Do you not know what these things are? Say, behold, the King of Babylon comes to Jerusalem, and he shall take its King.' And so forth. <note>This is a reference to Ezekiel 17:12, where the prophet uses an allegory of eagles and vines to describe political rebellion and divine judgment.</note> You know again what the wise man said in the twenty-fifth chapter of Proverbs: <note>original Hebrew: תפוחי זהב במשכיות כסף דבר דבר על אפניו</note> which is to say: 'Golden apples in silver filigree is a word spoken according to its two faces.' <note>This is a translation of Proverbs 25:11. While modern Bibles often translate this as "a word fitly spoken," the medieval tradition interpreted the Hebrew word *afnav* (wheels/faces) to imply a dual-layered meaning: an inner and an outer sense.</note> Listen, I pray, to the exposition of this sentence. Silver filigree refers to silver nets or mesh with very tiny holes, yet through which the sight can penetrate. Therefore, the sense is: A word spoken according to its two faces—that is, according to the internal and external sense—is like an apple in a silver net. It is as if he says it is necessary for the external sense to be precious and good, like silver. The internal sense, however, must be much better, like gold; just as silver relates to gold when compared. It is also necessary that there be something in the external sense that leads and draws the observer toward the internal. Just as a golden apple covered by a silver net, when viewed from a distance or without much scrutiny, seems entirely silver. But when one with sharp vision, provoked by the value and beauty of the silver, draws closer, he will certainly see the golden apple hiding within. So it is with the words of the prophets. For frequently, those things which are on the outside are wisdom useful for many things: such as for the ordering of morals and the state of human society. This is evident on the surface of the Proverbs of Solomon. However, those things which are within are wisdom that is extremely useful for things that must be believed according to the truth. This is what Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), arguably the most influential Jewish philosopher of the Middle Ages. This analogy is famously found in the introduction to his *Guide for the Perplexed*.</note> says. From these things, therefore, it is clear that the Talmudists considered the secrets of the Law only through the spiritual and mystical sense. But this will become far more evident in what follows. I pass over the Cabalists, and those well-versed in Cabala itself, who consider the secrets of the Law only through the anagogical <note>The 'anagogical' sense is the highest level of biblical interpretation, dealing with the soul's ascent and the mysteries of the divine realm.</note> understanding. 

**HOOGSTRATEN.** This name 'Cabala' is found nowhere among the holy fathers, nor among the Doctors of the Church, nor among our masters. From this, such a name is rendered extremely suspect. 

<margin>
What Cabala is, and why our ancestors did not mention it.
</margin>

**GALATINUS.** In ancient times, it was indeed forbidden for this faculty which they call Cabala to be handed down to anyone except the most learned and those of advanced age. For this reason, it was not permitted for even a small part of it to be committed to writing. Hence, besides those things said to be handed down by Rabbi Simeon, the son of Yochai <note>Simeon bar Yochai was a 2nd-century sage to whom the *Zohar*, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism, is traditionally attributed.</note>, few or no other things written by the ancients are found. For as it is said in the book <note>original Hebrew: חגיגה</note> *Hagiga*—that is, *The Festival*—in the chapter <note>original Hebrew: אין דורשין</note> *En Dorsin*—that is, *They are not preached*—it was permitted for no one to write anything concerning Cabala, but they handed it down only by mouth. From this, they not unsuitably called it <note>original Hebrew: קבלה</note> *Cabala*, which is interpreted in Latin as 'Reception.' However, the teachers of the more recent Jews, lest that ancestral teaching should vanish, published something of this faculty in writing, though scattered and obscured by several veils. Because of this, it happens that very few are able to grasp a correct understanding of it. If any, however, believe they have attained something from it, they soon [hide] it in their heart, as a secret to be revealed to no one...

He did this to show openly that he would soon produce far more and far deeper things than all others have written on this matter until now, which would bring the clearest light to such an obscure subject. Last of all, I, like one gathering clusters of grapes after the vintage, have decided to intersperse into what I am about to say—scattered wherever it may be necessary—only those things from this Cabalistic wisdom which seem necessary for relating the secrets of Catholic truth.

<margin>Galatinus's response.</margin>
But truly (if I may say so with your permission), you are greatly mistaken. Since it is very useful for our faith to reveal the truth in this matter as I perceive it, I shall respond to the things you have said for the sake of making that truth manifest.

<margin>To the first point.</margin>
And as to the first point, I admit that many absurd things are placed there; however, not all things that seem absurd are truly so.

<margin>The ancient Talmudists handed down the secrets of the Law under figures and enigmas.</margin>
For those ancient Talmudists handed down nearly infinite secrets through figures and enigmas, which seem like follies and absurdities to those who do not understand them. Yet, in truth, innumerable secrets regarding the Messiah and Catholic <note>original: "Catholicam"; here meaning the universal or orthodox Christian truth.</note> truth lie hidden within them. From this, the error of the younger Jews has grown. While they are ignorant of the ancient manner of theologizing and philosophizing, they turn many secrets of the Talmudic work into mockery and blasphemies. Hence, many of our own people, while they are unable to understand such mysteries, presume to revile and condemn them. 

Wherefore, to say nothing of others, a certain man endowed with no small skill in divine and human letters, writing against the Jews, mentions many things of this kind which he himself, misunderstanding them, calls follies and incongruities. And among other things which he says are found written in the Talmud against divine perfection, he especially reports this: That when God established the firmament <note>The sphere of the heavens or the sky.</note>, being unable to finish it, He left a certain hole in it on the northern side. The Jews assert (as that Doctor says) that He did this for the reason that if anyone should ever arise wishing to make himself equal to God, God—presenting the completion of that hole as a challenge—might say to him: "If you are God, just as I am, close that place which I have left open, if you can." 

But truly, it escapes no one how obvious a lie this is. For we always see the highest axis of the North Pole above us, never hidden, and we see it all whole, complete, and perfect. From this, the folly of this error is clearly evident. All these things are in that Doctor's opinion. Who, although he said these and all other things with a good heart and zeal for the Christian faith, was nonetheless (to tell the truth) not a little deceived. Nor does God, who is the highest Truth, require our lie for the exaltation of His faith. And especially since many of those things which he himself rejects as entirely erroneous, if they are rightly understood (as is proper), profit us more toward the truth of the Catholic faith against the Jews than if (as he says) they were esteemed as words utterly foreign to truth and reason. 

For to pass over other things, this example of the hole in the firmament left in the northern part—which he brings forward as a great incongruity—if it is rightly understood, will be seen not only to be no incongruity, but also most consistent with our faith. Wherefore, so that the truth of the Catholic faith might appear more clearly for the confounding of the unfaithfulness <note>original: "perfidiam"; a common Renaissance term used to describe the Jewish rejection of Christian doctrine.</note> of the Jews, I will first relate the words of that same example in Hebrew exactly as they are written in the Talmud; then the mystery which...

# BOOK
<header>FIRST</header>

...what lies hidden in that same example against the Jews of our age and for the truth of our faith, I will now reveal. Thus, Rabbi Eleazar, not the least of the ancient Talmudists, sets forth that very example in his chapters in the book *Zohar* <note>The Zohar is the foundational work of Jewish mysticism, known as Kabbalah.</note>:

-> "The Holy One, blessed be He, created the side of the north corner, but He did not finish it; for the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'Whoever says he is God, let him come and finish this corner that I have left, and then everyone will know that he is God.'" <note>original Hebrew: "Ruach pinnat tzafon..." and Latin: "Latus partis aquilonis..."</note> <-

Great mysteries are certainly hidden in these words. For first, it is shown that it is possible for some man to be God. Second, that the sign of his divinity is that he is able to complete the northern part. For a right understanding of these things, it must be known that the ancients were accustomed to call the malice of men and the wickedness of demons "the left side" or "the north" <note>original: "aquilonem"</note> allegorically, following that passage in the first chapter of Jeremiah: "From the north all evil shall be spread upon all the inhabitants of the land," and in Ecclesiasticus chapter 10: "The heart of a fool is in his left hand." 

However, no malice of men or temptation of demons is greater than that which leads to the worship of idols. Therefore, the cult of idols is attributed primarily to the north, as is easily seen in Ezekiel chapter 8. What else, then, is designated by this opening <note>original: "foramen"; referring to the unfinished "gap" in the north side of creation.</note> than the temptation or power of demons, which especially looks toward the worship of idolatry? Why is that opening said to be left behind by God, except because—by His permission—the worship of idolatry proceeded from free will (which God himself had given to man) through a bad choice? 

Therefore, according to the doctrine of the ancient Talmudists in this example, the sign of divinity is to be able to completely overcome the power of demons and to drive out idolatry. This is plainly confirmed by what is written in the book *Zohar*, where Rabbi Recanati <note>original: "Racanad," referring to Menahem Recanati, a 13th-century Italian Kabbalist.</note> says the following on the fourth chapter of Genesis:

-> "The Presence of God <term>Shekhinah: The indwelling or divine presence of God, often viewed in Kabbalah as the feminine aspect of the divine.</term> called *Attah* <note>Hebrew for "You."</note>, shall rule over the Angel of Death" <note>original Hebrew: "Shekhinah ha-nekrat Attah timshol be-malakh ha-mavet"</note> <-

—that is, the devil. And in the same place: "The word *Attah* [You] hints at the Wisdom of God." From this it is clearly held that through the Wisdom of God—which in divine matters is attributed to the Son—united to human nature, the power of the devil was to be conquered. In this example, therefore, the ancient Talmudists mystically handed down the divinity of the Messiah, which was to be recognized chiefly by this sign: that the Messiah would complete the northern part itself. That is, he would conquer the devil by freeing the human race from his power and by driving out his worship—that is, idolatry—from the world. That Christ did this, no one could rightly deny, especially since through his Apostles idolatry was utterly driven out. Whence it is clear that through this Talmudic example—which that teacher of ours <note>Likely referring to Hogostratus or a critic of the Talmud.</note> brings forward as a great absurdity against the perfection of God—not only is the wickedness of the Jews confounded, who believe the Messiah will not be God but a mere man...

They think all those shameful things are said of Jesus our most glorious Savior. <margin>Regarding the third point.</margin>
The Jews assert that the Talmudic traditions were delivered by God to Moses along with the law on Mount Sinai, then revealed by Moses to the ancient fathers in successive order, and at last written down in the *Talmud* by their ancient Doctors. I say that to believe this concerning *everything* that is in the *Talmud* is nothing other than the insanity of a headstrong mind. <meta>This page continues Galatinus’s defense of using Jewish texts to support Christian doctrine. It transitions from a specific anecdote about Jesus the Nazarene to a broader argument: just as one wouldn't discard honey because it comes from stinging bees, one shouldn't discard truth found in the Talmud. The text highlights the 1312 decree by Pope Clement V to establish language schools for mission work and polemics.</meta>

-># BOOK<-

Indeed, no one, unless they were completely deprived of their mind, would despise the Law and the prophets simply because he found them among the Jews. Likewise, no one except a person lacking reason would look down upon a **precious stone** <note>This refers to the "toadstone" or "bufonite," a mythical jewel once believed to be found inside the heads of old toads and dragons, thought to have medicinal properties.</note> just because it was found in the head of a dragon or a toad. Furthermore, no one but a fool or a madman would consider **honey** something to be rejected because it is the "spit of bees"—or some other perhaps less dignified thing—simply because it is produced by those animals that have a poisonous sting. Rather, a wise person would know how to turn it to his own or others' useful purposes and would know how to avoid the harm of the sting. 

In no way, therefore, should traditions of this kind be rejected. This is partly because they could have reached those who wrote them down in a continuous line of succession from Moses, the prophets, and the other fathers. Indeed, we can hardly think that they came from anywhere else *but* from the prophets and those holy fathers. But it is especially because nothing can be found so powerful for refuting the impudence of the Jews, and nothing so effective for convicting them of their wickedness. Finally, what could be more pleasant for a Christian than to snatch the **sword from the hands of the enemies**, and—following the example of David—cut off the head of the infidels with their own blade, or like Judith, sever it with their own dagger? 

<margin>
The Decree of Clement V.
</margin>
For this reason, it was surely by divine providence that Pope Clement V <note>Pope Clement V (r. 1305–1314) presided over the Council of Vienne.</note> ordained at the holy council that the **Talmudic books** of the Jews should be translated into the Latin language by faithful men skilled in the Hebrew tongue, and should be read publicly by Christians. This is found in the *Clementines*, under the heading *Concerning Teachers* <note>Referring to the "Constitutiones Clementinae," a book of canon law. The specific decree "Inter Sollicitudines" came from the Council of Vienne in 1311–1312.</note>. There, among other things, it is said: "With the approval of this sacred council, we have provided for the establishment of schools for the following types of languages wherever the Roman Curia happens to reside, as well as in the universities of **Paris, Oxford, Bologna, and Salamanca**. We decree that in each of these places, Catholic men who have sufficient knowledge of the **Hebrew, Greek, Arabic, and Chaldean** <note>In this period, "Chaldean" usually referred to Aramaic, the language of the Talmud and many biblical commentaries.</note> languages shall be maintained—specifically two experts for each language—to direct the schools there. By faithfully translating books from those languages into Latin, they shall diligently teach those languages to others and pass on their expertise to them through careful instruction. Thus, being sufficiently instructed and taught in these languages, they may, with God as the author, produce the hoped-for fruit, healthily propagating the faith among the infidel peoples." So it says there. 

Where it speaks of translating and publicly reading the books of the Jews, this is not to be understood as referring to the **Bible**, since that has been translated so many times; nor do the Scriptures belong only to the Jews, but rather are ours, or at least common to both. Instead, it must be understood to refer to other Jewish books, and especially the **Talmudic** ones, in which so many Catholic truths are contained, as will be made very clear in the following pages. From all that has been said, therefore, it is clearer than the midday sun: the **Talmud** itself ought to be accepted by Christians—not, however, in all things, but only in those things which are good. This is something the ancient Talmudists themselves admit, as is clearly seen in the book <term>חגיגה</term> <gloss>Haghiga</gloss> <note>Tractate Chagigah is a section of the Talmud dealing with festival offerings and, in its second chapter, mystical speculations.</note>. There, among other things, it is read: "What is the meaning of that which is written in Malachi 2: *For the lips of the priest preserve knowledge, and they seek the law from his mouth, for he is the angel of the Lord...*"

<meta>This page continues Pietro Galatinus's argument that certain ancient Jewish scholars, known as the Scribes or *Sophrim*, intentionally altered the biblical text.
