...to pronounce it as it is written, they do not dare; but in its place, they utter **Adonai** <note>original: "אדני" — meaning "My Lord."</note>, which is the same as **Lord**. However, those who contend that this name sounds like **Ioua** <note>An early Latin attempt at pronouncing the Tetragrammaton, similar to "Jova."</note> in our letters attempt to prove it primarily by this: the Hebrew grammarians say that when a *shva* <term>sceua: a Hebrew vowel mark indicating a very short sound</term> follows any of the guttural letters, often both the *shva* itself and the guttural letter are removed together through **syncopation** <note>The shortening of a word by omitting sounds or letters from the middle.</note>.

For example, **Iehuda** <note>original: "יהודה" — Judah</note> is sometimes both written and pronounced as **Iuda** <note>original: "יודא"</note>; and **Iehosua** <note>original: "יהושע" — Joshua</note> as **Iosua** <note>original: "ישוע"</note>; and **Iehoiachin** <note>original: "יהויכין"</note> as **Ioiachin** <note>original: "יויכין"</note>; and **tehilim** <note>original: "תהלים" — Psalms</note> as **tillim** <note>original: "תלים"</note>. And many other things of this kind. They wish for the same thing to happen similarly in this great name of God. From this, they infer that it sounds like **Ioua** among us, since in it a *shva* precedes the guttural letter **he** <note>The Hebrew letter ה (H).</note>. 

But if this were true, the name itself would not be written as **יהוה** <note>YHWH</note> but as **יה** <note>YH — "Yah"</note> without the *shva* and the letter *he*. And thus it would not be a **Tetragrammaton**, or a name of four letters, but only of three. This is something that cannot even be thought of. For it is a sacrilege for anything to be either added to or taken away from that name. Rather, it must be written and pronounced in its entirety (if indeed it is to be pronounced at all) just as God Himself commanded Moses that it should be written. 

Therefore, the rule of the Hebrew grammarians which they bring forward has no place here, although it is also preserved nowhere or very rarely in the rest of the sacred twenty-four books, but perhaps only in other volumes, and especially among the **Talmudists** <note>Scholars of the Talmud, the central text of Jewish civil and ceremonial law.</note>. It is necessary, therefore, for the **Tetragrammaton** name of God itself to be both written and pronounced with the *shva* and the letter *he*, which has a gentle breathing sound. Wherefore, let those who affirm that it sounds like **Ioua** among us take heed. For it is to be pronounced not as **Ioua**, nor **Ieoua**, but **Iehoua** <note>Jehovah</note> with a gentle breathing, just as it is written.

**CHAPTER.** How the Hebrews interpret this name.
**GALATINUS.** Some among them interpret it as "The Begetter"; others as "He who gives essence" or "He who gives being to all things"; still others as "One and All," or "All things united as a cause," or "The One containing all things pre-eminently."

**CHAPTER.** Why the Jews do not dare to pronounce this name.
**GALATINUS.** Because of those things which are held in the book **Kiddushin** <note>original: "קידושין" — "Sanctifications," a tractate of the Talmud concerning marriage and legal status.</note>, that is, of sanctifications, in the chapter **Hassara Iohasin** <note>original: "עשרה יוחסין" — "Ten Lineages."</note>, that is, the "Ten Nobles," regarding that passage in Exodus chapter 3: *This is my name forever.* For it is read there that a certain elder said it is not written **leolam** <note>original: "לעולם" — "forever"</note>, but **lealam** <note>original: "לעלם" — "to be hidden" or "to be concealed"</note>. 

But **Rabbi Abina** objected, saying: "It is written: *This is my name.* And it is written again in the same place: *This is my memorial*," said the Holy and Blessed God. "I am not read as I am written. For I am written with *yod*, *he*, *vav*, *he*—namely **יהוה**, which is the **Tetragrammaton** name—and I am read with *aleph*, *daleth*, *nun*, *yod*, which letters make **Adonai** <note>original: "אדני"</note>, which is the same as **Lord**." Wherefore the masters commanded that in its place, **Adonai** ought to be read. So it is said there. Furthermore, as it is read in the book **Sanhedrin** <note>A Talmudic tractate dealing with law and the high court.</note> in the chapter **Helec**: **Abba Saul** said, "He who pronounces the four-letter name itself according to how its letters sound shall have no part in the world to come." For that reason—

Who also says in the same place: "When this name was uttered in the sanctuary and in the blessing of the people, it was not known to every man how it was pronounced, or with which vowel each of its letters produced a sound, and whether it was necessary for any of them to be doubled, or to be uttered simply or softly. But there were wise men who received from one another the meaning of the name itself and the manner of its pronunciation. They taught no one except a disciple worthy of them, and only once a week." 

I am of the opinion that when the wise men taught their sons the name of four letters, and only once a week, this was not merely to teach how it was pronounced, but also its meaning: the reason why such a name was found and established. For in it, truly, is a divine mystery. Thus far the Rabbi.

For from these (as has been said), the sound **Jehovah** <note>original: "Iehoua"</note> is produced. Rather, it is entirely ineffable regarding the significance of the mystery. For it signifies the divine essence so distinctly that it openly suggests the trinity of divine persons and their eternal distinction, origin, and production, along with His most simple unity. Therefore, because the God who is Three and One, who is entirely ineffable and incomprehensible, is signified through this name: for that reason, the name itself is called ineffable. ...because of this, wherever they found that name, they did not dare to utter it at all, but pronounced **Adonai** <note>Hebrew for "Lord," used as a substitute for the sacred name.</note> in its place. I believe, however, that when the wise men taught their sons the four-letter name, and only once a week, this was not only to teach how it was pronounced, but also its meaning: why such a name was discovered and assigned. For in it lies a divine mystery. Thus far that Rabbi.

**GALATINUS**: This cannot be without a great mystery. For from these (as has been said), the word **Jehovah** <note>original: "Iehoua"</note> is produced. But in regards to the meaning of the mystery, it is entirely ineffable. For it signifies the divine essence so distinctly that, along with His most simple unity, it clearly suggests the Trinity of divine persons, and their eternal distinction, origin, and production. Because, therefore, God—three and one, who is entirely ineffable and incomprehensible—is signified through this name, the name itself is called ineffable. # BOOK

Taught by that great Moses, and in order to designate this inexpressible nature of the divine trinity and unity, they determined that this name should not be spoken at all. Instead, wherever it was found, the name **Adonai** <note>Hebrew: אדני, meaning "Lord."</note>, which is interpreted as "Lord," ought to be pronounced in its place. For this reason, whenever we encounter this name to be translated, we are accustomed to render it into Latin <note>In this translation, into English.</note> sometimes as "God" according to its inherent meaning, and sometimes as "Lord" according to its pronunciation, as it seems most appropriate.

Because of this ineffability of God, Rabbenus Haccados <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, often called "The Holy Rabbi."</note> said (as we mentioned a little earlier) that God himself has no name of which we can have knowledge. This is a sentiment that even Mercurius Trismegistus <note>Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the author of ancient wisdom texts.</note> seems to hold when he says: *For He who is, is without a name* <note>original Greek: "ὅτι γὰρ ὁ ὢν ἀνώνυμος"</note>. Even a demon could not remain silent on this matter; for the Delphic Apollo <note>The famous oracle of ancient Greece.</note>, when someone asked him what God was, replied among other things: *Whose name cannot even be contained by a word* <note>original Greek: "ὅ τὸ ὄνομα μηδὲ λόגῳ χωρούμενον"</note>.

->How the mystery of the divine trinity is distinctly expressed through the four-letter name of God. Chapter 10.<-

**CAPNIO** <note>The character representing the author, Johann Reuchlin.</note>: I beg you now to reveal in what way this four-letter name of God <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>From the Greek for "four letters," referring to the Hebrew name YHWH.</note> might distinctly suggest the secret of the divine trinity and unity.

That which is one refers to the unity of essence; but that which is three refers to the trinity of persons.

**CAPNIO**: I ask that you explain these things more clearly.

# LIBER

...is the first principle <note>original: "principium"</note>, since every writing takes its origin from it, while it takes its origin from none. Most rightly, it suggests the Father in divine matters, who, since He is from no one and the other persons emanate from Him, is called the "beginning without a beginning." But the second letter, namely **ה** <note>the letter He</note>, which signifies "to be" or "to live," most aptly hints at the Son in divine matters, through whom all things that were made began to be, and whatever was made, in Him was life. The third letter, however, namely **ו** <note>the letter Vau</note>, which denotes the conjunction "And," most excellently expresses the Holy Spirit. Since He is the love of the Father and the Son, by which they love each other in turn, He is rightly called the bond, that is, the connection between both.

### CHAPTER. Why is only the second of these letters doubled?

<margin>Why the second letter of this name is doubled.</margin>
GALATINUS: To suggest that only the Son, who is the second person in the Trinity, has a double respect. For the Father, who is the first person, since He is only the producer and not produced, has only one respect in this regard. The Holy Spirit also, who is the third person, since He is only produced and not a producer <note>In the Western tradition Galatinus follows, the Spirit is produced by the Father and Son but does not produce another divine person.</note>, also has only one respect. But the Son himself, who is the second person, since He is both produced and producing, has two respects: for He is produced by the Father, and together with the Father, He produces the Holy Spirit.

### CHAPTER.

<margin>Why the Chaldeans write ∴.</margin>

GALATINUS: Two secrets are suggested in this. One of them is indeed because (as we said) *iod* is the same as "beginning." And although "beginning" in the internal works of the Trinity applies to the Father alone, in external operations <note>The "external operations" refer to the Trinity acting upon the created world (like Creation), where all three persons act as one.</note> it is common to the three persons. Therefore, the three *iods* are the three divine <term>hypostases: A theological term for the distinct persons of the Trinity.</term>. The single <term>qametz: A Hebrew vowel mark resembling a small "T".</term> placed under the three *iods* is the divine nature, which is communicated to each person entirely and indivisibly. The circle, however, by which the three *iods* are enclosed, is the very identity of the divine essence, by which the divine persons concur together as a single principle and one primary cause in the actions of all things. The other secret is that the three equal *iods* signify the equality of the three persons. The *qametz* designates the one divine essence existing in those three divine persons. The circle denotes the identity of the essence itself, by which each person is said to be in the others through <term>circumincessio: Also known as perichoresis, the mutual indwelling of the three persons of the Trinity.</term>.

Nor is the divinity itself more in the three persons together than it is in each one; rather, it is whole in each, and whole in the three. ### CHAPTER. <margin>Three divine names composed from the letters of this name.</margin>
CAPITO: What are those three divine names which the ancient Hebrews asserted are composed from the four letters of this name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH.</note>?

GALATINUS: These indeed: **יה** *Iah*, **וה** *Hu*, and **יהו** *Vehu* <note>original: "iah, hu, uehu". Note that the OCR for "Vehu" shows three letters (Iod-He-Vau), though the text describes it as being formed from the 3rd and 4th letters (Vau and He).</note>. For the first is composed of the first and second letters, namely from *Iod* and *He*, in this manner: **יה** *Iah*, which is the same as "God," and designates the Father, who is the fountain of all divinity. The second name consists of the second and third letters, thus: **וה** *Hu*, which is interpreted as "He Himself," and signifies the Son. For He is surely the one whom the prophets foretold would come to save the human race, and who would one day be pointed out with a finger, according to that passage in Isaiah, chapter 35: **אלהים הוא יבא וישעכם** <note>original Hebrew: "Elohim hu yavo ve-yoshakhem"</note>, which is to say: "God himself will come and save you." Finally, the third name is constituted from the third and fourth letters, namely from *Vau* and *He*, thus: **יהו** *Vehu*, and the whole of it sounds like "and He Himself," denoting the Holy Spirit. For He too was to be sent visibly after the Son, though not in the same manner. For the Son was to be sent in a human nature <term>hypostatically united</term> <note>A theological term meaning the union of divine and human natures in one person.</note> to Himself. But the Holy Spirit was sent in the form of a dove and in tongues of fire, not hypostatically united to Him, but as if under a sign. 

Furthermore, in this we see that the second name descends from the first, and the third from the second. For the letter **ה** (*He*) is common to the first and second names, while **ו** (*Vau*) is common to the second and third; this clearly shows that the Son is <term>consubstantial</term> <note>Of the same substance or essence.</note> with the Father, by whom He was begotten, and the Holy Spirit is consubstantial with the Son, who is consubstantial with the Father. Thus it is openly clear that the Son is in the Father, and the Father in the Son, and the Holy Spirit in both.

### CHAPTER.
CAPITO: I also judge it to have been done not without a great mystery that all the letters of this name are the very same ones from which the three tenses—namely the past, present, and future—of the substantive verb <note>The verb "to be."</note> in the indicative mood consist among the Hebrews.

GALATINUS: It is exactly as you say. For in this, two secrets are revealed. The first is that since only the substantive verb signifies substance (whence it is called "substantive"), while other verbs signify accidents (which is why they are called "adjectives"), only the substantive verb in the indicative mood designates stability, while the others designate flux. Therefore, because all the letters of this name are taken from the substantive verb in the indicative mood, the total and eternal stability of the divine persons is denoted. 

The second secret is that this name consists of the same letters from which the three tenses of the same verb are composed: the past, present, and future. Among them, they sound like this: **היה** *haiah*, that is, "he was"; **הוה** *houe*, which means "is"; and **יהיה** *ihie*, that is, "he will be." Thus, from this, the eternity of these same persons is most clearly revealed: namely, that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit always were, are, and shall be.

For He is surely the one whom the prophets foretold would come to save the human race, and who would one day be pointed out with a finger, according to that passage in Isaiah, chapter 35: **אלהים הוא יבא וישעכם** <note>original: "Elohim hu yavo veyoshakhem"</note>, which is to say: "God Himself will come and save you." Finally, the third name is constituted from the third and fourth letters, namely from *Vav* and *He*, thus: **ויהו** (*Vehu*), and the whole of it sounds like "And He Himself," denoting the Holy Spirit. For He also was to be sent visibly after the Son, though not in the same manner. For the Son was to be sent in a human nature hypostatically <term>hypostatically: the union of divine and human natures in the single person of Christ</term> united to Himself. The Holy Spirit, however, was sent in the form of a dove and in tongues of fire, not hypostatically united to Himself, but as if under a sign.

In this, moreover, the second name descends from the first, and the third from the second. For the letter **ה** (*He*) is common to the first and second names, and the **ו** (*Vav*) is common to the second and third. This clearly shows that the Son is consubstantial <note>of the same essence or substance</note> with the Father, by whom He was begotten, and the Holy Spirit is consubstantial with the Son, who is consubstantial with the Father. Thus it is openly clear that the Son is in the Father, and the Father is in the Son, and the Holy Spirit is in both.

**CHAPTER.** I also judge it was not done without a great mystery that all the letters of this name are the very same as those from which the three tenses—namely the past, present, and future—of the substantive verb <note>The verb "to be."</note> in the indicative mood are formed among the Hebrews.

**GALATINUS.** It is exactly as you say. For in this, two secrets are revealed. The first indeed is that only the substantive verb signifies "substance" (from which it is called substantive), while others signify "accident" <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "substance" is what a thing is, while "accidents" are secondary qualities like color or size.</note>, which is why they are called adjectives. Therefore, only the substantive verb in the indicative mood designates stability, while the others designate changeability. In this, therefore, because all the letters of this name are taken from the substantive verb in the indicative mood, the absolute and eternal stability of the divine persons is denoted.

The second secret is that this name consists of the same letters from which the three tenses of the same verb are composed, which are the past, present, and future. Among them, they sound like this: **היה** (*haiah*), that is, "He was"; **הוה** (*houe*), which signifies "He is"; and **יהיה** (*ihie*), that is, "He will be." From this, the eternity of these same persons is most clearly revealed: namely, that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit always have been, are, and will be.

**CHAPTER.** Why is this name called among the Hebrews **שם המפורש** (*Shem HaMephorash*), which for us is the same as "The Explained" or "The Declared" name?

**GALATINUS.**

# BOOK TWO

<margin>Why this name is called *Sem hammephoras*.</margin>
The four-letter name of God <term>Tetragrammaton: The sacred four-letter name of God in Hebrew, YHWH.</term>, although it clearly (as has been shown) suggested the mystery of the divine Trinity alongside the unity of His essence. Because, however, the full declaration of this mystery had been reserved for the Messiah, it was not explicitly set forth in the Old Testament. This was done lest those unrefined and worldly people fall into the error of those who worship a plurality of gods. For this reason, Moses spoke to them with a veiled face. This was to imply that secrets of this kind ought not to have been handed down to them except through figures and riddles. Those, however, who were inspired by the grace of the Holy Spirit and understood the meaning of this name, handed it down only to a very few and worthy individuals. They explained the name itself first through a twelve-letter name, and finally through a forty-two-letter name. Nevertheless, as Rabbi Moses ben Maimon <note>Also known as Maimonides (1138–1204), one of the most influential Torah scholars and philosophers of the Middle Ages.</note> says in the book *The Guide* <note>The *Moreh Nevukhim* or *Guide for the Perplexed*.</note> in the 40th chapter of the first part: they did not assert that either the twelve-letter name or the forty-two-letter name was the *Sem hammephoras* <note>original: "שם המפורש", *Shem HaMephorash*</note>, which means "the explicit name." For the *Sem hammephoras* belongs to the holy and blessed God alone, and it is the four-letter name, just as we showed a little earlier. These other two names, however, necessarily provided a person with the knowledge and understanding of God, because through them they explained the four-letter name itself. Therefore, they called this Tetragrammaton *Sem hammephoras*, that is, the "explained" name, because the ancient Hebrews explained it through the names of twelve and forty-two letters—and it was to be explained even better, more distinctly, and more clearly by the Messiah.

However, it is clear to me, and it is my strong opinion, that it was not a single name, but two or three names joined together, whose letters totaled twelve. And those ancient holy fathers, whenever the four-letter name—namely יהוה <note>YHWH</note>—occurred in sacred scripture, they would pronounce and explain it using those twelve letters. Just as today we pronounce it with these four—aleph, daleth, nun, iod—that is, with the name אדני *Adonai* <note>Meaning "Lord." Nor did they prevent anyone from knowing it; rather, they taught it to anyone who wished to learn. But they did not do so with the four-letter name. For they taught it to no one who knew it except their sons and disciples who were worthy of such knowledge, and this only once a week. But when schismatic and insolent men multiplied in the world and learned the twelve-letter name, they corrupted religious belief with it. Just as happens to one who is imperfect when he perceives a matter is not as it first seemed to him. For this reason, those fathers hid that twelve-letter name and taught it to no one further except to the honorable and modest who were in the priesthood, so that they might bless the people in the sanctuary with it, after they forbade the memory of the 'Exposed Name' <note>The *Shem HaMephorash* or Tetragrammaton.</note> in the sanctuary due to the malice of the sons of Adam." All these things says that Rabbi Moses the Egyptian, son of Maimon. Since, therefore, this Rabbi says that the twelve-letter name was not one name, but two or three names consisting of twelve letters, through which those ancient fathers pronounced and explained the Tetragrammaton name (which distinctly suggests the mystery of the divine Trinity), it is established without doubt

# THE TWELVE-LETTER NAME

The second indeed, namely בן <note>original: "Ben"</note>, which is the same as Son, is also written with two letters. <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'N' depicting a figure in a landscape with buildings in the background.</image-desc> **N**ow it remains for you to say what the name of God of forty-two letters is, and how the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> name of God was explained by the ancient Jews through it.

<note>The following is a Hebrew passage from Maimonides, which translates as follows:</note>
Rabbi Tarfon said: "Once I went up after my mother’s brother to the priest’s platform, and I inclined my ear toward the High Priest, and I heard him swallowing [muffling] the Name during the singing of his brother priests." Indeed, these words of many letters were called a "Name" because they pointed to a single concept, just like other proper names. These many words were necessary for the understanding of the matter, because a single concept cannot be understood except through many words.

# SECOND [BOOK]

Understand this many times over: the matter that was learned consisted of the concepts indicated by those names, not merely the speech of the inscribed letters devoid of meaning. Neither the Twelve-Letter Name nor the Forty-Two-Letter Name was called the <term>Explicit Name</term> <note>Hebrew: "Shem Ha-Mephorash." This refers to the unique, specific name of God (the Tetragrammaton) as opposed to descriptive titles.</note>; rather, the Explicit Name is the name specifically assigned to Him, as we have explained. However, these other two names necessarily teach some portion of Divine Science. The proof that the Forty-Two-Letter Name teaches wisdom is what is said of it: it is "holy and sanctified," and it is not handed down except to one who is humble, middle-aged, not prone to anger, not given to drink, not insistent on his own way, and whose speech is gentle with other creatures. Anyone who knows it, is careful with it, and guards it in purity is beloved above and cherished below; he is feared by all creatures, his learning remains established in his hand, and he inherits two worlds: this world and the world to come. This is written in the <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism. This specific passage is found in the tractate Kiddushin 71a.</note>. Yet, how far removed is the common understanding of this passage from its true intent! For most people think these are merely letters to be spoken as a single word, and it is not explained to them that these words lead to those great concepts. It is distressing to see those who rush to teach the understanding of these mentioned words; for it is clear that all of this is nothing but the communication of divine matters from the collection of topics known as the <term>Secrets of the Torah</term> <note>Hebrew: "Sitrei Torah." These are the esoteric or mystical interpretations of the law, often reserved for advanced scholars.</note>, as we have explained. It has already been explained in books composed on Divine Science that this wisdom cannot be forgotten—that is to say, the attainment of the <term>Active Intellect</term> <note>A philosophical concept from the Middle Ages referring to the medium through which human beings achieve intellectual understanding and connection to the Divine.</note>—and this is the meaning of the phrase "his learning remains established in his hand."

This is: Rabbi Tarphon said, "I once went up behind my mother's father into the Temple, and I inclined my ear toward the priest. I perceived that his brothers, the priests, were asking him questions. Among them was the Name of Forty-Two Letters." However, anyone with a strong intellect knows it is impossible for a single word to consist of forty-two letters; rather, they were many words composed of forty-two letters. There is no doubt that all of them signified certain reasons that lead a person to the truth of the Creator's essence, in the manner we have described. Indeed, those words of many letters were called "one name" because of the single thing they signified, just as other names are taken from various works. But there was a multitude of those words so that the concept might be understood, which perhaps could not be understood except through many words. Therefore, take note of this. And consider that the matter demonstrated by the science of the reasons signified by those names was not a matter of simple speech or letters. For it was never said that the Twelve-Letter Name or the Forty-Two-Letter Name was the <term>Shem Ha-Mephorash</term> <note>original: "sem hammephoras." The Explicit Name.</note>, that is, the "Exposed Name." For the Explicit Name is that which is uniquely appropriate to Him, as we have already declared. These two names, however, were of great help to a person in knowing the Creator. The proof of this matter is that, as the Sages say, the Forty-Two-Letter Name is holy and sanctified, and it is not revealed except to the humble, to one who has passed the middle of his life, and who is not at all wrathful, or a drunkard, or of perverse morals, but is instead affable. Whoever possesses the knowledge of that name, is cautious with it, and guards it with purity: he is loved by those above and desired by those below; he is feared by every creature, his discipline is perpetual in his hand, and he shall obtain two worlds—

# [SECOND] BOOK

...it is found. As when many words or names occur in the same clause: the letter **ו** (*vau*) <note>The Hebrew letter *Vav*, which functions as the conjunction "and."</note>, which makes the word copulative, is always found placed with the last one. And to omit other examples of this kind, I will bring forward that one from Exodus chapter 3: **יהוה אלהי אבותיכם אלהי אברהם אלהי יצחק ואלהי יעקב שלחני אליכם** <note>original: "YHVH Elohei avoteichem, Elohei Avraham, Elohei Yitzchak, v'Elohei Yaakov shelachani aleichem"</note> That is: "The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob has sent me to you." You see that the letter **ו** (*vau*), which effects the coupling, is placed only with the last name: and you will find it so in similar cases as well.

But then we say: that a certain one of their ancients, whom they call **רבינו הקדוש** <term>Rabbenu Haccados</term> <note>Literally "Our Holy Teacher," the title for Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century redactor of the Mishnah.</note>—whom to contradict is considered a sin among them—in the first petition of the book **גלי רזיא** <term>Gale Razeya</term> <note>Meaning "Revealer of Secrets"; a work of mystical lore Galatinus frequently cites to support Christian doctrines.</note>, explains the Four-Letter Name of God through forty-two letters in another way, and nowhere places this letter **ו** (*vau*). For he says thus (as we said above): "Because truly nothing is found in God that is not God, from the Name of Twelve Letters emanates the Name of Forty-Two, which is: **אב אלהים . בן אלהים רוח הקדש אלהים שלשה באחד אחד בשלשה** <note>original: "Ab Elohim, Ben Elohim, Ruach Ha-Kodesh Elohim, Sheloshah b'Echad, Echad b'Sheloshah"</note> This is: Father God, Son God, Holy Spirit God: Three in one, and one in three: or Trinity in unity, and unity in trinity." 

In this phrase there are forty-two letters. In these, although the exposition itself may vary, the sense of the exposition does not vary at all: but is exactly the same in both places. For those ancient fathers, who were the disciples and successors of the prophets, when they explained the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name YHWH.</note> either through the Name of Twelve Letters or the Name of Forty-Two Letters, even if they explained it in diverse ways, all nevertheless agreed upon one and the same meaning. Namely, they were expressing the three divine persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—by the very same names by which we express them. They asserted each of these to be God, yet they said they were not three gods, but one God. And thus they expressly explained the Trinity of divine persons with the unity of the divine essence through forty-two letters. 

And this was the true and perfect exposition of the Four-Letter Name of God, which the ancient Hebrews performed through the Name of Forty-Two. The more recent [Jews], however, are entirely ignorant of it, and for that reason their prayers are not heard at all: as it is said in the <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>An ancient homiletic commentary on the Book of Psalms.</note> regarding that verse of Psalm 91: **אשגבהו כי ידע שמי יקראני ואענהו** "I will exalt him, because he has known my name: he shall call upon me, and I will answer him." But in the time to come, the Holy One (blessed be He) will make it known, as it is said: 'Because he knew my name.' At that hour they shall pray and immediately be answered, as it is said: 'He shall call upon me, and I will answer him.'" That is to say, for the reason...

# [SECOND] BOOK

...of the Jews <note>The text likely begins mid-word with "Iudaeorum" (of the Jews).</note>, because they do not know the Name *Shem HaMephorash* <term>hammephoras</term> <note>The "Explicit Name," refers to the Tetragrammaton (YHVH), which was traditionally only pronounced by the High Priest in the Temple.</note>, or the Four-Letter Name <term>tetragrammaton</term>. But it shall come to pass that God, holy and blessed, shall teach it to them, as it is said in Isaiah 52: "My people shall know my name." Then they shall truly pray, and they shall be heard. As it is said: "He shall call upon me, and I will answer him." This is the tradition. Since, therefore, according to this tradition, God himself was to teach men this blessed name—manifestly unlocking the mystery of the divine Trinity through its true exposition, which was to happen in the time of the Messiah, as <term>Rabbenu Haccados</term> <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century editor of the Mishnah.</note> testified in the preceding sections. For this reason, the Lord Jesus, the true Messiah and true Son of God, most perfectly taught his disciples (who were Israelites), most openly revealing the mystery of the divine Trinity. As is said in Matthew chapter 28: "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you." Therefore, in this form in which he commanded the instructed to be baptized, when he placed the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: he clearly suggested that he had already thoroughly taught his disciples the secret of the Trinity and divine Unity. For these three names—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—express the Trinity of the divine persons. Furthermore, in that he said "in the name," and not "in the names": he evidently showed that there is one essence and nature of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. And this is undoubtedly the most true and distinct exposition of the Four-Letter Name of God, which was explicitly contained both in the Name of Twelve Letters and in the Name of Forty-Two. With these names, namely of twelve and forty-two letters, our Lord Jesus Christ most perfectly explained the Four-Letter Name of God to his disciples. Wherefore, addressing the Father (as is held in John chapter 17), he said: "Father, I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me." And again he said: "These have known that thou hast sent me, and I have made known unto them thy name." Following the doctrine of the disciples of Christ, Athanasius <note>St. Athanasius (c. 296–373 AD), a key defender of Trinitarianism against Arianism.</note> excellently and perfectly explained the Four-Letter Name of God itself: first through the Name of Twelve Letters, which is (as was clear a little above) Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; then through the Name of Forty-Two, saying: "God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, and yet there are not three Gods, but there is one God." From which it is clearly evident that the faith of the ancient Hebrews and our own was one and the same.

## [SECOND] BOOK

...name <note>original: "nomen"</note> this [YHVH] <note>The Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God.</note> of which we made mention a little while ago, is called *Arba Otiyot* <note>Hebrew: ארבע אותיות; meaning "four letters."</note>, that is, "of four letters" or the *Tetragrammaton* <term>tetragrammaton</term>? GALATINUS: Because the letters of no other name so distinctly indicate the internal secrets of the divinity. For there is no doubt that this name [YHVH], of which we spoke just above—which is proper to God and signifies the divine nature more distinctly than others—also designates the secrets of the divine Trinity and Unity above all others. Other names of God, since they are not proper to God alone but are derived from works similar to those found in us <note>i.e., names based on human concepts of "Power" or "Judgement."</note>, do not so distinctly (like that one) introduce the sacred mysteries of the divine Trinity and Unity. Therefore, only that name, above the others, is called the Tetragrammaton by excellence, even if certain other names of God are found among the Hebrews to have four letters. CAPITO: For a greater expression of Catholic truth, I would wish you to say something about each of those names I brought forward as examples. And first indeed, in what way is the Trinity of divine persons suggested through the name *Adonai* <note>Hebrew: אדני</note>, which they pronounce in place of the four-letter name? GALATINUS: Certainly, the Trinity of divine persons is designated somewhat obscurely through this name *Adonai*, which is interpreted as "Lord." For just as the name *Elohim* <note>Hebrew: אלהים</note> implies plurality (as we showed above), so also *Adonai* is a plural name. For from this name *Adon* <note>Hebrew: אדון</note>, which is singular and signifies "Lord," comes the plural *Adonim* <note>Hebrew: אדונים</note>, which is the same as "Lords." From the singular name *Adon* comes *Adoni* <note>Hebrew: אדוני</note>, which is interpreted as "my Lord." But from the plural *Adonim* comes *Adonai*, which is a divine name and properly signifies "my Lords." Therefore, those ancient fathers, taught by Moses, decreed that God should be called "Lords" in the plural number, so that from this it might be openly shown that the universal dominion of things is common to the three divine persons. For the Father is Lord, the Son is Lord, the Holy Spirit is Lord. However, to suggest that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not three Lords, but one Lord, it was decreed that the name *Adonai* itself, even if it is plural, should not be joined except with a verb in the singular number, or with an adjective likewise in the singular.

[...has] sent me to you. If they say to me, "What is his name?" what shall I say to them? God, therefore, wishing to reveal his name to him, answered (as is found in Exodus, chapter 3): *“Ehyeh asher Ehyeh”* <note>original: אהיה אשר אהיה; typically translated as "I am who I am."</note> Thus you shall say to the children of Israel: *“Ehyeh”* <note>original: אהיה; meaning "I AM"</note> has sent me to you. This is *Ehyeh* <note>original: אהיה</note>, that is: I was, I am, and I will be. *Ehyeh Asher* <note>original: אהיה אשר</note>, that is: He who was, is, and will be. And he said: Thus you shall say to the children of Israel: *Ehyeh* <note>original: אהיה</note>—that is, he who was, is, and will be—sent me to you. 

Here, therefore, is placed the name of God, *Ehyeh*, which encompasses the distinctions of the three tenses of the indicative mood of the substantive verb <term>substantive verb</term><note>A grammatical term for the verb "to be" (am, was, shall be).</note>: namely the past, the present, and the future, which are "I was," "I am," and "I will be." Therefore the name itself, *Ehyeh* <note>original: אהיה</note>, is interpreted as "I was, I am, and I will be." For the second and third letters of the name itself, namely *He* <note>original: ה</note> and *Yod* <note>original: י</note>, designate the first person (which is the third person among them <note>In Hebrew grammar, the third-person masculine singular is the root form, unlike Latin or English which often begin with the first person "I."</note>) of the past tense of the same verb, which is *hayiti* <note>original: היתי</note>, that is, "I was." 

The fourth letter of that name, however, namely *He* <note>original: ה</note>, indicates the first person of the present tense, which is *hoveh* <note>original: הוה</note>, that is, "I am." Moreover, the first letter, namely *Aleph* <note>original: א</note>, which is usually placed at the beginning of the first person of the future tense of any verb, denotes the first person of the future tense of that same verb. Although the first person for us is the third for them, and the third for us is the first for them—since they begin to conjugate verbs from the third person—it is manifest from these things that this name *Ehyeh* <note>original: אהיה</note> contains within itself the differences of the three tenses of the indicative mood of the verb "to be." 

For this reason, "I was, I am, and I will be" is most aptly interpreted to suggest the supreme, all-encompassing, and eternal stability of God, who always was, is, and will be. Next, in order to show the Trinity of persons and the unity of essence, God himself, addressing Moses, added this in Exodus, chapter 3: *“YHVH Elohei avotekhem, Elohei Avraham, Elohei Yitzchak, v’Elohei Yaakov shelachani aleikhem”* <note>original: יהוה אלהי אבתיכם אלהי אברהם אלהי יצחק ואלהי יעקב שלחני אליכם</note>. That is: "Thus you shall say to the children of Israel: The Lord <note>original: יהוה; the Tetragrammaton</note> God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob has sent me to you." 

For in the fact that he said "God" three times, he expressly suggested the Trinity of persons. But in the fact that he said "Lord" <note>original: Dominus</note> once, and said "he sent" <note>singular</note> rather than "they sent" <note>plural</note>, he demonstrated the unity of the divine nature. Finally, so that he might indicate that this name *Ehyeh* <note>original: אהיה</note> was his own—through which the eternal and all-encompassing stability of the divine Trinity and Unity is conveyed—he immediately added: "This is my name forever" <note>original: זה שמי לעולם</note>.

**HOGOSTRATUS.** Since these things are as you say, I wonder greatly that the author of our edition <note>Referring to the Vulgate, the standard Latin Bible used by the Church.</note> did not translate this passage in the way you have. For he says it thus: God said to Moses, "I am who I am." Thus you shall say to the children of Israel: "He who is, has sent me to you."

For there are many things in the secrets of the Law and the Prophets which the Hebrew way of writing and reading suggests, which nevertheless cannot be transferred into another language. This appears most especially in the divine names themselves, in which for the most part both the Greek as well as...

**CAP.** <note>Capnio, the nickname for Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering Christian Hebraist.</note> Although those things you said about the name *Ehyeh* <note>original: אהיה; "I AM"</note> are so true that they can in no way be denied, there is one thing, however, which I wonder at greatly. For when God, speaking of this name, said: *Zeh shemi le-olam* <note>original: זה שמי לעלם; "This is my name forever" (Exodus 3:15).</note> all our interpreters (as you also interpreted) translate it as, "This is my name forever." Without it, the word can be read differently.</note> [לעולם], but since it is written without the *vav* [לעלם], it should be pointed not as *le-olam* [forever], but as *le-allem* [to hide], since this word comes from the verb *alam* <note>original: עלם</note>, which signifies "to obscure" or "to conceal." Therefore, that saying of God should be correctly translated as: "This is my name to be hidden," or "to be concealed." By this, it is clearly understood that other secrets, besides those you mentioned, lie hidden in the name *Ehyeh*, which are left to be discussed by the Kabbalists. I would therefore like to know from you what these secrets are, lying hidden in this divine name. 

**GAL.** <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), the author of this work and defender of Hebrew learning.</note> I would rather desire to learn these things from you, who not only have the best knowledge of Hebrew letters, but also excel others in the skill of Kabbalistic wisdom. However, to satisfy your request, I will bring forward the words of Rabbi Abraham of Pico <note>original: Abraham Picí; likely referring to a source used by Pico della Mirandola or a specific Kabbalistic manuscript.</note>, who in the little book he published on the meaning of the <term>taghín</term> <note>Taghin are small decorative "crowns" or strokes drawn on certain letters in a Torah scroll.</note>, that is, the apexes which are written above the letters of the Law, says thus:

"And behold, I awaken you to the matter of the secret of this great sign, and do not forget; and this sign includes letters. Look at them and you will find upon them, in the first parts, strokes; and this is the secret of *Ehyeh*. This sign is included with the Great Name <note>The Tetragrammaton (YHWH).</note>, and to this God hinted when he said to Moses: 'I AM THAT I AM' (*Ehyeh asher Ehyeh*). The seal of the verse is: '*Ehyeh* has sent me to you.' This means *Ehyeh* three times, corresponding to the three strokes on each and every letter. And you should exert yourself in the whole sign, the secret of your calculation. Another thing: the three strokes on each letter correspond to the three fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—who are mentioned immediately after it is said: 'And God said to Moses, I AM THAT I AM; thus shall you say to the house of Jacob and tell the children of Israel: The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob has sent me to you. This is my name to hide (*le-allem*) and this is my memorial from generation to generation.' And look at the letters of the names of the fathers and you will understand the secret of the thirteen attributes, as we have explained. Also, when you examine closely, you will understand the secret of *Yah* <note>A shortened form of the divine name.</note>, for you will find fifteen strokes above the names of the fathers. Here then is the secret of the thirteen attributes, the secret of *Ehyeh*, and the secret of the Great Explicit Name. Indeed, concerning each name of the fathers and the power of the Divinity which said 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob,' when you examine the name *Elohei* [God of], you will find the Name hinted in it twice. He who understands will understand. And this is what is meant by 'This is my name to hide' (*le-allem*) in its written form; it means to say: 'This is my name to be hidden,' which is not to be revealed except to a person who is modest and understands the Kabbalah. Furthermore, this is hinted at in the Prophets: 'But the Lord is in his holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before him' [Habakkuk 2:20]. And thus he hinted at the secret of the Lord [*Adonai*]... and besides the Great Name, you will find the Great Name hinted in this verse: 'And they shall say to me, what is his name?'... and it appears that by way of these verses the name *Ehyeh* is said: 'This is my name to hide,' in 'I AM [*Ehyeh*] has sent me to you.'"

### *Concerning the name of God Agla, through which the infinite power of the divine trinity is expressed. Chapter xv.*

->GALATINUS,<-

In order that I may say even a very few things concerning the name of God *Agla* <note>original: אגלא</note> to satisfy your request, I would have you know that the name of God *Agla* itself (as its letters suggest) denotes nothing other than the eternal and infinite power of God, which He possesses in respect to creation, whether yet to be produced or already produced. For the first letter, namely *Aleph* <note>original: א</note>, stands for *Atta* <note>original: אתה</note>, which is "Thou." The second, namely *Ghimel* <note>original: ג</note>, stands for *Ghibor* <note>original: גבור</note>, which is interpreted as "Mighty." The third, namely *Lamech* <note>original: ל</note>, stands for *Leholam* <note>original: לעולם</note>, which is the same as "forever." Finally, the fourth, namely *Aleph* <note>original: א</note>, stands for *Adonai* <note>original: אדני</note>, which is translated as "Lord" in our language. From this it is clearly evident that the name *Agla* itself signifies nothing other than this whole phrase: *Atta Ghibor Leholam Adonai* <note>original: אתה גבור לעולם אדני</note>, that is: "Thou art mighty forever, O Lord." <note>This is a famous acronym or "notarikon" derived from the second blessing of the Amidah, a central prayer in Jewish liturgy.</note> From these things, therefore, it is plain that this same name *Agla* openly expresses the very omnipotence of the divine trinity.

---

### *Concerning the name of God Shaddai, through which the all-encompassing sufficiency, by which God alone is sufficient unto Himself, is best designated. Chapter xvi.*

->CAPNIO,<-

There is also another name of God, which frequently occurs in the sacred scriptures, called *Sadai* <note>original: שדי; usually transliterated as Shaddai</note>. I ask that you say something concerning it as well.

GALATINUS: One must therefore note what Rabbi Moses, son of Maimon <note>Moses Maimonides, the influential 12th-century philosopher and jurist.</note>, says concerning this name in that book which among the Jews is titled *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: מורה הנבוכים; More hannebochím</note>. For there, at the end of the forty-second chapter of the first part, he says among other things: The name *Sadai* is composed of the word *dai* <note>original: די</note>, which is "it suffices," and from the letter which is called *Shin* <note>original: ש</note>. Moreover, the word *dai* signifies sufficiency, as is evident from this: in the first [chapter] of Obadiah <note>original: Abdiam</note> it is said: "If thieves had come to you, or if robbers by night, how would you have been silenced? Would they not have stolen *dayam* <note>original: דים</note>," that is, their sufficiency? <note>Obadiah 1:5; standard English bibles usually translate this as "as much as they wanted" or "enough for themselves."</note> Furthermore, the letter *shin*, which is placed before this name *Sadai*, is the same as *asser* <note>original: אשר; asher</note>, that is, "who" or "which." For which reason *Sadai* is the same as *asser dai*, that is, "He who suffices," or "He who is sufficient," or "He who is sufficiency." Therefore, this name is never found among the Hebrews except as spoken of God alone. Nor is it a wonder, since its meaning is (as has been said) "He who suffices," or "He who is sufficient," or "He who is suffi—"

<meta>catchword: —ciency (sufficientia)</meta>

<summary>This page explains the mystical acronym Agla as "Thou art mighty forever, O Lord" and begins an etymological analysis of the name Shaddai based on Maimonides' Guide for the Perplexed.</summary>

<header>BOOK</header>

is sufficiency. It is manifest that this belongs to God alone. For as the philosopher *Al-Ghazali* <note>original: "Algazel"; referring to the 11th-century Persian theologian and philosopher</note> says in the book written concerning the names of God, God alone is simply and absolutely wealthy, and the one who bestows wealth. For He depends on no other either in His substance or in His qualities, but with all things pertaining to Himself, He is entirely immune from all dependency. Then he adds: Therefore, He who is wealthy and sufficient unto Himself absolutely and in truth is the one who needs nothing else. And this is God alone. Truly, concerning all others, this is said figuratively, or according to a certain respect. Thus far *Al-Ghazali*. Since, therefore, the one and triune God alone is sufficient unto Himself, for that reason the name <term>Shaddai</term> <note>original: שדי (Sadai); traditionally translated as "Almighty," though derived here from the Hebrew "She-dai," meaning "He who is sufficient"</note> rightly implies and signifies the sufficiency of the divine Trinity, by which God is sufficient unto Himself.

### Concerning the seventy-two names of God, through which the perfections of the divine trinity and unity are most aptly suggested.
#### Chapter XVII.

->CAPNIO,<-

**S**ince many have said many things about the seventy-two names of God, and some indeed empty and worthy of laughter: for that reason, for a greater knowledge of the divine names, I would finally like to hear your opinion concerning them. **GAL.** I shall therefore say regarding these things only what I have received from the Kabbalistic books. First, I will bring forward the texts from which the names themselves are formed, from the fourteenth chapter of Exodus, where it is said thus in Hebrew:

<note>The following are Exodus 14:19, 20, and 21 in Hebrew. Each verse in the original Hebrew contains exactly 72 letters.</note>
וַיִּסַּע מַלְאַךְ הָאֱלֹהִים הַהֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵי מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֵּלֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶם וַיִּסַּע עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן מִפְּנֵיהֶם וַיַּעֲמֹד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶם׃
וַיָּבֹא בֵּין מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיְהִי הֶעָנָן וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ וַיָּאֶר אֶת־הַלָּיְלָה וְלֹא־קָרַב זֶה אֶל־זֶה כָּל־הַלָּיְלָה׃
וַיֵּט מֹשֶׁה אֶת־יָדוֹ עַל־הַיָּם וַיּוֹלֶךְ יְהוָה אֶת־הַיָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה כָּל־הַלַּיְלָה וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת־הַיָּם לֶחָרָבָה וַיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמָּיִם׃

->This is it, that I may render it word for word.<-

And the Angel of the Gods <note>original: "Deorum"; Galatinus often uses the plural "Gods" for "Elohim" to argue for the Trinity</note> who went before the camp of Israel moved himself, and went behind them: and the pillar of the cloud moved itself from their face, and stood behind them.

And it came between the camp of the Egyptians, and between the camp of Israel, and there was a cloud and darkness, and it illuminated the night, and the one did not approach the other all night.

And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and God took away the sea by a strong south wind <note>original: "uento noto"; the Hebrew "kadim" usually means east wind, but Galatinus uses the Latin term for a southern/moist wind</note> all night, and turned the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided.

This series of words is indeed distinguished among the Hebrews into three <term>pasukhim</term> <note>original: פסוקים; meaning "verses"</note>, that is, texts or verses. Each of which consists of seventy-two letters. From which the Kabbalists in a certain wondrous way [derive] two...

they extracted seventy-two names of God <note>These are known as the Shem HaMephorash, derived from three verses in Exodus (14:19–21), each containing 72 letters.</note>. And they did this indeed in ten ways.

<margin>Rule for names of the first mode</margin>
The first of these is that first, the first letter of the first verse is taken, which is *vav* <note>original: ו (uau)</note>. Immediately after, the last letter of the second verse, which is *he* <note>original: ה (he)</note>; finally, the first letter of the third verse, which is *vav* <note>original: ו (uau)</note>. From these three letters results the first name of the first mode, which is *Vav-He-Vav* <note>original: והו</note>. Next, they take the second letter of the first verse, which is *yod* <note>original: י (iod)</note>: then the second-to-last of the second, which is *lamed* <note>original: ל (lamed)</note>: finally, the second of the last verse, which is *yod* <note>original: י (iod)</note>. And thus they constitute the second name, which is *Yod-Lamed-Yod* <note>original: ילי</note>. And so, observing this order, they proceed continuously until the entire number of letters is exhausted. This is easily apparent to anyone looking at the names of the first mode themselves.

<margin>Rule for names of the second mode.</margin>
Indeed, the names of the second mode are formed from the same letters according to them in this way. First, therefore, take the first letter of the first verse or text, which is *vav* <note>original: ו (uau)</note>; and the first of the second, which is also *vav* <note>original: ו (uau)</note>; and the first of the third, which is likewise *vav* <note>original: ו (uau)</note>. And thus you will form the first name of the second mode, which is *Vav-Vav-Vav* <note>original: ווו</note>. Then if you take the second letter of the first text, which is *yod* <note>original: י (iod)</note>; and the second of the second, which is similarly *yod* <note>original: י (iod)</note>; and the second of the third, which is also *yod* <note>original: י (iod)</note>; you will constitute the second name of the second mode, which is *Yod-Yod-Yod* <note>original: ייי</note>. Likewise, from the third letter of the first text, which is *samekh* <note>original: ס (samach)</note>; and from the third of the second, which is *bet* <note>original: ב (beth)</note>; and from the third of the third, which is *tet* <note>original: ט (teth)</note>: the third name of the second mode is composed, which is *Samekh-Bet-Tet* <note>original: סבט</note>. And so by proceeding in this order until all the letters of the same texts are exhausted, seventy-two names of the second mode are produced. As can be seen by looking at these same names of the second mode. Moreover, as for the names of the remaining eight modes, and how they are composed from these same letters: I do not hand down those rules now for the sake of avoiding wordiness, but I leave them to be investigated by the studious. For everyone will think (as I suppose) that I have done enough when they see that I have both handed down the rules for composing the names of the first and second modes, and reported all the names themselves of the ten modes (just as I found them in the books of the Kabbalists).

<meta>This page transitions from the technical listing of the 72 names of God into a dialogue between Capnio (the scholar Reuchlin) and Galatinus regarding the specific Hebrew vowel-pointing (punctuation) used in these names. It explores the legitimacy of these markings and their mystical significance within Christian Kabbalah.</meta>

<page-num>100</page-num>

->BOOK<-

**CAPNIO:** Some of our people say that the names of the first and second modes, punctuated <term>punctuated: Referring to the *nikkud*, or Hebrew vowel points, which indicate pronunciation in a script that otherwise only uses consonants.</term> as you have set them down, are not truly Hebrew, because they are punctuated contrary to the usual custom of Hebrew writing.

**GALATINUS:** Perhaps those who say this are of that class of men who, failing to measure themselves and their own abilities correctly, think they know everything to such an extent that they assume no one else can know what they themselves do not. You, however, would never say such a thing—partly because you have always loathed the habits of such men, and partly because you have (I believe) frequently read these same names punctuated this way in Kabbalistic books, especially those of the first mode. I too have found them punctuated exactly this way in many places, and particularly in Rome, in the library of the Supreme Pontiff, in that place where the books of Flamineus <note>original: "libri Flaminei." This likely refers to the collection of the scholar and poet Marcantonio Flaminio, or perhaps a reference to the Vatican's specific Hebrew holdings managed by certain scholars.</note>—a man once most skilled in the three languages—are kept in storage. Therefore, let those who deny that these names are Hebrew when punctuated this way seek them there among the Hebrew codices; they will find the names of the first mode punctuated exactly so. And even if they are somewhat corrupted there by the fault of the scribes, I have nevertheless taken care to report them more correctly according to the rules of the Kabbalists.

<margin>Why the names of the first and second mode are punctuated in this way.</margin>

**CAPNIO:** It is not without reason, then, that many desire to know why these names are punctuated with marks of this kind.

**GALATINUS:** Although this is considered a supreme secret among the Kabbalists—so much so that they command it must by no means be written down, but only revealed by word of mouth and only to the very few who are worthy—lest by "casting pearls before swine" <note>A reference to Matthew 7:6, suggesting that sacred knowledge should not be shared with those who will not respect it.</note> the divine names should become known to the unworthy and the vile. Nevertheless, since it is my greatest desire to hide the truth from no one, but rather to make it plain to all, I shall speak. These names are punctuated in this way because the letters from which they are fashioned are found punctuated thus in the aforementioned texts. For the letters that are found punctuated in those texts, together with the points themselves, join together to form these names. However, those letters that are not found punctuated in those same texts—such as those placed at the end of words, which for the most part happen not to be punctuated—are punctuated in these names with the points that their natural pronunciation requires. This is clear to anyone looking at the names themselves. Nor did the Kabbalists wish them to be punctuated this way without a great mystery: for from this kind of punctuation, there results in each of these names a **trinity of syllables**, which distinctly designates the **trinity of divine persons** in one divine essence.

**CAPNIO:** How are these names interpreted?

**GALATINUS:** Certain of our people have interpreted the names of the first mode in this way:

The Exalter, The Helper, Hope, Salvation, The One who is Sought, The One who is Proclaimed, The Patient One, The One to be Adored, The One to be Remembered, You, The One to be Exalted, The Timely One; The Celebrated, The Uplifter, Being, The Advocate, The Ruler, Justice, The One who Hears, The Rescuer, The Strong, The Right Hand, The Guardian, The One to be Awaited; The Wonderful, The One to be Invoked, The Savior, The Swift, The Healer, From Youth, The Only One, The Upright, The Thoughtful, Expectation, Entreaty, Glory; The Face, The Refuge, The Helper, The Repeller, The Liberator, The Guardian, The One of the Morning, The Teacher, The Compassionate, The Worker, The Magnificent, The Revealer; The Greatest, The Clement, The Rejoicing, The Most High...

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between the scholar Capnio (Johannes Reuchlin) and the theologian Galatinus. On the previous page, they were discussing the list of divine names (the 72-fold name of God) and their specific linguistic structure. Here, they address the unusual vowel-pointing (vocalization) of these names and provide their Latin-to-English semantic interpretations.</meta>

<header>BOOK</header>

**CAPNIO.** Some of our people say that the names of the first and second modes, pointed with vowels as you have set them down, are not truly Hebrew, because they are pointed contrary to the standard custom of Hebrew writing. **GALATINUS.** Perhaps those who say this are of that sort of men who, not measuring themselves or their own abilities correctly, believe they know everything so thoroughly that they think no one else can know what they themselves are ignorant of. You, however, would never say such a thing—partly because you have always detested the manners of such men, and partly because you have (I believe) frequently read these same names pointed in this way in Kabbalistic <term>Kabbalistic: Referring to Kabbalah, a school of thought in Jewish mysticism; Christian scholars like Reuchlin and Galatinus studied it to find parallels with Christian doctrine.</term> books, especially those of the first mode. I, too, have found them pointed exactly thus in many places, and particularly in Rome, in the library of the Supreme Pontiff <note>The Vatican Library.</note>, in the place where the books of Flamineus <note>original: "Flaminei." Refers to Flavio Mithridates, a 15th-century Jewish convert and scholar who translated Kabbalistic texts for Pico della Mirandola and the Pope.</note>—once a man most skilled in three languages—are kept in storage. Therefore, let those who deny that these names are Hebrew because of their pointing look there among the Hebrew manuscripts, and they will find the names of the first mode pointed in this very way. And even if they have been somewhat corrupted there by the error of scribes, I have nevertheless taken care to report them more accurately according to the rules of the Kabbalists.

<margin>Why the names of the first and second modes are pointed in this way.</margin>
**CAPNIO.** Not without reason, then, some desire to know why these names are vocalized with points of this kind. **GALATINUS.** Although this is a very great secret among the Kabbalists—so much so that they command it should by no means be written down, but revealed only by word of mouth and to only a very few worthy people, lest by "placing pearls before swine" <note>A biblical idiom meaning to share sacred knowledge with those who cannot appreciate its value.</note> the divine names should become known to the unworthy and the base—nonetheless, I, who have it most at heart to hide the truth from no one, but rather to reveal it to all, shall speak. These names are pointed thus because the letters from which they are constructed are found pointed in that way in the aforementioned texts. For the letters found pointed in the scriptural texts themselves, along with those same vowel points, concur in the formation of these names. However, those letters that are not pointed in the same texts—such as those placed at the end of words, which for the most part do not receive vowel points—are vocalized in these names with the points that their natural pronunciation requires. This is clear to anyone looking at the names themselves. Yet the Kabbalists did not wish them to be pointed thus without a great mystery. For from this kind of pointing, a trinity of syllables results in each of these names, which distinctly designates the Trinity of Divine Persons in one divine essence. <note>This is a central argument of "Christian Kabbalah": that Hebrew mystical structures secretly confirm the Christian doctrine of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note> **CAPNIO.** How are these names interpreted? **GALATINUS.** Some of our people have interpreted the names of the first mode in this way:

Exalter, Helper, Hope, Salvation, Sought, Announced, Patient, Adorable, Memorable, You, Worthy of Exaltation, Timely; Renowned, Uplifter, Being, Advocate, Ruler, Justice, Hearer, Deliverer, Strong, Right Hand, Guardian, Long-Awaited; Wonderful, Invokable, Savior, Swift, Healer, From Youth, Alone, Righteous, Thoughtful, Expectation, Entreaty, Glory; Face, Refuge, Assistant, Driver-away, Liberator, Guardian, Morning, Teacher, Compassionate, Worker, Magnificent, Revealer; Greatest, Merciful, Joyful, Most High,

To these seventy-two aforementioned verses, which are taken from various Psalms, they apply the seventy-two interpretations previously discussed. They claim these are the interpretations of those seventy-two names of God, which are formed from the letters of the three previously mentioned texts in the first method. <note>This refers to the "First Method" of extracting the 72 names from Exodus 14:19-21.</note> But they are certainly very much mistaken. For these interpretations are clearly recognized as belonging not to the names themselves, but rather to the verses to which they are applied.

Indeed, the Jews <note>The author uses 'Iudæi' to refer to the Hebrew scholars and Kabbalists whose works he is examining.</note> devised these seventy-two interpretations according to the meaning of these seventy-two verses, treating them like the seventy-two names of God so they might serve as a kind of index for those same verses. This is clearly shown by the fact that these interpretations correspond not to the names of God themselves, but to the verses to which they are attached. For example, this name *The Exalter* <note>original: "Exaltator"</note> has no connection with this name <term>YHV <note>original Hebrew: יהו</note></term>, but only fits the verse to which it is applied: namely, "And you, God, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who exalts my head." <note>Psalm 3:3.</note> Similarly, *The Helper* <note>original: "Auxiliator"</note> in no way matches this name <term>YHVH <note>original Hebrew: יהוה</note></term>, but only this verse to which it is applied: "And you, God, do not stay far away; my strength, hasten to my help." <note>Psalm 22:19.</note> You will find the same thing in all the others if you look carefully.

# Concerning the divinity of the Messiah and concerning his names designating his divine nature.

### *That the Son of God was to be incarnated, taking a body from a woman. Chapter 1.*

->CAPNIO,<-
<note>Capnio is the Greek-style pseudonym of Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and Hebraist.</note>

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'C' depicting a nude infant or putto sitting amidst elaborate scrolling floral and leaf motifs.</image-desc>SINCE you have sufficiently proved through the Jewish scriptures that God is both three and one, it is now fitting for you to say something regarding those things contained in their books about the incarnation of the Son of God. 

GALATINUS. It is certainly necessary, not merely fitting; for we must speak especially against their lack of faith <note>original: "perfidiam." In Renaissance polemics, this specifically refers to the Jewish rejection of Christian doctrine.</note> regarding those matters which pertain to the Messiah. While they deny that he would be both God and man in the future, they are by no means willing to believe in the work of the divine incarnation. The prophet Habakkuk prophesied well concerning their unbelief in the first chapter, saying: "For a work is being performed in your days, which you will not believe when it is told." <note>original Hebrew: "כי פועל פועל בימיכם לא תאמינו כי יסופר" (Habakkuk 1:5).</note> That is: *Because a work will be done in your days, which you will not believe when it is told.* It is certain that the prophet was speaking here about the work of the divine incarnation, which the greatest part of the Jews, in their obstinacy, was by no means going to believe. 

HOOGSTRATEN. <note>Jacob van Hoogstraten (c. 1460–1527), a Dominican inquisitor who was often a foil to Reuchlin in historical debates.</note> Our edition <note>Referring to the Latin Vulgate Bible.</note> has it differently in this place. For it says: "Because a work has been done in your days, which no one will believe when it is told." 

GALATINUS. The "Hebrew Truth" <term>Hebraica veritas</term> <note>A term used by scholars like Jerome and Reuchlin to refer to the original Hebrew text as the ultimate authority over translations.</note> which I myself have translated here, is far better than what the author of our edition translated. For whether this work is to be understood literally as referring to Nebuchadnezzar, or mystically as the incarnation of the Messiah—in any event, if we wish to respect the force of the words, neither our edition nor the Greek edition <note>The Septuagint.</note> (when it says: "No one will believe the truth") seems consistent. First, if it is understood to be about Nebuchadnezzar, all the Jews certainly believe it happened. Second, when it is explained as the incarnation of Christ, countless Gentiles and very many Jews have indeed believed. Therefore, our translation, by not following the sense of the Hebrew truth in this and by admitting this sort of difficulty—"No one," that is, "rarely anyone will believe"—forces us to interpret it figuratively. But the Hebrew letter admits no such difficulty in this; indeed (what is quite pleasing to us...

What is the meaning of "from my flesh"? He should have said "from my bone." Rather, "from my flesh" is meant literally. And what is this? <header>BOOK I</header>

<note>original: "דתנית ליה מינן אוליפנא..." This Hebrew/Aramaic passage is a quote from the Zohar regarding the covenant and the lineage of the Messiah.</note>
As we have learned from this: whoever guards this <term>covenant<note>The "covenant" refers to the "Sign of the Covenant" or circumcision, which Kabbalists viewed as a physical mark of spiritual purity.</note></term> maintains the kingdom that was granted to him. As it is written: *As the Lord lives, lie down until the morning,* <note>Ruth 3:13. In Jewish tradition, Boaz is praised for resisting temptation with Ruth until morning.</note> for he [Boaz] subdued his natural inclination through that oath and guarded this covenant. Because of this, he was worthy that there should come from him kings who rule over all other kings, and the King Messiah, who is called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He.

That is,

What does it mean, *From my flesh*? <note>Job 19:26: "And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet from my flesh shall I see God."</note> For it would have been more suitable to say, "From my substance." Nevertheless, he said, *From my own flesh.* This is what is written: *And the holy flesh shall pass from you.* <note>Jeremiah 11:15.</note> And furthermore it is written: *And my covenant shall be in your flesh.* <note>Genesis 17:13.</note> This signifies the sign that was given to us. For whenever a man is marked with this sign that proceeds from Him, he will see God himself, and his holy soul shall become one with Him. But when he does not keep this covenant, it is written of him: *By the breath of God they perish.* <note>Job 4:9.</note> If indeed this sign is of God and men do not observe it, they perish. But if you have been worthy of that sign and have guarded it, the divinity shall by no means depart from you; in time you shall be bound to holiness, and you shall ascend into the prepared place. 

But what is the reason for what we read above concerning the union of the holy soul—that is, of God—to man? It is certainly nothing else than that one male and one female shall be joined into one, which shall be called by one name, just as justice proceeds from the supernal mercy that rests upon them. In this word is the rest of the clarity or splendor of the male. And what is this mercy? I say it is the mercy which comes from the highest wisdom, and is crowned by the Word, and therefore is incorporated into the female. Indeed, it has been handed down to us in this way: God—behold, God the strong illuminator. The letter **י** <note>The Hebrew letter Yod, the first letter of the divine name Yahweh, representing the masculine principle or Wisdom.</note> is called masculine, and the letter **ה** <note>The Hebrew letter He, the second letter of the divine name, representing the feminine principle or Understanding.</note> is feminine; they are joined into one, which is called God <note>original: "Deus" (God), here referring to the name "Yah" (יה), composed of Yod and He.</note>. And His most holy soul is placed in this location, yet not bound within it. And for this reason it is written: *And from my flesh I shall see God.* 

Since this happiness is considered universal, it follows: *And from my flesh*, as if he were saying: "From this very flesh of my own." Because of this, those of the people of Israel who are holy shall be found worthy, for they shall say that this is God; they shall be worthy both in this world and in the world to come. And for the sake of this matter, it is written: *He who guards this covenant.* And from this we have learned that for him who guards this pact, God will guard him. But what is the proof of this? This is clear in the case of Boaz, who said to the Moabite woman: *As God lives, lie down until morning.* <note>Ruth 3:13. Galatinus emphasizes that Boaz’s self-control protected the "covenant in his flesh."</note> Even though he was enticed by lust, he nevertheless guarded this covenant. Therefore he deserved that from him should come forth Kings more powerful than all other Kings, and moreover the King Messiah, who is called by the name of the holy and blessed God. 

Thus far spoke that Rabbi Simeon ben Jochai. <note>Simeon bar Yochai (2nd century CE), the traditional author of the Zohar.</note> From his words, it is clearer than the midday sun that God himself was to be incarnated
