...for day and night, so that they may be in their proper time. This is the very covenant he made with Noah and his sons when He said in Genesis, chapter 8: *Day and night shall not cease.* <note>Genesis 8:22</note> Thus he spoke. Since, therefore, it is established that from the destruction of the second city of Jerusalem until now, more than 1,440 years have already passed <note>Based on the destruction of the Temple in 70 AD, this places the writing of this text around 1510 AD.</note>, during which they have never had a King from the house of David or of their own, nor a high priest, nor a lesser priest, nor a sacrifice, they certainly cannot show us by any true or even plausible reasoning that God fulfilled the words he had promised them through Jeremiah according to the letter. Consequently, it is necessary for them to concede that the Jewish promises made by God were conditional.

### That very few of the Jews were to be saved, while the rest were to be killed, destroyed, and scattered. Chapter 11.

->CAPNIO,<-

**A**nd if, from what you have said, it is easily apparent that the promise made to the Jews by God regarding their salvation in the time of the Messiah was conditional—namely, if they were to receive the Messiah himself and obey him. Therefore, if the greatest part of them, through the coming and passion of Christ, was not only not saved spiritually, but even lost and scattered temporally, it ought to seem not at all strange, since they neither received nor wished to hear the true Messiah himself, but rather killed him by a most shameful death. Yet, so that their <term>perfidy</term> <note>From the Latin *perfidia*, meaning faithlessness; in this period, it was a standard theological term for the rejection of the Christian faith.</note> may be more fully convicted, you would do a thing very much suited to our purpose if you proved from their own writings that not all Jews, but only a very few, were to be saved through the Messiah. **GAL.** This is clearly demonstrated first through their own tradition, which is placed in the book *Sanhedrin* at the end of the chapter *Helec* <note>The eleventh chapter of the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, which deals with the world to come.</note>. There it is read word for word: Rabbi Shammai <note>original: שמאי</note> said, it is stated in Jeremiah, chapter 3: *And I will take you, one from a city, and two from a family.* <note>original Hebrew: ולקחתי אתכם אחד מעיר ושנים ממשפחה</note> And again it is said: *And I will bring you to Zion.* <note>original Hebrew: ואביא אתכם ציון</note> Therefore, their departure from Egypt was measured against their entry into the land. Just as their entrance into the land consisted of two out of six hundred thousand. Where the <term>gloss</term> <note>An explanatory commentary, likely referring here to Rashi (Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac).</note> of Rabbi Solomon says: "The rest (he says) died during the three days of darkness." Rabbi Akiba said: "And so it shall be in the days of the Messiah." Just as it is said in the first chapter of Hosea: *And she shall respond there,* or *she shall sing there, as in the days of her youth, or her childhood, and as in the days of her ascent from the land of Egypt.* <note>original Hebrew: וענתה שמה כימי נעוריה וביום עלותה מארץ מצרים</note> This is the tradition. From which it is clearly held that, just as out of the six hundred thousand Jews who had departed from Egypt, none entered into the promised land except for only two, Joshua and Caleb; so too in the days of the Messiah (as the tradition proves through the prophet Hosea) there were to be only two of the Jews out of...

<summary>Galatinus argues that God's promises to the Jews were conditional on their acceptance of the Messiah, citing the 1,440-year lack of a Jewish king or priest as proof. He further cites the Talmud to argue that only a small remnant of the Jewish people was ever destined to be saved by the Messiah, paralleling the few who survived the Exodus.</summary>

### BOOK NINE

...out of six hundred thousand to be saved, as if one from a city and two from a family <note>original: "cognatione"; referring to Jeremiah 3:14</note> (as had been prophesied through Jeremiah) were to be taken, while all the rest were to be utterly destroyed and scattered. Nor does the aforementioned destruction of the Jews, which occurred in the days of Christ, detract from him in any way; rather, it provides a powerful testimony to him for all who are not ignorant of the truth, seeing how the ancient fathers of the Jews (by the testimony of their own Talmud) understood the words of the prophets.

<margin>Tradition of the sons of Rabbi Hiya</margin>
For it is read in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter that begins with **Dine mammonoth** <note>Hebrew: דיני ממונות; "Laws concerning money" or "Monetary Judgments"</note>, that the sons of Rabbi Hiya sat before "Rabbi" <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, the primary redactor of the Mishnah</note> at a banquet. Since they were unwilling to speak anything of the secrets of the Holy Scripture which they had received from their father, Rabbi said to the servant: "Give them more wine, so that they will speak." When this had been done, one of them opened his mouth and said: "The Son of David shall not come until the two 'houses of the fathers' in Israel have failed—these being the Head of the Captivity, which was in Babylon, and the **Nasi** <note>Hebrew: נשיא; "Prince" or "President"</note>, who is the Prince in the land of Israel." *And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offense to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. The author provides the Latin: "Et erit ad sanctificationem... ad lapidem offensionis..."</note>

When the wine enters, the secret comes out." <note>This is a famous play on Gematria, the Jewish system of numerology. The Hebrew word for 'wine' (Yayin) and the word for 'secret' (Sod) both have a numerical value of 70.</note>

This is the tradition. Furthermore, Rabbi Kimhi <note>David Kimhi, a famous 12th-13th century grammarian and commentator known as Radak</note>, explaining that passage of Isaiah, *And he shall be for a sanctuary*, says: "This means: He will be a place to which a man goes so that he may be saved in it." There are also those who explain *He shall be for a sanctuary* as "for a preparation"—as if to say, for the preparation of vengeance, according to what is said in Jeremiah chapter 12: *Sanctify them for the day of slaughter.* <note>Jeremiah 12:3</note> Thus says Rabbi Kimhi. Regarding this tradition, then, it must first be noted that those words of Isaiah, *And he shall be for a sanctuary*, along with the rest, are spoken concerning the Messiah. Second, regarding the truth of this matter and the meaning of the verse that precedes these words—namely: *Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself*—the Chaldean translation <note>The Targum, an Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note> of Rabbi Jonathan says: *And let him be your fear, and let him be your strength. And he shall be for a sanctuary,* and so forth. From this it follows necessarily that the Messiah is not only a man, but also God. Third, it must be noted above all that the Messiah was intended to be a sanctuary and a preparation not for all, but for some of the Jews—that is, only for those believing in him and obeying him—so that he might make them holy and prepared...

### That the Jews who were not to receive the Messiah were destined to lose the understanding of the Scriptures, remaining like fools and asses without sense.
### Chapter III.
### CAPNIO.

Regarding what you have already said in the preceding remarks—namely, that the grace of understanding the scripture was to be taken away from the Jews and conferred upon the disciples of the Messiah—I would like you to show this from their own writings. And especially, I would like you to prove that those who were not to receive the Messiah would necessarily lose the understanding of the scriptures entirely. **GAL.** This is clearly held, first of all, in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helec* <note>original: "Helec," referring to Perek Helek, the eleventh chapter of the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, which discusses the afterlife and the Messianic era</note>, where it is read as follows: Rabbi Judah said, "In the generation in which the Son of David <note>A common title for the Messiah</note> is to come, the house of preaching will be turned toward fornication." <gloss>Gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Referring to Rashi, the famous 11th-century commentator</note>: that is, the place where the wise masters taught the law.</gloss> "And the men of Gazith" <gloss>Gloss of Rabbi Solomon: that is, the Sanhedrin, which is the 70 ordinary Judges</gloss> "shall wander from city to city, and no one will have mercy on them. And the wisdom of the scribes shall rot, and those who fear to sin will be rejected. And the face of that generation will be like a dog" <gloss>Gloss of Rabbi Solomon: literally, they will be as impudent as dogs</gloss> "and truth will be diminished." Also, in the book *Siphre* <note>An ancient Jewish legal commentary on the books of Numbers and Deuteronomy</note>, that saying from Deuteronomy chapter 32 is explained in this way:
<margin>A crooked and perverse generation: Do you thus requite the LORD, O foolish and unwise people? <note>Deuteronomy 32:5–6</note></margin>
That is: "A wicked and perverse generation, will you thus repay God, O foolish and unwise people?" He calls them "foolish people" specifically regarding the things that have already happened. And he calls them "not wise" regarding the things that will happen in the "world to come." And this is what is said in Isaiah chapter 1:
<margin>Israel does not know, my people do not understand. <note>Isaiah 1:3</note></margin>
That is: "Israel did not know, my people did not understand." Israel did not know the things that have passed. My people did not understand concerning the world to come. What did Israel deserve, that they should be made foolish and hardened in heart? It was because they were not wise in the words of the law. And so Job himself says in chapter 4:
<margin>Is not their cord plucked up within them? They die, and not in wisdom. <note>Job 4:21</note></margin>
That is: "Has not their cord departed with them? They shall die, and not in knowledge or wisdom." Thus far the tradition. Since, therefore, the "world to come" or "future world" in the Talmud almost always refers to the time of the Messiah, it is quite clearly held according to the aforementioned tradition that the Jews were made foolish because they were not wise, nor did they understand the words of the law in which the Messiah is clearly shown, so that they might receive him. Their "cord," moreover, departed from them at that time when, by denying the Messiah, God their Savior, they rushed headlong into the whirlpool of the Roman Empire in this world, and into the pit of hell in the future. They are like one who lets himself down from a height by a rope; when the rope breaks, he falls with it into the precipice. This is according to that prophecy of Isaiah in the 5th chapter, which says:
<margin>Therefore my people have gone into captivity for lack of knowledge; and their honorable men are famished, and their multitude parched with thirst. Therefore the grave has enlarged its soul and opened its mouth without limit; and her glory, and her multitude, and her pomp, and he who rejoices in her, shall descend into it. <note>Isaiah 5:13–14</note></margin>
That is: "Because of this my people are led captive, because they were without knowledge, and their honorable men died of hunger, and their common people were parched with thirst. For this reason [the grave] has enlarged...

For they enlarged themselves to swallow excessive food and drink, and they opened their mouths to deny God their savior; as it is said in Jeremiah, chapter 5: "They have denied the Lord, and said, He is not." <note>Jeremiah 5:12</note> Also in the book *Hagigah* <note>original: חגיגה, a Talmudic tractate concerning festival offerings</note>, that is, of the *Solemnity*, in the chapter that begins *Hakol Chayavin* <note>original: הכל חייבין, meaning "All are bound" or "All are obligated"</note>, it is read in this manner: It is written in Jeremiah, chapter 49: "Counsel has perished from the children, their wisdom is become foul." <note>original: אבדה עצה מבנים נסרחה חכמתם; Jeremiah 49:7</note> When did counsel perish from the children, and when did their wisdom become foul? When the wise men of the world were present. For the devil (by God's permission) infatuated the Jews, and took away from them the sense required for the understanding of the truth. And indeed, to such an extent that in the divine scriptures they are of less understanding than asses. This they themselves are compelled to confess. For in the book *Shekalim* <note>original: שקלים, a Talmudic tractate concerning the half-shekel tax</note>, that is, of *Weights*, in the chapter that begins *Ve-ellu hen* <note>original: ואלו הן, meaning "And these are they"</note>, it is read thus word-for-word: Rabbi Haggai said, "The predecessors plowed, and sowed, and hoed, and reaped, and made threshing floors, and threshed, and winnowed, and ground, and set before us bread"—that is, the doctrine of the scripture—"And we do not even have a mouth to eat it." Rabbi Abba said, "If the ancients were sons of men, we are asses." Rabbi Menahem said in that hour, "We are not even to be compared to the she-asses of Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair." All this is in the Talmud. There is yet another testimony of this in the book *Shabbat* <note>original: שבת</note>, that is, of the *Sabbath*. Where it is said thus to the letter: Rabbi Zera said, that Rabbi [Judah] said, "If the predecessors were sons of men, we are asses. And we are not even such as the ass of Rabbi Hanina, or like the ass of Rabbi Menahem, but like other ordinary asses." <note>This is a common Talmudic expression of humility regarding the greatness of past generations, which Galatinus here interprets literally to prove Jewish "stupidity"</note> From these things, although all Jews who have not received Christ are proven to be asses, it is established that those who draw others into the pit by false dogma are even worse than asses. Jeremiah calls these men "shepherds," and he names their "ass-like" nature "beastliness," saying in chapter 10: "Because the shepherds have become like beasts, and have not sought the Lord: therefore they have not understood, and all their flock is broken and scattered." <note>original: בערו הרועים ואת יהוה לא דרשו : על כן לא השכילו וכל מרעיתם נפוצה; Jeremiah 10:21</note> Again in chapter 50 he says: "My people have been lost sheep; their shepherds have caused them to go astray." <note>original: אבדות חיה עמי רעיהם התעום; Jeremiah 50:6</note> These are certainly the shepherds of the Jews, namely their masters and teachers; and if in the past they made them go astray many times, today they make them go astray most of all. Wherefore the Savior, speaking of them in the 15th chapter of Matthew, aptly said: "They are blind, and leaders of the blind. If the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit." <note>Matthew 15:14</note>

# BOOK NINE

### Chapter IV. On the perpetual rejection of the Jews, and that they were to be expelled from the house of God as enemies of God.

->CAPNIO,<-
<note>Capnio is the scholar-protagonist of this dialogue, representing the historical figure Johannes Reuchlin.</note>

They assert from their own scriptures that because God cast the Jews out from His house as rebels and enemies against Him, and rejected them forever, these things were destined to happen to them for their own confusion. This is most clearly shown by the testimony of *Hosea*, specifically in chapter 9, in the person of God saying: <note>original: על רע מעלליהם מביתי אגרשם לא אוסיף אהבתם</note> "Because of the wickedness of their deeds, I will drive them out of my house; I will love them no more." <note>Hosea 9:15</note> This is what Rabbi *Jonathan* <note>Referring to Jonathan ben Uzziel, the purported author of the Aramaic Targum</note> interpreted in the Chaldean language <note>term: Chaldean refers to Aramaic</note> as: <note>original: על בישת עובדיהון מבית מקדשי אתרכינון לא אוסיף לרחמא עליהון</note> "Because of the wickedness of their works, I will drive them out from my holy house, nor will I add to show mercy upon them." Concerning this, the prophet *Amos* also says in chapter 5: <note>original: נפלה לא תוסיף קום בתולת ישראל</note> "The virgin of *Israel* has fallen, she shall no more rise." <note>Amos 5:2</note>

<margin>An objection by the Jews. The response.</margin>
CAP. What if the Jews should say that these things were spoken only concerning the ten tribes? <note>Referring to the Northern Kingdom of Israel, which was exiled earlier than the Southern Kingdom of Judah.</note> GAL. Let it be said to them: If that were so, God would by no means have said through *Hosea*, "I will drive them out of my house," since the ten tribes were neither in the house of God, nor did they care for the house of God. This was more expressly foretold in *Jeremiah*, chapter 7, speaking thus: <note>original: והשלכתי אתכם מעל פני כאשר השלכתי את כל אחיכם את כל זרע אפרים</note> "I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brothers, all the seed of *Ephraim*." <note>Jeremiah 7:15</note> Where by *Ephraim*, the ten tribes are understood, because their King *Jeroboam* was from the tribe of *Ephraim*. This is also clearly shown in *Midrash Tehillim* <note>term: Midrash Tehillim is a traditional rabbinic commentary on the Book of Psalms</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Psalms, when commenting on that which is said in Psalm 76: <note>original: נודע ביהודה אלהים בישראל גדול שמו</note> "In Judea God was known; his name is great in *Israel*." <note>Psalm 76:1</note> Thus it is said: In the hour when God, holy and blessed, performs mercy with *Judah*, it is just as if He performs mercy with all *Israel*. For indeed, all *Israel* is called by the name of *Judah*. For *Israel* is called by four names, namely *Jacob*, *Israel*, *Ephraim*, and *Judah*. Concerning this rejection, *Amos* himself said in chapter 6: <note>original: נשבע אדני יהוה בנפשו נאם יהוה אלהי צבאות מתאב אנכי את גאון יעקב וארמנותיו שנאתי והסגרתי עיר ומלואה</note> "The Lord God has sworn by His soul, says the Lord God of hosts. I loathe the pride of *Jacob*, and I hate his palaces; and I have delivered up the city and its fullness." <note>Amos 6:8</note> Which Rabbi *Jonathan* translates into the Chaldean thus: <note>original: קיים יהוה במימריה אמר יהוה אלהי צבאות מנבל אנא ית בית מקדשא רבותיה דיעקב</note> "The Lord God has established in His word, or by His word. The Lord God of hosts said: I abhor the house of the sanctuary, which is the pride of *Jacob*." Moreover, the gloss of Rabbi *Solomon* <note>Selomo refers to Rashi, the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator</note> says: "I have delivered up the city and its fullness," that is, *Jerusalem* and its inhabitants. The house of the sanctuary was also called pride, according to that which was said in *Ezekiel* chapter 24: <note>original: הנני מחלל את מקדשי גאון עוזכם</note> "Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength..." <note>Ezekiel 24:21</note>

<summary>In this chapter, Galatinus argues that the Jewish people were permanently rejected by God, citing prophecies from Hosea, Amos, and Jeremiah alongside Rabbinic commentaries to prove their expulsion from the 'house of God'. He addresses the counter-argument that these prophecies applied only to the ten northern tribes, asserting instead that they apply to all Israel, including Judah.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the argument regarding the spiritual state of the Jewish people. Having previously discussed their loss of wisdom and understanding as divine punishment, the dialogue now explores the metaphor of the "shattered jar" to explain why their rejection is seen as permanent and why they are unlikely to return to their former status as long as they remain in their current state of belief.</meta>

# BOOK NINE

...I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength. <note>original: "phanabo sanctuarium meum, elationem fortitudinis uestrae"</note> Rabbi Solomon <note>H. Selomo refers to Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> also agrees.

**CAP.** Why is this rejection of the Jews so often <margin>Why the rejection of the Jews is called a "crushing."</margin> called a "crushing" <note>term: contritio; literally a grinding down or shattering into small pieces</note> in the Holy Scriptures, and why is it compared, rather unsuitably it seems, to a potter’s jar being smashed to bits?

**GAL.** Because their oppression in this captivity was to be so great that it could deservedly be compared to a "crushing" from which not even a single shard remains. For every break in a vessel can be soldered together and returned to some useful work. But if the shards of a vessel are smashed by a violent crushing, its parts are good for nothing except to be thrown away. And the longer a shattered jar lasts, the more the fracture always increases. Therefore, since their rejection is compared to this kind of crushing of shards—which are of no further use except to be cast out—it should be understood that in this captivity, they were to fall into such <unclear>destruction</unclear> that as long as they remain in their perfidy <note>term: perfidia; in this context, it refers to the historical Christian view of Jewish "unfaithfulness" or refusal to accept the Gospel</note>, they can never return to their former liberty. According to what is said by the Psalm-writer in Psalm 2:

<margin><unclear>The same [is said]...</unclear></margin> <note>original: תרעם בשבט ברזל ככלי יוצר תנפצם</note> "You shall break them with a rod of iron; you shall dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel." <note>Psalm 2:9</note>

That is, you will shatter them with an iron rod and cast them away like a potter’s vessel. From these things that have been said, it is manifest that the Jews, on account of the malice of their works, were deservedly to be cast out from their house by God himself, and were never to be loved by Him so long as they remained in the malice of their perfidy. Foreseeing this, Jeremiah, at the end of his Lamentations, asked the cause, saying:

<note>original: למה תשכחנו</note> "Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us for so long a time?" <note>Lamentations 5:20</note>

To which the Lord responded in the 8th chapter of the same prophet, saying:

<note>original: אליהם כה אמר יהוה היפלו ולא יקומו אם ישוב לא ישוב : מדוע שובבה העם הזה ירושלם משבה נצחת החזיקו בתרמת תשוב : הקשבתי ואשמע לוא כן ידברו אין איש נחם על רעתו לאמר מה עשיתי : כלהשב במרוצתם כסוס שוטף במלחמה : גם חסידה בשמים ידעה מועדיה ותור וסוס ועגור שמרו את עת באנה ועמי לא ידעו את משפט יהוה :</note> "You shall say to them: Thus says God: Shall they fall and not rise again? Shall they turn away and not return? Why then is this people of Jerusalem turned back with a persistent, or eternal, backsliding? They hold fast to deceit, and they refuse to return. I listened and heard, but they do not speak what is right; no man repents of his malice, saying, 'What have I done?' Everyone turns to his own course, like a horse rushing into battle. Even the stork in the heavens knows her appointed times; and the turtledove, the swift, and the crane observe the time of their coming. But my people do not know the judgment of God." <note>Jeremiah 8:4-7</note> From these things, the proposal is clear.

**GAL.** This is best demonstrated by what is found among them in the book <term>Yevamot</term> <note>original: יבמות; a tractate of the Talmud dealing with levirate marriage</note>, that is, *Of the Sisters-in-Law*, in the chapter that begins <term>Ha-aretz</term> <note>original: הארץ; meaning "The Land"</note>, that is, *The Earth*. For there was a first and a second possession for them, but there will not be a third. Rabbi Johanan said: Who was the author of <term>Seder Olam</term>, that is, the book of the *Order of the World*? Rabbi Yose. This is the tradition. 

This same point is also held in the same book, *Seder Olam*, in this manner: It is written in Deuteronomy chapter 30: "And the Lord your God will lead you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it." Could it be possible that there will be a third possession in the future? [The book] teaches what should be said to this by the phrase: "Which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it." For they were to have a first and a second possession, but there will not be a third possession for them. This is the tradition. 

Therefore, since the Jews were only to possess their former land twice, as is clearly evident from these traditions—and they have already possessed it twice in the past—it follows that they will not possess it again. For they possessed it the first time from the time of Joshua until the destruction of the first Temple; and the second time from the times of Zerubbabel and Ezra until the burning of the last Temple, or until the times of Hadrian Caesar, as is evident in many ways from their own scriptures. And since they are by no means to possess it a third time (as the aforementioned traditions attest), they themselves must necessarily concede that they will never possess their land again, and consequently, will never return to it. 

Therefore, whatever they object against us concerning their return to Jerusalem, the rebuilding of the Temple, and a third possession of that land, is entirely false and completely inconsistent with their own ancient scriptures. ### That the Jews were to be without a Prince, without sacrifice, and without God until the end of the world. Chapter VI.

->REUCHLIN,<-

I would wish that you would demonstrate through their own scriptures what you stated last: namely, that the Jews are destined to be without a Prince, without sacrifice, and without God until the end of the world. **GAL.** This is best proved by the statement in the third chapter of Hosea: <note>original: "כי רבים יושבו בני ישראל ימים רבים אין מלך ואין שר ואין זבח ואין מצבה ואין אפוד ותרפים"; Hosea 3:4</note> which is: "For the children of Israel shall dwell many days without a King, and without a Prince, and without sacrifice, and without an altar, and without an ephod <note>A ceremonial vestment worn by the High Priest</note> (that is, without the priestly ornament), and without images." Furthermore, Rabbi Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the purported author of the Targum (Aramaic translation) of the Prophets</note> translates this into Aramaic as follows: <note>original Aramaic: "ארי יומין סגיאין יתבו בני ישראל לית מלכא מדבית דוד ולית דיעביד שולטן בישראל ולית דבחה לרעוא בירושלם ולית קמתא בטומרון ולית אפוד ומחוי"</note> That is: "For many days the children of Israel shall remain, during which they will not have a King from the house of David, nor one exercising power over Israel, nor an acceptable sacrifice or one pleasing in Jerusalem, nor an altar in Samaria, nor an ephod that makes pronouncements." Therefore, just as the Jews were not to have a King from the house of David, nor any Prince among them, nor sacrifice, nor altar; it is also proved by the remaining points placed here that they were to have neither priest, nor law, nor even God, through that which is written in 2 Chronicles chapter 15: <note>original: "וימים רבים לישראל ללא אלהי אמת וללא כהן מורה וללא תורה"; 2 Chronicles 15:3</note> That is: "And many days shall be for Israel without the true God, or the God of truth, and without a teaching priest, and without law." Where I have translated "without the God of truth," the Hebrews deceitfully interpret this as "without judges of truth," because it is written <term>Elohe emeth</term> <note>original: אלהי אמת; literally "God of truth"</note>, which they say applies more equitably to God and to judges. But it is proved that they interpret this poorly and falsely chiefly from this: although the name <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: אלהים</note> is sometimes found in the sacred letters to signify "judges," yet in its primary meaning it signifies God, and it is in the plural on account of the Trinity of divine persons. For which reason it must be said to signify God here rather than judges. Especially since the ancient Talmudists accept that passage as referring to the true God. This is found in the book <term>Avodah Zarah</term> <note>original: עבודת זרה; meaning "Foreign Worship" or "Idolatry"</note>, in the chapter that begins <term>Lifnei Eideihen</term> <note>original: לפני איריהן; "Before their festivals"</note>. It reads thus, word-for-word: Rabbi Hanina said to Rabbi Elazar: "Blessed are you, who have exercised yourself in the law and in works of mercy. And woe to me, who exercised myself in the law alone." Since, as Rabbi Hunna said, whoever studies or exercises himself in the law only, is like one who has no God. As it is written in the fifteenth chapter of the second book of Chronicles: "Many days for Israel without the true God, and without a priest, and without law." And what does "without law" mean? Rabbi Hunna said: "Anyone studying in the law only, and [not] in works of mercy..."

### REUCHLIN

**A**lthough in the preceding sections you have sufficiently and abundantly proven that only a few of the Jews were to be saved at the time of the Messiah, while the rest were to be lost and scattered; you nevertheless assert that those who received our Redeemer as the true Messiah were both saved and, with their name changed, were called <term>Messihim</term> <note>original Hebrew: משיחים; literally "Messianics," here meaning "Christians"</note>, that is, Christians. Therefore, to more fully convict them of their own obstinacy, you ought to prove through their own scriptures that this division into unbelieving Jews and true Christians was destined to occur at the time of the Messiah.

# BOOK NINE

Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Judah, speaking of the ten tribes, reported that Israel did not go into captivity until they had all become <term>mamzerim</term> <note>original: ממזרים; meaning children of forbidden or illegitimate unions</note>, that is, spurious. Rabbi Johanan also said that Israel was not led into captivity until twenty-four sects of <term>minim</term> <note>original: מינים; a term used in Rabbinic literature to denote heretics or sectarians</note>, that is, heretics, had emerged from them. Hence it is written in the second chapter of Ezekiel: <note>original Hebrew: בן אדם שלח אני אותך אל בני ישראל אל גוים המורדים אשר מרדו בי המה ואבותם פשעו בי עד עצם היום הזה</note> "Son of man, I send you to the children of Israel, to the <term>Goim hamordim</term> <note>original: גוים המורדים; literally 'rebellious nations'</note>, that is, to the apostate gentiles who have rebelled against me; they and their fathers have been guilty against me even unto this very day." This is the tradition. Therefore, the Lord rightly said: "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel." Furthermore, regarding what was said in the previous tradition—namely, that Israel became <term>mamzerim</term>, or spurious—the following from the ninth chapter of Zechariah pertains: <note>original Hebrew: וישב ממזר באשדוד</note> This means, "And a <term>mamzer</term>, that is, a spurious one, shall sit or dwell in Ashdod." Rabbi Jonathan son of Uzziel, in his Chaldaic edition <note>referring to the Targum, an Aramaic translation and exposition of the Hebrew Bible</note>, shows that this is to be understood regarding Israel, saying: <note>original Aramaic: ויתיבו בית ישראל באשדוד</note> "And the house of Israel shall dwell in Ashdod." To this also pertains what is written in the book <term>Iebamoth</term> <note>Yebamot, a tractate of the Talmud dealing with levirate marriage</note>, that is, "Of the Sisters-in-law," in the chapter beginning <term>Nassim</term> <note>Nashim, meaning 'Women'</note>, in this manner: It is a tradition that the daughters—that is, the women—of those ten tribes of that generation were "castrated" <note>likely meaning spiritually or legally cut off from the assembly</note>. Nor were they moved from their own holy land until <term>Sennacherib</term> <note>The King of Assyria who conquered the northern kingdom of Israel</note> made them into perfect gentiles. Just as it is said in the fifth chapter of Hosea: <note>original Hebrew: ביהוה בגרו כי בנים זרים ילדו</note> That is, "They have dealt treacherously or deceitfully against God, for they have begotten strange children." However, there was no other cause for this division of the Hebrews and the rejection of the greater part of them—namely, the ten tribes—except that they first refused to have a part in David. For they said, as is read in 1 Kings 12: <note>original Hebrew: אין לנו חלק בדוד ולא נחלה לנו בבן ישי</note> "We have no portion in David, nor any inheritance in the son of Jesse." And also because they took up false gods in the form of two calves, as has been said. Therefore, just as in the time of Jeroboam the Hebrews were divided into "Israel" and "Jews" <note>referring to the Northern Kingdom vs. the Southern Kingdom of Judah</note>, so in the seventieth week of Daniel, the Jews themselves were divided into the faithless Jews and the true Christians. And just as then the greater part of the Hebrews—the ten tribes—said, "We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse," so in the time of the Messiah the greater part of the Jews said, "We have no king but Caesar," rejecting the Lord Jesus, the true Messiah prefigured in David. And just as those people, having rejected David, then worshiped false gods in the form of two calves, so these, having rejected the true Messiah, established for themselves two false messiahs, one after the other (as their own scriptures testify, and as has been discussed at great length previously). Again, just as those people, because of these and other things (as sacred history a little above attests), were both rejected by God and taken captive by Sennacherib; so also these, because they spat upon the true Messiah, the Lord Jesus, and received two false messiahs, were rejected by God forever and taken captive by the Roman princes <term>Vespasian and Titus</term>. And this is what the Lord says to them through the seventh chapter of Jeremiah...

But a very small part, clinging to Christ and following Him in faith and work, has embraced the truth. 

Furthermore, just as then the servants of God who followed the truth were named differently than before—for they were no longer called Hebrews, but were henceforth called Jews by a change of name—so now the servants of God, following the truth of the Christian faith, are called differently than they were previously named. For their name is used in an oath of [damnation]. For when they swear, they say negatively: "If I am not a Jew, I will do this." Or affirmatively: "May I be a Jew if I have done this." And the Lord God will slay them, as the prophet says, until the end of the world, as has been clear in preceding chapters and will be even more widely evident in those following. 

Finally, just as there was always a struggle between the Jews and their brothers, Israel; so also between the [Jews] and Christians, both in customs and in faith, conflict has never been lacking. For just as it was not enough for them to have abandoned God and the house of David, and to have worshiped one calf in Bethel and another in Dan as gods, but adding sins to sins, they also worshiped Baal; so it was not enough for these people to have rejected and killed the Messiah, and to have made for themselves one false Messiah in Jerusalem called <term>Bencozba</term> <note>original: Bencozba; referring to Simon bar Kokhba, leader of the second-century Jewish revolt, whose name was punned by his critics as 'Son of a Lie'</note>, that is, "son of a lie" or "son of falsehood," and to have made for themselves another Messiah of the same name [elsewhere]. Instead, fulfilling the measure of their fathers and piling errors upon errors, they still wait for a third for themselves. This is despite the fact that their fathers were so shamefully deceived in those two previous Messiahs (as their own scriptures testify, and they themselves by no means deny), and though their Masters assign various dates for the third one whom they still expect, all of them have at last been found to be speakers of lies, as has been abundantly shown above.

That these things were predicted concerning the destruction of the Jews which was to come by the Romans is clear through their own commentators. ...they did to the prophet Jeremiah, whom they cast into a pit so that he might die. To him also the Lord said (as it is written in Jeremiah 39): "Rescuing, I will rescue you, and you shall not fall by the sword, and your life shall be to you as a prize of war. Because you have trusted, or because you have hoped in me, says the Lord." <note>This refers to the rescue of Jeremiah and Ebed-Melech during the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians.</note> There was also there the house or family of the Rechabites, concerning whom it is said in the same prophet: "Go to the house of the Rechabites, and speak to them." And a little later: "There shall not fail a man of Jonadab the son of Rechab to stand before me forever." <note>The Rechabites were a group known for their strict adherence to their ancestor’s commands, often cited as a model of faithfulness.</note> Furthermore, at that time there was Jeremiah the prophet, and many other righteous and holy people who moved into Babylon during the exile. If, therefore, so many righteous people were in Jerusalem at the time of the destruction of the first temple, it is surely clear—judging by the conclusion of the aforementioned tradition, which says no righteous person was found in Jerusalem—that the beginning of the above-mentioned words of Jeremiah (which include: "Go about the streets of Jerusalem," with the rest) does not speak of the first destruction of that city, which was carried out by Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylon, but of the final one, which was to be carried out by the Roman Princes Vespasian and Titus.

The cause for which God destroyed the Jews through the Romans and overturned their house is shown when it is said in the same place: "For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, says God." What and of what kind this treachery was is clearly suggested when it immediately follows: "They have denied God and said, 'It is not he.'" Since, therefore, after the return from the Babylonian captivity, the Jews never denied God in word or deed through idolatry or any other false worship, it necessarily follows that they denied Him then—saying the Lord "is not he"—when they repudiated the Lord Jesus Christ, the true God and Son of God, and said that He was not the Messiah. Instead, they established for themselves two false Messiahs, one after the other. <note>This likely refers to figures like Bar Kokhba, whom some recognized as a messiah during the second century CE.</note> Therefore, in the same chapter of the same prophecy it is said:

על כן הכם אריה מיער זאב ערבות ישדדם נמר שקד על עריהם כל היוצא מהנה יטרף 
<note>original: "Therefore a lion from the forest shall strike them down, a wolf of the deserts [or evenings] shall devastate them, a leopard is watching over their cities; everyone who goes out from them shall be torn in pieces." (Jeremiah 5:6)</note>

That is: "A lion from the forest has struck them, a wolf of the desert (or of the evening) will lay them waste, a leopard watching over their cities. Everyone going out from them will be preyed upon." The commentary of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note> explains this as follows: "A lion from the forest struck them" refers to the Kingdom of Babylon; "a wolf of the desert (or of the evening) will lay them waste" refers to the Kingdom of the Medes; "a leopard watching over their cities" refers to the Kingdom of the Greeks; "everyone going out from them will be preyed upon" refers to Edom, that is, through the Kingdom of the Romans. 

Thus says Rabbi Solomon. By this interpretation it clearly appears that in the place where it is said in the words of Jeremiah, "Everyone going out from them will be preyed upon" by Edom—that is, by the Romans—all the things that follow must be understood as concerning the destruction carried out by the Romans. For there the other words are these: "Take away the branches, for they are not the Lord's. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, says God. They have denied God and said, 'It is not he.'" But the vine from which these branches or offshoots (which were not of God) were to be taken away was the entire house of Israel itself, according to what is said in Hosea 10: 

גפן בוקק ישראל 
<note>original: "Israel is a luxuriant [or empty] vine."</note> 

...that is, "Israel is a leafy vine." From all of which it is clearly evident that for this reason the Jews were to be destroyed by the Romans: because they were going to betray and deny God. Although there was also another cause for their ruin and eternal damnation: namely, that they were unwilling to receive the law of the Messiah.

But they said to him: "It is not our custom for a caravan to stay in an inn at night." After they had departed, the dead of night and darkness fell upon them. Returning, they asked the host to open the inn for them. But he said to them: "It is not the custom of the host to open the inn at night, because he does not admit a man during the night hours. At the time when I sought to receive you into the inn, you did not want it; now that you seek it, I do not want to admit you." So said the Holy One, blessed be He: "Seek the Lord while He may be found. Return, O backsliding children." And there was no one who would seek or return. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: "I will go and return to my first place." But after they were handed over to the Kingdoms—which are compared to wild animals—and they began to cry out: "Why, O Lord, do you stand afar off?"

...ascend to the number of <term>Berith</term> <note>Hebrew: ברית, meaning "covenant" or "pact."</note>, that is, of the pact or covenant. And you will understand the secret of that text written in Deuteronomy, chapter 31: <note>Original Hebrew: הנך שכב עם אבותיך וקם העם הזה וזנה אחרי אלהי נכר הארץ אשר הוא בא שמה בקרבו ועזבני והפר את בריתי אשר כרתי אתו</note> This is: "Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and this people shall rise up and go whoring after the foreign gods of the land into which they are entering to dwell; and they will forsake me and break my covenant which I have made with them." Rabbi Nehumias, who preceded the coming of our Redeemer by nearly fifty years, spoke these things.

For the explanation of these words, it must be noted that this Hebrew word **Berith**, which signifies a pact or covenant, contains the number 612 by arithmetic calculation <note>This refers to the practice of **Gematria**, where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values to find hidden meanings between words with the same total.</note> among the Hebrews. For it is written with four letters, each of which carries a certain number among them. For <term>Beth</term> (ב) signifies two, <term>Resh</term> (ר) 200, <term>Yod</term> (י) 10, and <term>Tav</term> (ת) 400. Therefore, **Berith**, which is composed of these, contains 612.

The names of the mother of the Messiah and her son also contain this same number (as is shown elsewhere). For the name of the mother of the Messiah (as shown in the preceding pages by the same <term>Rabbenu Haccados</term> <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince.</note>) was to be **Miriam** (מרים), that is, Maria. The name of her son, the Messiah, by which he was to be called by the Gentiles who would accept his faith, was to be **Jesu** (ישו) <note>This is a common historical spelling of Jesus' name in Hebrew polemics and mystical texts, lacking the final 'ayin' found in *Yeshua*.</note>, that is, Jesus. As the same Rabbenu Haccados previously showed. 

These names, namely **Miriam and Jesu** (מרים ו ישו)—that is, Mary and Jesus—also contain 612 by arithmetic calculation among the Hebrews. For <term>Mem</term> (מ) signifies 40, <term>Resh</term> (ר) 200, <term>Yod</term> (י) 10, <term>Mem</term> (מ) 40, <term>Vav</term> (ו) <note>Meaning "and."</note> 6, <term>Yod</term> (י) 10, <term>Shin</term> (ש) 300, and <term>Vav</term> (ו) 6. And so the names of the mother of the Messiah and her son, which are Mary and Jesus, contain the same number as the word **Berith** itself, namely 612. 

The words introduced from the aforementioned text of Deuteronomy by Rabbi Nehumias himself also carry this same number: **Elohe nechar ha-aretz** (אלהי נכר הארץ), that is, "the foreign gods of the land." For <term>Aleph</term> (א) signifies one, <term>Lamed</term> (ל) 30, <term>He</term> (ה) 5, <term>Yod</term> (י) 10, <term>Nun</term> (נ) 50, <term>Kaph</term> (כ) 20, <term>Resh</term> (ר) 200, <term>He</term> (ה) 5, <term>Aleph</term> (א) 1, <term>Resh</term> (ר) 200, and <term>Tzadi</term> (צ) 90. All of these added together make 612. 

From these things, therefore, the previously mentioned words of Rabbi Nehumias are evident: "When you know the name of this rock, that is, of the mother of the Messiah, which is Mary, and the name of her son, that is, the Messiah himself, which is Jesus, both rising by arithmetic calculation to the number of the covenant (**Berith**), which is 612—then you will understand the secret of that text: 'Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers,' and the rest." Therefore, it was a very great secret that the Lord revealed to Moses in Deuteronomy chapter 31, saying: "Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and the people rising up will go whoring," along with the other things that follow. 

The sense of these words is this: After you depart from this life, this people of yours will rise up and "go whoring," that is, they will go astray. Their error will be that they will say Jesus and Mary are "foreign gods of the land" and idolatries. And in this they will err, and they will forsake me, and they will make void my **Berith**—that is, my covenant—which is my Jesus and my Mary...

### BOOK IV. 638.

Rabbi Joden said, it is written in Psalm 46: <note>Original Hebrew: הרפו ודעו כי אנכי אלהים</note> "Be still, and know that I am **God**." <note>Psalm 46:10 in modern English Bibles.</note> That is: vacate or cease, and recognize that I am **God**. Therefore, the Holy and Blessed God said to Israel: Cease from your evil works, and perform <term>repentance</term> <note>Original Latin: pœnitentiam; Hebrew: Teshuvah</note> in the blink of an eye, and you shall know that I am God. Indeed, Rabbi Joden said: If the children of Israel were to perform repentance for even a single day, they would be redeemed immediately, and the Son of David—that is, the Messiah—would come to them right now. 

From where does he prove this? From that which is written in Psalm 95: <note>Original Hebrew: היום אם בקלו תשמעו</note> "Today, if you will hear his voice." <note>Psalm 95:7.</note> This is the tradition. From which it first appears clearly that if the Jews wished to perform repentance for a single day, setting aside the hardness of their disbelief, they would be redeemed at once and would have the Messiah. Indeed, the tradition proves this through that verse of the Psalm: "Today, if you will hear his voice." Therefore, if they were willing to recognize the sin which their fathers committed and perform repentance, they would soon have the Messiah and be completely liberated from their present captivity. 

Furthermore, from this same tradition, it is clearly elicited that the Messiah is God, through that which is said earlier in the same Psalm: <note>Original Hebrew: נחיה ונכרעה נברכה לפני יהוה עשנו : כי הוא אלהינו ואנחנו עם מרעיתו וצאן ידו</note> "Come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the face of the Lord our maker. For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand." <note>Psalm 95:6-7.</note> And immediately afterward follows that which was introduced concerning the Messiah in the aforementioned tradition, namely: "Today, if you will hear his voice." From this, it follows plainly that the Messiah is God. 

This same point is also evident in what is written in the <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>A Jewish homiletic commentary on the Psalms.</note>—that is, in the exposition of the Psalms—regarding the title of Psalm 44 <note>Psalm 45 in modern numbering.</note>, which is as follows: <note>Original Hebrew: למנצח על ששנים</note> "To the Victor," or "To the Conqueror," or "For the victory upon the lilies." Thus it is said: The Holy and Blessed God said to Israel: Everything depends on you. For just as this sort of lily sprouts or flourishes, and yet its heart is directed upward, so also you must perform <term>tessuba</term> <note>Original Hebrew: תשובה (Teshuvah), meaning repentance or "returning."</term> before me; and let your heart be right, or ordered upward, like this sort of lily. And then he will bring to you the <term>Goel</term> <note>Original Hebrew: גואל, meaning Redeemer.</term>. Just as it is said in Hosea 13 <note>Actually Hosea 14:5.</note>: <note>Original Hebrew: אהי כטל לישראל</note> "I will be as the dew to Israel." Which <term>Rabbi Jonathan</term> <note>Referring to the Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, an Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Prophets.</note> thus explained in Aramaic: <note>Original Aramaic: יהי מימרי כטלא לישראל</note> "My **Word** <note>Original Aramaic: Memra, often used to refer to God's manifest presence or agency.</note> shall be like the dew to Israel." And then this shall be: When he shall sprout like the lily. For it follows there in Hosea: <note>Original Hebrew: כשושנה</note> "he shall sprout," or "he shall flourish like the lily." Because of this, it says: "To the Victor upon the lilies." Thus far the tradition. From which the proposition is quite clearly evident. 

The same is also confirmed from the sayings of that ancient teacher, whom they call <term>Rabinnu haccados</term> <note>Our Holy Teacher, referring to Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century editor of the Mishnah.</note>. In the book titled <term>Gale razeya</term> <note>The Revealer of Secrets; a work of mystical or theological nature.</note>, at the end of his response to the petition of the Consul Marcus Antoninus, he says in this manner: "Indeed, from Israel, those who obtain the precepts of the author, the Messiah, shall attain the glory of the world to come. As it is written: <note>Original Hebrew: ועמך כלם צדיקים לעולם ירשו ארץ נצר מטעי מעשה ידי להתפאר</note> That is: 'Your people shall all be righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch [of my planting...]'" <note>Isaiah 60:21.</note>

### That the Gentiles were bound to adhere to the Messiah. Chapter XII.

->CAPNIO,<- <note>Capnio is the scholarly nickname for Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous German humanist and Hebraist.</note>

<margin>Concerning Galatinus.</margin>
Since you have spoken so much until now regarding the rejection of the Jews who persist in their faithlessness: <note>The original Latin "perfidia" here refers to a theological "lack of faith" or "unbelief" in the Christian Messiah.</note> it is only right that you also bring forth something from the *Hebrew* scriptures concerning the calling and election of the Gentiles. Therefore, first show that the Gentiles themselves were to adhere to the *Messiah*. GAL. <note>Galatinus, the other speaker in this dialogue.</note> This is most clearly evident from the fact that Zechariah prophesied it would be so in Chapter 2, saying: <note>Original Hebrew: ונלוו גוים רבים אל יהוה ביום ההוא והיו לי לעם</note> *That is, "And many nations," or many Gentiles, "shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and shall be my people."* <note>Zechariah 2:11.</note> Which *Rabbi Jonathan* <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the reputed author of the Targum (Aramaic translation) of the Prophets.</note> explains in the *Chaldean* <term>Chaldean</term> <note>At the time this was written, "Chaldean" was the common term for Aramaic.</note> verse as follows: <note>Original Aramaic: ויתוספון עממין סגיאין קדם עמיא דיהוה ביום ההוא ויהון קדמי לעם</note> That is, *“And many peoples shall add themselves to the people of the Lord in that time, and they shall be a people before me.”* <margin>Objection of the younger Jews.</margin> CAP. Jewish impiety <note>The author uses "impietas" to characterize the contemporary Jewish arguments he is trying to refute.</note> claims here that nations are to be added to God in the days of the Messiah not so they may be saved, but so they may serve the Jewish people. GAL. This is easily refuted; their falsehood is proven. For just as God said of them in *Leviticus chapter 26*: <note>Original Hebrew: והתהלכתי בתוככם והייתי לכם לאלהים ואתם תהיו לי לעם</note> *That is, "And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people."* <note>Leviticus 26:12.</note> So too does He say here of the Gentiles: "Many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and they shall be my people." From this it is manifestly clear, both from the divine page and the Chaldean translation, that they are telling total lies. This is also expressly evident from the sayings of their own ancient Teachers. For it is read in the <term>Massekhet Bikkurim</term> <note>Original: מסכת בכורים; The Mishnaic tractate regarding "First Fruits" brought to the Temple.</note>—that is, in the Book of First Fruits—in this manner: The Masters have handed down in the name of *Rabbi Judah*, that a <term>Ger</term> <note>Original: גר; a proselyte or convert.</note>—that is, a stranger or convert who comes from the Gentiles to the faith—is himself to bring the first fruits and say that which is in *Deuteronomy chapter 26*: <note>Original Hebrew: הגדתי היום ליהוה אלהיך כי באתי אל הארץ אשר נשבע יהוה לאבותינו לתת לנו</note> That is, *“I declare today to the Lord your God that I have come into the land which the Lord swore to our fathers to give to us.”* <note>Deuteronomy 26:3.</note> What is the proof of this? That which is written in *Genesis chapter 17*: <note>Original Hebrew: ולא יקרא עוד את שמך אברם והיה שמך אברהם כי אב המון גוים נתתיך</note> *That is, “Your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, because I have made you a father of a multitude of nations.”* <note>Genesis 17:5.</note> <margin>Tradition of Rabbi Judah.</margin> For in the beginning he was the "father of Aram" <note>Aram refers to the region of Syria/Mesopotamia.</note>, and therefore he was called Abram. But afterward, he became the "father of the whole world," and for that reason his name was called Abraham.

## BOOK II.

Thus far the tradition. Furthermore, Rabbi Rahmon <note>Likely referring to a Rabbinic authority cited in mystical or polemical literature, such as the Zohar or the Midrash; in this context, he is used to provide a Jewish perspective that supports Christian claims.</note> said, concerning that passage in Jeremiah 31:27: <margin>Jeremiah 31:27</margin> *Behold, I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.* <note>Original Hebrew: וזרעתי את בית ישראל ואת בית יהודה זרע אדם וזרע בהמה</note> That is to say: "The seed of man"—these are the people of Israel. Just as it was said in Ezekiel 34:31: <margin>Ezekiel 34:31</margin> *And you, my sheep, the sheep of my pasture, are men.* <note>Original Hebrew: צאן מרעיתי אדם אתם</note> And concerning them, the Holy and Blessed God said in Isaiah 65:9: <margin>Isaiah 65:9</margin> *And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob.* <note>Original Hebrew: ומיעקב זרע</note> However, that which follows, "the seed of the beast," refers to the converts from the nations <note>The "Gentiles" or non-Jews who join the faith.</note>, of whom it is said in the book of Joshua: *And many beasts.* And in Job chapter 18, Bildad the Shuhite said: *Why are we counted as beasts?* And concerning them, God himself said in Zechariah 2:10: *Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, for behold, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of you, says the Lord. And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and shall be my people.* But regarding Israel and the nations of the world, the Scripture speaks in Zechariah chapter 8, saying: <margin>Zechariah 8:10</margin> *For before those days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction.* <note>Original Hebrew: כי שכר האדם לא נהיה ושכר הבהמה איננה וליוצא ולבא אין שלום מן הצר</note> "Before those days," he means to say, before the days of the Messiah; for in the days of the Messiah, there shall be peace for him that is far off and him that is near. Just as it was said in Isaiah chapter fifty-seven: <margin>Isaiah 57:19</margin> *I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, says the Lord; and I will heal him.* <note>Original Hebrew: שפתים שלום שלום לרחוק ולקרוב אמר יהוה ורפאתיו</note> Concerning this, the Scripture also says in Zechariah chapter 9: *And he shall speak peace to the nations.* <note>Original Hebrew: ודבר שלום לגוים</note> For in that hour, there shall be peace for those departing from the world <note>Literally "from the age" or "from this life."</note> through the way of repentance, and for those entering, or coming before the Holy and Blessed God with good works and acts of charity. Just as it was said in Proverbs 14:34: <margin>Proverbs 14:34</margin> *Righteousness exalts a nation, but the kindness of nations is a sin.* <note>Original Hebrew: צדקת תרומם גוי וחסד לאמים חטאת. The author is interpreting the Hebrew "chatat" not as "sin" but as "sin-offering" or "atonement" in this specific context.</note> Where the commentaries of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval French commentator.</note> and Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra <note>A celebrated 12th-century Spanish scholar and grammarian.</note> state: the righteousness that the nations perform, and the piety they render—that is, charity—shall be for them in the place of a sacrifice for the propitiation <note>Atonement or making amends.</note> of sins. This is the tradition. From all these things, it is clear that the nations were not to be joined to the Messiah simply to serve the Jews (as the Jews themselves vainly chatter), but rather that they might be saved and made the people of God, just as God himself had foretold through Hosea in chapter 2, saying: <margin>Hosea 2:23</margin> *And I will sow her for myself in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, "You are my people"; and they shall say, "You are my God."* <note>Original Hebrew: וזרעתיה לי בארץ ורחמתי את לא רחמה ואמרתי ללא עמי עמי אתה והוא יאמר אלהי</note> Furthermore, it was proven extensively above in the sixth book that the Gentiles were to be saved at the time of the Messiah, and that they ought to embrace the Messiah himself in heart, word, and deed upon receiving him.

### *That the Gentiles who receive the Messiah were to be loved by God, and were destined to be the chosen and peculiar people of God. Chapter XIII.*

->CAPNIO,<-

To the greater confusion, therefore, of the Jews—who have been so shamefully rejected by God and held in eternal hatred—it must also be proven through their own scriptures: that the Gentiles, in the time of the Messiah, were to be converted to the worship of the one and true God, were to be loved by God, and were to be made and called His chosen and special people. GAL. This is most evident from the fact that, as a figure of this very thing, God himself commanded in the Old Testament that proselytes—that is, those coming from the Gentiles to the worship of the one God—be loved. Hence Nathan used to say: "The blemish that is in yourself, do not speak of it to your neighbor." For the newcomers—that is, the converts—are beloved. For in every place, a warning is given on their behalf, such as that in Exodus 22: *And the gher* <note>original: "גר"; the Hebrew word for a stranger or a convert to Judaism</note>—that is, the convert—*you shall not oppress.* And the stranger—that is, the convert from Gentility—you shall not rebuke. Rabbi Eliezer said: "Since the turning away of a newcomer—that is, a conversion—is a most difficult thing <note>The Latin "pessima" suggests that the act of a convert falling back into old ways, or the mistreatment of them, is considered a grave evil</note>, therefore a warning is given for him in many places." But Rabbi Simeon said: "Behold, God himself says in Judges chapter 5: *And you shall love him like the rising of the sun in its strength.* <margin>Judges 5:31</margin> For which of the two is greater: he who loves the King, or he whom the King loves? Behold, without a doubt they say: he whom the King loves." Regarding whom it is said in Deuteronomy 10: <note>Original Hebrew: עשה האל הגדול הגבור והנורא אשר לא ישא פנים ולא יקח שחד : משפט יתום ואלמנה ואהב גר לתת לו לחם ושמלה</note> That is: *The great God, mighty and terrible, who does not accept faces*—that is, show favoritism to persons—*nor receives a bribe, who executes judgment for the orphan and the widow, and loves the gher*—that is, the convert from the Gentiles—*to give him food and clothing.* The newcomers—that is, the converts—are also beloved. For in all things the *gher* himself—that is, the convert—is named or described just as Israel is. For Israel indeed are called the servants of God. ### That all the dignities once granted to the Jews were to be taken away from them, and granted to the Gentiles who would receive the Messiah, as the true and chosen people of God. Chapter XIV.

->CAPNIO,<- <note>Capnio is the Greek-style pseudonym of the famous Christian Hebraist Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522).</note>

I do not think it should be overlooked here that it is proved through the Jewish scriptures that all the dignities once granted to the Jews were to be taken away from them—as from unworthy possessors—and were to be granted to the Gentiles who would receive the Messiah, as the true, special, and chosen people of God. <margin>GAL.</margin> <note>Galatinus, the author of the book.</note> This is shown most clearly through what is read in the *Midrash Tehillim* <note>original: "Midras tehilim"; the traditional Rabbinic commentary on the Book of Psalms</note>, in the exposition of the 75th Psalm, regarding the verse: *And I will cut off all the horns of the wicked, and the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.* <note>Psalm 75:10</note> For it is said there:

It does not say "horn" but "horns." For there are ten horns that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to Israel. The horn of Abraham, as it is said in Isaiah 5: *My beloved had a vineyard on a horn of the son of oil.* <note>Isaiah 5:1; a literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for a fertile hill.</note> The horn of Isaac, of which it is written in Genesis 22: *And behold, a ram was caught in the thicket by its horns.* The horn of Joseph, as it is said in Deuteronomy 33: *And his horns are the horns of a wild ox.* <note>original: "rhinocerotis"; the Latin Vulgate often translates the Hebrew 're'em' (wild ox) as rhinoceros.</note> The horn of Moses, of which it is said in Exodus 34: *That the skin of his face was horned.* <note>Exodus 34:30; another famous Vulgate translation. Where modern Bibles say Moses' face "shone," the Latin followed the Hebrew root 'qaran' which can also mean 'to grow horns.'</note> The horn of power <note>or "prophecy," as the Latin translation below specifies</note>, as it is said in 1 Samuel 2: *And Hannah prayed and said: My heart exults in the Lord, and my horn is exalted.* The horn of the Law, as it is said in Habakkuk 3: *And there were horns coming out of his hand.* The horn of the priesthood, as is read in Psalm 112: *His horn shall be exalted in glory.* The horn of the Levites, as it is said in 1 Chronicles 25: *All these were the sons of Heman, the King's seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn.* The horn of Jerusalem, as it is said in Psalm 22: *And you have heard me from the horns of the wild oxen.* And the horn of King Messiah, as it is said in the second chapter of 1 Samuel: *And he shall give strength to his King, and shall exalt the horn of his Messiah.* And so it says in Psalm 132: *There I will make the horn of David to sprout; I have prepared a lamp for my Messiah.* But when Israel sinned, these horns were taken away from them and given to the nations of the world, as it is said in the latter days: *And I saw in the visions of the night, and behold, a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and exceedingly strong; and it had great iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet; and it was different from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.* <note>Daniel 7:7</note> For the nations of the world are compared to these beasts, and as long as the horns of the nations of the world remain, the horns of Israel are diminished, as it is said: *He has cut off in his fierce anger every horn of Israel.* <note>Lamentations 2:3</note>

That is: "Horn" was not said, but "horns." For there are ten <term>horns</term> <note>In biblical symbolism, a "horn" represents strength, dignity, or royal authority.</note> which the Holy One and Blessed gave to Israel. Namely, the horn of Abraham, of which it is said in Isaiah 5: *A vineyard was for my beloved on a horn of the son of oil.* The horn of Isaac, of which it is written in Genesis 22: *And behold, one ram held fast in the thicket by its horns.* The horn of Joseph, that is, the horn of the Kingdom, of which it is said in Deuteronomy 33: *And his horns are the horns of a rhinoceros.* The horn of Moses, of which it is said in Exodus 34: *That the skin of his face was horned.* The horn of prophecy, of which it is said in 1 Samuel 1: *And Hannah prayed and said, My heart has exulted in the Lord, and my horn is exalted.* The horn of the law, of which it is said in Habakkuk 3: *And two horns from his hand are for him.* The horn of the priesthood, of which it is read in Psalm 111: *His horn shall be exalted in glory.* The horn of the Levites, of which it is said in 1 Chronicles 25: *All these sons of Heman, the seer of the King in the words of God, to exalt the horn.* The horn of Jerusalem, of which it is said in Psalm 22: *And from the horns of the unicorns you have heard me.* And the horn of King Messiah, of which it is said in the second chapter of the first book of Kings: *And he gave strength to his King, and shall exalt the horn of his Messiah.* And so Psalm 132 says: *There I will make the horn of David to sprout; I have prepared a lamp for my Messiah.* When, however, Israel sinned, these horns were taken away from them and given to the nations according to...

As it is said in Daniel 7: *After this I saw in the night visions, and behold, a fourth beast, terrifying and wonderful, and exceedingly strong; it had great iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet. And it was different from all the beasts that were before it, and it had ten horns.* <note>Daniel 7:7</note> For the nations of this world are likened to wild beasts of this kind. Moreover, at whatever time the horns of the nations of the world are healthy, the horns of Israel shall be broken. As it is said in Lamentations, chapter 2: *He has cut off in his fierce anger every horn of Israel.* <note>Lamentations 2:3. The Latin "Tren." refers to Threni, another name for the Book of Lamentations.</note> All this is from tradition. These things are placed in almost the same words in the <note>original: "איכה רבתי" - Echa Rabbathi</note> **Lamentations Rabbah**—that is, in the exposition of the Lamentations of Jeremiah—concerning that saying in the second chapter of the same book: *He has cut off in his fierce anger every horn of Israel.* This is the same, except for the fact that in the tenth place it does not put the "horn of the Messiah," but only the "horn of Israel." Therefore, since in this tradition all the aforementioned horns are said to have been given to the head of Israel, and then truly taken from them because of their fault and handed over to the nations, and since one of those horns was the Messiah, it follows that the Messiah has already come. First, indeed, he was given to the Jews; then truly (their perfidy demanding it) he was taken from them along with all the other horns and given to the nations. 

**CAPNIO.** Because the extremely fraudulent malice of the younger Jews asserts that the "beast" mentioned just now is our Pope and the Roman Church, from which they hope the aforementioned horns will be taken away and restored to themselves. On that account, you would do very well if you would explain when these horns of the Jews were given to this fourth beast—that is, to the Roman Empire—which, because of its idolatry, was not inaptly compared to a beast.

<margin>
The objection of the younger Jews.
</margin>

**GALATINUS.** <margin>The Response.</margin> The **horn of the Jewish kingdom** was then placed upon the head of this fourth beast when the Jewish kingdom, along with the Jews themselves, was given over to the power and possession of the Roman Empire to be crushed and scattered, in the times of Vespasian, Titus, and Hadrian. <note>Vespasian and Titus oversaw the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD; Hadrian suppressed the Bar Kokhba revolt in 135 AD.</note> But the **horn of the priesthood** and the Levites was then taken away from the Jews when [the Empire] slew their priests and Levites and utterly destroyed the divine worship among them because of their crimes. But in the time of **Sylvester**, the Roman Pontiff, and the Emperor **Constantine**, that same horn was placed upon the head of the Romans. <note>Pope Sylvester I and Emperor Constantine the Great, under whom Christianity became the dominant religion of the Roman Empire in the 4th century.</note> 

The **horn of the Messiah** was also given to them at that time when the Messiah himself was sent to them for their salvation. But then it was taken from them when they, rejecting the Messiah himself, crucified him. At that time, however, the same horn was given to the Roman Church and the rest of the faithful, when the nations took up the worship of that same Messiah. Furthermore, the **horn of Jerusalem** and of the sanctuary was then taken from them and handed over to the Romans when the city itself and the Temple were overturned and burned by Titus. 

Finally, the **horn of the Law**, as far as the ceremonies are concerned, was handed over to this beast to be destroyed when the Roman Princes forbade the Jews from keeping the Sabbath, circumcision, and other legal requirements, as will be more broadly evident in the following book. But then the same horn, as far as moral matters are concerned, was given to the Romans and other Gentiles to be kept more perfectly, when the Gentiles themselves received the law of the Lord Jesus, the true Messiah, to be observed as divine.

# On the institution of the new divine law which was to be established through the Messiah.

### Chapter 1: That the Messiah was to establish a new divine law, more perfect than the old, which the Gentiles were to receive.

---

->CAPNIO<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'N' depicting a figure seated in a landscape with foliage, possibly a classical or mythological scene.</image-desc>Therefore, since the Gentiles were to receive the new law of the Messiah as divine—those who, as you have already proved, would adhere to the Messiah himself (the Jews having been largely rejected for their unfaithfulness)—it is now quite fitting, in order to further subdue the stubborn pride <note>literally "stiffest neck," a biblical idiom for obstinacy</note> of those same Jews, to speak of the institution of that same new divine law. For this reason, you must first show by Hebrew testimonies that the Messiah himself was to establish a new divine law, more perfect than the old, and that the Gentiles were to receive it.

<margin>GALATINUS</margin>Indeed, it was prophesied long ago by Jeremiah in chapter 31 that God would give a new law, different from the one He gave through Moses on Mount Sinai, in these words:

> Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will cut a new covenant <note>original Hebrew: "ברית חדשה" - berith chadashah</note> with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. Not like the covenant that I cut with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, for they broke my covenant, and I neglected them, says the Lord. But this will be the covenant that I will cut with the house of Israel: After those days, says the Lord, I will put my law <note>original Hebrew: "תורתי" - torati</note> in their midst, and write it upon their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be my people.

That is to say: "Behold, the days will come," says God, "and I will cut with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah a new league or pact." Not like the pact that I cut with their fathers on the day I took their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, who disrupted my pact, and I neglected them, says God. "But this shall be the pact that I will cut with the house of Israel. After those days," says God, "I will give my law in their midst, and upon their heart I will write it. And I will be to them as God, and they shall be to me as a people." Just as it is said in Deuteronomy 24 <note>This citation follows the numbering in the source; in modern bibles this is Deut 29:1 or 28:69</note>:

These are the words of the covenant <note>original: "הברית" - ha-berith</note> which the Lord commanded Moses to cut with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which He cut with them at Horeb.

# BOOK NINE

Jerusalem. But from Sinai he came to Jerusalem. **Regarding the law of the Messiah**, therefore, it must be understood that it went out from Jerusalem to the nations through the apostles and his other disciples. For the Messiah himself—the Son of God according to his divinity and the wisdom of the Father—descending from the highest heights and from the seat of his majesty for the redemption and salvation of the human race, was sent by the Father and came to Zion and Jerusalem. There he fulfilled his new law, which is the Gospel, by teaching, admonishing, persuading, arguing, performing miracles, suffering, dying, rising again, ascending into heaven, and directing the light of the Holy Spirit to the apostles. Thus, this prophetic saying was fulfilled when the apostles, after receiving the Holy Spirit, first proclaimed the law of the Gospel in Jerusalem, and afterward, departing from there, spread it everywhere to the nations of the earth. 

That the nations of the world were to receive this new law and doctrine with joy from the chosen disciples of the Messiah is held from what is said in Isaiah 12:3: "And you shall draw waters with joy from the fountains of salvation." <note>original Hebrew: *u-sh’avtem mayim be-sason mi-ma’aynei ha-yeshu’ah*. The author notes the Hebrew word for "salvation" (*yeshu’ah*) is the root of the name *Jesus*.</note> For Rabbi Jonathan <note>The Targum of Jonathan, an ancient Aramaic translation and expansion of the Hebrew Bible</note> translated this into Aramaic as: "And you shall receive a new doctrine with joy from the chosen ones of the righteous one." <note>original Aramaic: *ve-yitkabelun ulpana hadata im hedva min behirei tzadikiya*</note> That is, from the Messiah. 

All the Jews of our time are therefore foolish, and entirely astray and alienated from the truth of the divine scripture, who assert that the Messiah would be bound by [the old] laws. For we have proved in many ways in the preceding pages that he is God. He himself is the wisdom of the Father, and the laws are his. He is the one who gave the old law on Mount Sinai. He is the one who established the new law in Jerusalem. He is the creator of the men to whom the laws were handed down, and the supreme craftsman of all things in heaven and under heaven. For that reason, it was both fitting and worthy that in his descent to earth, he should reserve greater and better things to give himself than those he had delivered through Moses on Mount Sinai. 

And this is a sufficient argument against the Jews of our age. For if anyone seeks a more "necessary" reason in matters of the will than the voluntary acts themselves provide, he is utterly unteachable, according to the opinion of Aristotle in the first book of the *Ethics*. <note>Referring to Aristotle’s *Nicomachean Ethics*, where he argues that one should only seek as much precision as the subject matter allows.</note> Since this reasoning concerns voluntary acts <note>referring to God’s free choice to give a new law</note>, it is therefore entirely sufficient. For we see the same thing happen in human governments: Kings and Princes, upon their arrival, reserve the very best things to be bestowed upon their cities. And this is for a twofold reason: First, so that they may make their arrival more honorable through more honorable gifts; and second, so that they may make themselves more pleasing and welcome to their cities and Kingdom.
