<page-num>852</page-num>

<header>CABALA</header>

...[of the so]ns, the bow of testimony, the glory of the Lord, the foundation of prophecy, [of] David, redemption, the world of souls. They are also reduced to the tenth numeration: **Adonai** <note>Lord</note>, kingship, life, the second cherub. The non-illuminating vision <note>original: *Speculatio non illuminans*; a reference to the "dull mirror" of prophecy associated with the lowest emanation</note>. The back parts. The end. The Congregation of Israel, the Bride in the Song of Songs, the Queen of Heaven. The Virgin of Israel. The mystery of the law given by mouth <note>The Oral Torah</note>. The Eagle, the fourth letter of the **Tetragrammaton** <term>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</term>. The kingdom of the house of David. The temple of the king, the gate of God, the ark of the covenant, and the two tablets within it. The Lord of the whole earth. 

You have heard a brief account of the ten properties, or notions, or divine attributes, which are called by the Kabbalists **Belimah** <note>original: בלימה (*Belimah*), a word from the *Sefer Yetzirah* often translated as "nothingness" or "ineffable"</note>, which some understand as *Beli* (without or except) and *Mah* (what); as if to signify: "Ten beyond 'what'"—namely, excluding the "whatness" or essence of God. Hence they are accustomed to interpret *Belimah* as being beyond that which is ineffable; others derive it from "restraining your mouth and your tongue from speaking" <note>original: בלום פיך ולשונך מלדבר (*Belum pikekha u-leshonekha mi-ledabber*)</note>, as if these were sacred words that should not be disclosed to the common people.

Now we should speak of the angelic princes and the demonic leaders whom the Kabbalists place at the sides of Mercy and Severity, a matter indeed requiring much discussion, if we were not already passing midday and moving toward evening. For who could explain such great things in a short time? Who could so quickly finish describing the thirty-five princes of purity and the seventy princes of Ishmael on the side of the fourth numeration <note>The emanation of *Chesed* (Mercy/Lovingkindness)</note>? Likewise, who could sufficiently explain, so briefly and perfunctorily, the thirty-five princes of guilt and the seventy princes of Esau in the fifth numeration <note>The emanation of *Gevurah* (Severity/Judgment)</note> of weight and fear? These things require their own volumes, and quite extensive ones at that; therefore, setting them aside for the present, let us proceed to more difficult matters.

The happiness, I say, of the most contemplative men depends—according to the manner of their choosing—upon day and night meditation on the Law, that is, the twenty-four books which we call the Hebrew Bible <note>original: *Varba*; likely a Latinization of *Arba'a [ve-Esrim]*, "The Twenty-Four," a traditional Jewish name for the Tanakh</note>, as is understood from the sacred letters. For it is written: "Blessed is the man (among other things) who will meditate on His law day and night" <note>Psalm 1:1-2</note>. It does not say "he who reads," "he who writes," or "he who speaks," but "he who meditates"; lest perhaps the writing or reading of the law, once finished and ended, should force happiness to cease and end as well. 

The one, finally, who compels the thoughts in his heart to focus there, so that—having dismissed fleshly things—he may meditate on the spiritual aspects of the law; that man, I say, is blessed, for he shall see God with a pure heart. For in my judgment, such great diligence need not be applied to the histories of Holy Scripture, which are as clear to the Hebrews as Titus Livius <note>Livy, the Roman historian</note> is to the Latins. Likewise for the commands and precepts that have a fixed number, as well as for the religious rites and ceremonies which even the unrefined and unlearned common folk often perform without fault or sin; hence they do not merit such great happiness, as these things consist of bodily senses, so as to require such assiduous, continuous, and diligent meditation day and night. But a far greater happiness can be found in the higher degrees of contemplation, as [this work] demonstrates...

### BOOK III.

...the Kabbalistic understanding of the law extends so far that it imbues our minds with spiritual meditation and forms them, as it were, into its own likeness. We conjecture this to be the meditation on the law which was finally delivered by the mouth of God to Moses after the law was given in fire, and the stone tablets had been broken and then restored. For first, as the Kabbalists assert, God wrote His law in a sphere of fire, using dark fire upon white fire; for Ramban of Girona <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, also known as Nachmanides (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar</note> says: <gloss>original Hebrew: שבא לנו בקבלה שהיתה כתובה באש שחורה על גבי אש לבנה — "It has come down to us through Kabbalah that it was written in black fire upon a surface of white fire."</gloss> That is: "What appears to us through Kabbalah is that the writing was in dark fire upon the back of white fire." Hence that passage in Deuteronomy 33 appears: *From His right hand came a fiery law for them.* 

And the letters were then (as they say) confused and jumbled together; those who were most studious, looking upon them contemplatively and considering them diligently while led by the Holy Spirit, could easily select, read, and collect them from here and there, up and down, back and forth, to and fro, and form them into any words to make a sentence, signifying good for the good and evil for the evil. But Moses, instructed by God, reduced them all into the order to be published to the people, so that all might know and observe the things of the law; and from there the law was divided into books and placed in the ark, just as he received it from the Lord. 

However, the art of ordering and varying the letters and interpreting the Holy Scripture most sweetly for the elevation of the mind—which was then received from the Divine Majesty—he did not reveal to the common people, as it was a most divine matter imperceptible to the unrefined. Instead, he passed it on "mouth to mouth" <note>The Latin *ore ad os* implies a direct, oral transmission of secret knowledge</note> only to the chosen Joshua and the seventy elders, from whom afterwards the most select individuals always received it; and this reception, as you have heard before, is called **Kabbalah** <term>from the Hebrew *Qabbalah*, meaning "tradition" or "received thing"</term>. 

Even the wisest of the Christian doctors support this somewhat; although I am a Jew, I have gladly read many of them, creeping into "foreign camps" like a scout. For concerning our Moses, that Greek Gregory Nazianzen <note>A 4th-century Church Father known as "The Theologian"</note>, surnamed the Great, says in his book *On the State of Bishops*: <gloss>original Greek: δέχεται νόμον, τοῖς μὲν πολλοῖς, τὸν τοῦ γράμματος, τοῖς δ' ὑπὲר τοὺς πολλοὺς, τὸν τοῦ πνεύματος — "He receives the law: for the many, that of the letter; but for those above the many, that of the spirit."</gloss> And in the first book of *Theology*: <gloss>original Greek: βούλεται οὕτω πλαξὶ σεῤῥαῖς καὶ λιθίναις ἐγγραφῆναι, καὶ ταύτας ἀμφοτέρωθεν· διὰ τε τὸ φαινόμενον τοῦ νόμου καὶ τὸ κρυπτόμενον, τὸ מὲν τοῖς πολλοῖς καὶ κάτω μένεσι, τὸ δὲ τοῖς ὀλίγοις καὶ ἄνω φθάνουסי — "He willed it to be written thus on solid and stone tablets, and these on both sides; because of both the manifest and the hidden aspect of the law—the one for the many who remain below, the other for the few who reach upward."</gloss> 

From these words it appears to certain very learned men, even among your own people, how Moses delivered the text of the law to the common folk, but reserved the mysteries, parables, and symbols for himself and the more eminent. We have understood that this art of Kabbalah was divided into three ways, by the testimony of Solomon who says in Proverbs 22: *Have I not written to you three times in counsel and knowledge, that I might make known to you the certainty of the words of truth?* For thus our people are accustomed to speak when mention must be made of Kabbalah,

# OF KABBALAH

...so that they call it **Words of Truth** <note>original Hebrew: *imre emet*</note>, that is, written words of truth, specifically **According to the Way of Truth** <note>original Hebrew: *al derekh ha-emet*</note>, that is, according to the path of Kabbalah. This usage was frequent for the Egyptian <note>The Jewish philosopher Maimonides (1138–1204), who lived in Egypt</note> and the one from Gerona <note>The scholar Nachmanides (1194–1270)</note> and others. But others have displayed five parts of Kabbalah, such as Rabbi Hamai in the *Book of Speculation*, who names them thus: **Rectification, Combination, Discourse, Speech, and Calculation** <note>original Hebrew: *Tikkun, Tziruf, Ma’amar, Melal, and Cheshbon*—these represent different ways of manipulating and understanding the divine language</note>. Your Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a famous Italian Renaissance philosopher who integrated Kabbalah into Christian thought</note> wrote in his *Nine Hundred Conclusions* in these words: "Whatever other Kabbalists may say, I would distinguish the science of Kabbalah by a primary division into the science of the <term>Sefirot</term> <note>The ten creative powers or attributes of God</note> and of <term>Shemot</term> <note>The Divine Names</note>, as if into practical and speculative branches." But Rabbi Joseph bar Abraham the Castilian <note>Likely referring to Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305), a major Spanish Kabbalist</note> and the vast majority of Kabbalists follow King Solomon in believing that this art can be practiced not only speculatively but also practically in three ways, according to the triple condition of all things: **number, figure, and weight** <note>A reference to the biblical Book of Wisdom 11:20: "But thou hast arranged all things by measure and number and weight"</note>, indeed reducing those five parts into these three. For since the whole business is allegorical, and one thing is understood for another through a third, so that the meaning itself is one thing in place of another, we shall say openly that either a word is placed for a word, or a letter for a word, or a letter for a letter. First, certainly, a word is taken for a word, as through the transposition which is called metathesis <note>Rearranging letters to form new words</note>, or through an equal number included in the words <note>This is the method of Gematria, where words with the same numerical value are seen as connected</note>. A letter is placed for a word either at the beginning or at the end or anywhere else, indicated by a mark placed above <note>This is the method of Notarikon, or creating acronyms</note>. A letter is placed for a letter through alphabetical revolution <note>The method of Temurah, where letters are substituted for others based on a specific cipher or "revolution" of the alphabet</note>; clearly, the whole is done so that every proportion may finally be completed in arithmetic, geometry, and music. For example, that passage of Psalm 21, *O Lord, in your strength the king shall rejoice*, they understand Kabbalistically as referring to the Messiah, saying: *O Lord, in the strength of your four-letter name, the King Messiah comes* (or works). For the Messiah is the power of God and works in the power of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>. I am led to this by this word **shall rejoice** <note>original Hebrew: *yismach* (ישמח)</note>, whose letters, if transposed, will be **Messiah** <note>original Hebrew: *Mashiach* (משיח)</note>. And likewise in the place where the Lord said to Moses, *For my angel shall go before you* (Exodus 23). Who is that angel according to the Kabbalists? Some say Michael, for by transposing the letters of **my angel** <note>original Hebrew: *malakhi* (מלאכי)</note> it becomes Michael. Others, taking it according to the method of the Kabbalistic art, affirm that it is **Metatron** <note>A high-ranking angel in Jewish mysticism who serves as the celestial scribe</note>, because God said, "For my name is in him." Now, Metatron is the name **Shaddai** <note>Almighty</note> through an equal number included in both words <note>Both Metatron and Shaddai sum to 314 in Hebrew numerology</note>, which the one from Gerona wonderfully embraces in the place cited before. Do you now see the two symbolic ways of Kabbalah? Or do you wish to see the third, where a letter is put back for a word? Read Isaiah chapter 65: *He shall be blessed in God, Amen.* Who is this God? The Kabbalists will respond that it is **The Lord, the Faithful King** <note>original Hebrew: *Adonai Melekh Ne’eman* (אדני מלך נאמן)</note>; these three words by their initials will be noted by the three letters of **Amen** <note>א-מ-נ</note>, as Renat wrote regarding Exodus 15. The fourth species and third part of Kabbalah is literary commutation, where a word written with certain letters symbolically from the figure...

# BOOK III.

...another expression composed of other letters, which is done through alphabetical revolution according to Abraham’s *Book of Creation* <note>original: *Sepher Ietzira*</note> in twenty-two variations, corresponding to the twenty-two alphabets read therein. An example is provided to us by **Mazpaz** <note>original Hebrew: מצפץ</note>, a name of God written with these four letters. Regarding this, your Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), who attempted to harmonize Kabbalah with Christian theology</note> says: "The name of God of four letters, which consists of *Mem*, *Tzade*, *Pe*, and *Tzade*, should be attributed to the Kingdom of David." Since that name is not clearly read in the text of Holy Scripture, I ask, of what shall it be held as a symbol? The Kabbalists respond that it is the symbol and seal of the ineffable <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, considered too holy to pronounce</note> and proceeds from the last alphabet, which is the twenty-second of the book called the *Book of Creation* <note>original: *Sepher Ietzira*</note>, and it is called **Ath-bash** <note>A substitution cipher where the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>. For in that system, *Yod* is exchanged for *Mem*, *He* for *Tzade*, and *Vav* for *Pe*, so that **Mazpaz** is **Lord** <note>original: *Adonai*</note>, **Yod-He-Vav-He**. I have just spoken of those things pertaining to the art which is performed by crossing, transposing, or changing expressions, syllables, or letters, according to the four methods by which the senses of the scriptures are ingeniously and skillfully allegorized.

Regarding those matters which stand without such art and are performed by tradition alone—which I call **Atechna** <note>original Greek: *atechnos*, meaning "without technical art" or "unskilled"</note>—I have made you more than sufficiently informed, although previously you both, by your own profession, had acquired no small amount of knowledge of them through your own study. Namely, how simple things are abstracted from the composite, and higher things from the lower, and how almost all things are referred back to the intelligible world, or the super-supreme and incomparable world. Often, while reading the holy letters, certain arguments of piety may come to our minds which first lead us to a wonder of divine things and then entice us into the love of them; yet these cannot be handed down by any certain art. For example, the idea that Gabriel is of stronger power than Michael, because it is read of him in the book of Daniel: "with double power, flying swiftly" <note>Referencing Daniel 9:21; the Latin text interprets the Hebrew "wearied in flight" as a doubling of power</note>. Of Michael, however, it is only said that he "comes to help." Therefore, among the <term>Intelligences</term> <note>Angelic or celestial beings</note>, Gabriel is philosophically regarded as the power of the **Active Intellect**, and Michael as the power of the **Passive Intellect**. So writes Rabbi Levi Ben Gersom <note>Known as Gersonides (1288–1344), a philosopher and astronomer</note>, who is called by the Latins **Master Leo of Bagnols**.

Philolaus then said: It seems to me, Simon, that what you call "without art" <note>original: *Atechnon*</note> contributes most greatly to the Kabbalistic art. For unless we have in hand the revelations of the ancestors—which you rightly think do not fall under the rules of art—every person would be granted a reckless license to explain and turn Holy Scripture wherever they wished. This is just as we have heard certain common <term>Sophists</term> <note>In this context, academic philosophers who used complex logic but lacked spiritual insight</note> do, who in this age seem to have brought those most holy oracles of the Divine Spirit into public contempt with their syllogisms. But now, when all things (as I believe) must be applied to what has been revealed, a certain "line" is spoken of, "beyond or on this side of which the right cannot consist" <note>A quote from Horace’s *Satires*, suggesting there is a middle path or boundary to truth</note>, so that the works of the worst men do not turn the products of the art toward idleness.

Then Simon said: You clearly speak the truth. For there is almost nothing else that twists the oracles more erroneously toward one’s own feelings than this, although it is not always done out of malice, but often more through ignorance. For who, being devoted...

-># CABALA<-

...committed a sin in the performance of sacred rites? In this way, Saul was once deceived by an ambiguity of words and strayed from the divine oracle. For when God had promised: **I will blot out the memory of Amalek** <note>original Hebrew: אֶמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק (*emheh et zecher amalek*); see Exodus 17:14</note>, Saul believed he had satisfied the command by killing the males, because the word *memory* can also signify *male* <note>original Hebrew: זָכָר (*zachar*). In unpointed Hebrew, the letters Z-K-R can mean both "memory" (*zecher*) and "male" (*zachar*)</note>. God, however, intended the memory of Amalek to be blotted out, using a word that specifically designates remembrance. At that time, there was not yet a distinction in the writing through vowel points and accents, which only began in the years of Ezra <note>Ezra the Scribe (5th century BCE), traditionally credited with standardizing the Hebrew script and formalizing the use of vowel signs</note>. Therefore, the word *ZKR* without points signifies both *memory* and *male*, and this ambiguity provided the occasion for Saul’s downfall.

To this, Marranus added: A similar thing happened among the Greeks regarding the word **light** <note>original Greek: φῶς (*phos*)</note>, which signifies both *man* and *light* <note>In archaic Greek, φώς (*phōs*) with an acute accent means "man," while φῶς (*phôs*) with a circumflex means "light"</note>. Because of this ambiguity, certain worshipers at the festivals of Saturn were deceived; they would sacrifice a human being to Saturn every year, when in fact the sacrifice could have been performed just as well by lighting lamps according to the oracle, so that the god might be appeased. Indeed, that foolish nation finally ceased this practice under the instruction of Hercules. It is a pitiable thing even in our own age how much certain dull and proud sophists err through their ignorance of languages. This might be bearable, were it not for the fact that they contend they have not erred, and they harbor a deadly envy toward those who point out their mistakes. But, oh our teacher, please follow through more fully on the **Kabbalistic art** whose introduction you have begun.

Simon replied: It is the opinion of the most skilled men that this art consists of three things. First, the calculation of numbers, which is called <term>Gematria</term> <note>original Hebrew: גִּמַטְרִיָא; a method of interpreting biblical names and phrases based on the numerical value of their letters</note>, as if it were a "Geometry" of earthly characters; a numerical dimension which nevertheless depends on that higher arithmetic which, because of its pure simplicity, is not graspable by any senses and is therefore not subject to any crude craftsmanship. It was called Geometry rather than arithmetic, although in truth both function as one in this art. 

Secondly, sometimes syllables are changed, or a word is transformed, or a term is simply inverted. This is called <term>Notarikon</term> <note>original Hebrew: נוֹטַרִיקוֹן; derived from the Latin *notarius* (shorthand writer). A system where each letter of a word stands for another word, or the first and last letters are used to form new meanings</note>, because there any letter is noted at the summit so that it may be a sign for an entire word. 

Thirdly, this art consists of the permutation of letters, when one is placed for another by ingenuity; this is called <term>Temurah</term> <note>original Hebrew: תְּמוּרָה, meaning "exchange" or "substitution"</note>. Because of this, Rabbi Joseph the Minor of Salerno <note>A 13th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> named the books he wrote on this subject **The Garden** <note>original Hebrew: גִנַּת (*Ginnat*)</note>, on account of the three letters of that word, each of which designates a portion of the Kabbalistic art. For the letter *Gimel* [ג] signifies **Gematria**, *Nun* [נ] signifies **Notarikon**, and *Tav* [ת] signifies **Temurah**. Thus, the parts of the whole art are these: **Gematria** (Arithmetic), **Notarikon** (the system of notations), and **Temurah** (the commutation of elements). To this title, the author alludes to the verse of Solomon in the Song of Songs: *I went down into the garden of nuts.* 

Regarding the first part, I shall begin from that which is the principle. It is written in Zechariah that the Lord of the four-letter name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> shall be **One** <note>original Hebrew: אֶחָד (*Echad*)</note>, and His name shall be **One** <note>original Hebrew: אֶחָד (*Echad*)</note>.

It then defines the three branches of Kabbalah: Gematria (numerology), Notarikon (acronyms), and Temurah (letter substitution).</summary>

### BOOK III.

...one, or perhaps more truly, the Lord God will be **Aleph**, that is the beginning, as you Greeks say **Alpha and Omega**, and *Yah* <note>original Hebrew: יה (*Yah*), a shortened form of the divine name</note>, that is, one, as He who is the beginning of the one. For He Himself is above all unity and is the eternal origin of all unity. And perhaps He is not called "one," just as He is not called "being," because He is above all being from which whatever exists emanates. Whence He is named by the most contemplative ones *Ayin* <note>original Hebrew: אין (*Ayin*), meaning "Nothingness" or "Non-existence"</note>, that is, non-being, as is read in Exodus 17: **Is the Lord among us, or not?** <note>original: *Num est ens Adonai inter nos, an non ens?* The author interprets the Hebrew word *ayin* (nothing/not) at the end of the verse as a name for God’s transcendent non-being</note>. Moreover, it is read in the book *On the Way of Faith and Expiation* that He is both: **the Lord is** <note>original Hebrew: היש יהוה (*ha-yesh YHVH*)</note>, that is, Being and non-being, since those things which are, and those which are not, are from Him, and follow after Him.

So also He is not "one," because He is the cause of all unity, and unity is after Him, and He is none of those things—neither those which are after Him nor those which are not—as in the *Book of Speculation* by Rabbi Hamai, who after many things says thus: **that all things are emanated from His unity and He is not like that one itself.** <note>original Hebrew: שכלם נאצלים מאחדותי הוא אינו דומה לאחר (*she-kulam ne'etzalim me-achduti hu eno domeh l'acher*)</note>. Nor do our people alone confess this, but your sages likewise assert it, whom you prove to be most wise. For Dionysius the Areopagite <note>A 5th-6th century Christian theologian and philosopher, often cited in mystical traditions</note>, in his book *On Mystical Theology*, subscribed to the same opinion about God in these words: **that He is neither number nor order, nor one, nor unity.** <note>original Greek: ὅτι οὐκ ἀριθμὸς ἐστιν οὔτε τάξις, οὔτε ἕν, οὔτε ἑνότης</note>

What then is He? Simonides replied to Hiero: "The more I think, the less I understand." And a similar thing happens to me: when, having passed through all created things, I ascend above all being, I find nothing other than an infinite sea of nothingness, and the fountain of all entity flowing perpetually from the abyss of darkness. O height! O depth! O our weakness! But it ought to seem enough that we know of Him what He Himself has revealed to us of Himself: that He is the beginning, which is **Aleph**, and the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, which is signified by **Aleph** and denotes the divine essence, which is nothing other than *Hovayah* <note>original Hebrew: הויה (*Hovayah*), meaning "Existence" or "Being"</note>, namely, "it is," which certainly will be almost the same as the essence of the Tetragrammaton <note>original Hebrew: יהוה (*YHVH*)</note>. For on account of their equal value <note>A reference to Gematria, where words with the same numerical sum are linked</note>, the scripture has joined both, as if of Him who is the first and the last, in Exodus 9: **Behold, the hand of the Lord is** <note>original Latin/Hebrew: *Ecce manus Tetragrammati hoiah*</note>, as if to say "it is," namely the end of the works and miracles of God, as is clear in the ten plagues of Egypt. For elsewhere that word is not found in this way. Moreover, by the testimony of Solomon of Troyes <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note>, it indicates an imminent essence.

But the fact that the Tetragrammaton begins with **Iod** <note>The Hebrew letter *Yod* (י)</note> was clearly done for our sake, so that we might recognize Him to be the infinite point and the fulfillment of every number—that is, of every thing. For **Iod** signifies ten. And in the expansion of the name of the Tetragrammaton, the tenth letter is found thus: **YHVH YHV YHY** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה יהו יהי</note>. Where after the Tetragrammaton is found **YHY** <note>original Hebrew: יהי (*Yahi*)</note>, which is the symbol of *Ehieh* <note>original Hebrew: אהיה (*Ehieh*), the name "I Am" or "I Will Be" from Exodus 3:14</note> itself, that is, of being, through equality of number. And nonetheless it also signifies the essence of the Creator, as in Exodus 3: **Ehieh sent me to you**; not that which remains within, but that which flows outward. For the Tetragrammaton <note>original Hebrew: יהוה (*YHVH*)</note> is the seal of God with which **Ehieh** sealed the world, and it is called **Truth** <note>original Hebrew: אמת (*Emeth*)</note>, because it in itself—

# ON KABBALAH

...is born by multiplying arithmetically. Then follows **Yah** <note>original Hebrew: יה (*Yah*)</note>, the name of essence, merit, and retribution: as in the Psalms, **If you, Yah, should mark iniquities.** <note>original Latin: *Si iniquitates obseruaueris Iah*; Psalm 130:3</note>. You see, therefore, three essential names in the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: the four-letter name of God, YHWH, often considered too sacred to pronounce</term>. The **Ineffable** <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> denotes the first essence; **Ehieh** <note>original Hebrew: אהיה (*Ehieh*), meaning "I Am" or "I Will Be"</note> the essence in things; and **Yah** the effect in merits: and these are predicated in that which is the "what." And that is called **Mah** <note>original Hebrew: מה (*Mah*), meaning "What"</note>, which is the "whatness": For the Tetragrammaton, when spelled out as **Yod He Vav He** <note>The letters of the name YHWH written out phonetically: יוד הא ואו הא</note>, signifies **Mah** through equality of number, for both contain the value of 45 <term>Gematria: a system where Hebrew letters represent numbers; the sum of the letters in "Mah" is 45, matching this specific expansion of the divine name</term>. And when Moses said, **What is His name, what shall I say?** it is answered to him, **Ehieh**. Then, if you diligently consider the words of the Holy Spirit, which are not placed there in vain in the same passage of Exodus 3: **To me, what is His name is established.** <note>original Latin/Hebrew: *li mah shemo mah* (לי מה שמו מה); the author is performing a linguistic analysis on the Hebrew text of Exodus 3:13</note>

And look at their terminal letters, and you will have the four-letter Ineffable name **YHWH** whose beginning is **Ehieh**, its middle is **Yah**, and its end is infinity. For its parts are **YHY YHY YHY** <note>original Hebrew: יהי (*Yehi*), meaning "Let there be"</note> which we divide into three intervals. The first is **YHY**, the second is **YHY**, the third is **YHY**. All these serve to define "being" and "essence." Concerning **Yah**, we read in Exodus 15: **My strength and my praise is Yah.** Concerning **YHY** in the same place: **And He has become my salvation.** Concerning **YHY** in the first chapter of Genesis: **Let there be light.** These two last words contributed greatly to the craftsmanship of the world and the existence of things, as in: **Let there be light, and light was made.** <note>original Latin: *Fiat lux, & factum est lux*</note>. And there was evening, and there was morning. **Let there be a firmament, and let there be a distinction, and it was made so.** **Let the waters be gathered, and it was made so.** **Let the earth sprout, and it was made so.** **Let the earth bring forth, and it was made so.** **Let there be lights, and it was made so.** Always adding this: **And it was made evening and it was made morning.** In all these things (so that they truly might be), we perceive that the seeds and the secret Ineffable name are present.

Indeed, we see only **Elohim** <note>original Hebrew: אלהים (*Elohim*), a name for God usually associated with Justice or the natural order</note>, that is God, expressed in the works of the six days. But when the world now appeared perfect, after the various and wonderful works of the most divine powers were completed—so that finally a triumph for merit might be celebrated and the fourth day declared—behold, the **Tetragrammaton King** and **Lord of lords** entered alongside **Elohim**, and then for the first time it was said: **These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created in the day that the Tetragrammaton Elohim made the heaven and the earth.** <note>original Latin: *Istæ sunt generationes cœli & terræ...*; Genesis 2:4. Note that Genesis 1 uses "Elohim," but Genesis 2 begins using "YHWH Elohim"</note>. Here the Tetragrammaton first thundered publicly in the ears of all creatures, by which we understand the mercy of God joined with His justice: for in whatever place of Holy Scripture the Tetragrammaton joins **Elohim** to itself, there we observe the property of mercy and justice together. It is sometimes composed with **Adonai** <note>original Hebrew: אדני (*Adonai*), meaning "Lord"</note> as in the prayer of Habakkuk: **The Tetragrammaton Adonai is my strength**; and in reading, we understand the power of the Tetragrammaton to descend to the spoken **Adonai** itself. But if it is found in the reversed order, **Adonai Tetragrammaton**, as in Genesis 15: **Adonai Tetragrammaton, what will You give me?**—in this we conceive in the mind that the numerations (that is, the divine properties), ascending from the lower to the higher, take hold of the supreme light. It also happens sometimes that the name **El** <note>original Hebrew: אל (*El*), meaning "God" or "Mighty One"</note> is found joined, as in Psalm 118: **El YHWH**...

# BOOK III.

...the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH, often substituted in speech with "Lord"</term> has shone upon us and signifies mercy. In a similar way, when **Elohim** <note>original Hebrew: אלהים (*Elohim*), a name of God often associated with justice and the natural order</note> is added, it is spoken thus: **The God of Gods, the Tetragrammaton, has spoken and called the earth** <note>original Latin: *El Elohim Tetragrammatus locutus est*; Psalm 50:1</note>. In this instance, it denotes the Ineffable Name clothed in both grace and severity. 

Sometimes it is read—and this only in the Prophets and the Holy Writings—as the **Tetragrammaton of Hosts** <note>original Latin: *Tetragrammatus Sabaoth*; often rendered as "Lord of Hosts"</note>. In Psalm 46: **The Tetragrammaton of Hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our protector.** This suggests, in this manner, the attribute of judgment. For this reason, the prophets use this style of address when rebuking, directing their words toward severity. You may search more broadly for explanations of this kind in the book *The Gates of Light*, and much more extensively in the book *The Gates of Justice* by **Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla** <note>referred to in the text as Carnitolis, a 13th-century Spanish Kabbalist</note>. 

Furthermore, consider the thirteen attributes of that same Tetragrammaton, which the lawgiver Moses invoked in Exodus 34 in this sense: **Tetragrammaton, Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient, of much mercy and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, taking away iniquity, passing over wickedness and sin, and the innocent shall not be deemed innocent, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children unto the third and fourth generation.** 

I appeal to you here, most excellent men: for I may say this certainly without falsehood, that many studies and words would be needed by anyone who wished to make public all the mysteries of the name Tetragrammaton, of which no end is ever found, just as no end is found of the essence of God. Therefore, leaving aside the proper name of the divine essence, I will show a few of its derivatives. For it is customary, according to the rule of grammarians, that we form common nouns from proper ones. 

These are **El**, **Elohim**, and **Eloha** <note>original Hebrew: אל, אלהים, אלוה</note>, each of which has drawn its origin from the ineffable Tetragrammaton. The Tetragrammaton contains four letters—see, four—and designates the number 26—see, twenty-six—all of which are a single symbol of God—see, one <term>Gematria: A Kabbalistic method where the letters of the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-W-H) add up to 26; here the author adds the 4 letters and the 1 essence to create new combinations</term>. Join these individual numbers, namely four, twenty-six, and one, and it becomes **El** <note>4 + 26 + 1 = 31, which is the numerical value of the name אל (*El*): Aleph (1) + Lamed (30) = 31</note>. If you add the ending of the Tetragrammaton, **Yah** <note>original Hebrew: יה (*Yah*)</note>, to this, **Eloha** <note>original Hebrew: אלוה (*Eloha*)</note> is born. 

Now concerning **Elohim**, it is said that its letter **Mem** <note>original Hebrew: מ</note> is not part of the meaning of the thing, but a grammatical inflection, as is apparent from this: for if it were to be read in a construct state, the letter *Mem* would be missing. Therefore, if you add **El** to the beginning of the Tetragrammaton **Yah** in reverse order, it soon becomes **Elohi**, and by assuming the grammatical declension, which is *Mem* at the end, it will be pronounced **Elohim**. This name is also often written with the letters of the Ineffable Name <note>YHWH</note>, yet it is nonetheless vocalized as *Elohim*. 

In the **Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah: The Jewish mystical tradition focused on the nature of the divine</term>, the use of reversed order is frequent, and its power and the praise of its power are great; for in whatever way the syllables are transposed, the letters remain the same without reduction, although the meanings are often not the same. Abraham mentions this matter in the *Book of Formation* <note>the *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient foundational text of Kabbalah</note>, when he says: **Male and female, male in Emes, and female in Eshem** <note>original Hebrew: זכר ונקבה... באמש... באשם; this refers to the permutation of the three "mother letters" Aleph, Mem, and Shin</note>, where the transposition of letters also indicates a change in the thing. For example, **El** and **Lo** <note>original Hebrew: אל (*El*) meaning God, and לא (*Lo*) meaning "not"</note>, which are "God" and "not." While this is common elsewhere, it is nevertheless profoundly admirable in this Ineffable Name, that no matter how its letters [are moved] here and there...

# BOOK III.

...the Tetragrammaton <note>original: *Tetragrammatus*</note> has shone upon us, and it signifies clemency. It is not much different when **Elohim** <note>Hebrew: אלהים (*Elohim*), a name for God often associated with justice or power</note> is added, and it is said thus: **The Tetragrammaton God of Gods has spoken, and summoned the earth.** <note>original Latin: *El Elohim Tetragrammatus locutus est*; Psalm 50:1</note> In that instance, it denotes the ineffable name of grace clothed in severity. I appeal to you here, excellent men: for I may say this certainly without falsehood, that one would need many studies and many words to publicize all the mysteries of the name **Tetragrammaton**, of which no end is ever found, just as there is no end to the substance of God. Therefore, leaving aside the proper name of the divine essence, I will show a few of its derivatives. For it is customary, according to the decree of grammarians, that we form common titles from proper names. These are **El, Eloha, and Elohim** <note>Hebrew: אל אלוה אלהים</note>, each of which draws its origin from the ineffable Tetragrammaton, which contains four letters—behold, **four**—and designates the number 26—behold, **twenty-six**—all of which are a single symbol of God—behold, **one**. <note>In Gematria, the numerical value of the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-W-H) is 10+5+6+5 = 26</note> Join these individual numbers, namely four, twenty-six, and one, and it becomes **Yah** <note>Hebrew: יה (*Yah*), where Y=10 and H=5, totaling 15. Now regarding **Elohim**, it is said that its **H** is not for the meaning of the thing, but a grammatical inflection, as is apparent from this: for if it must be read through an attachment or a grammatical construction, there is no doubt that it will lack the letter **H**. Therefore, if you add **El** <note>Hebrew: אל</note> in reverse order to the beginning of the Tetragrammaton, **Yah** <note>Hebrew: יה</note>, it quickly becomes **Elohí**, and by assuming the grammatical declension, which is **M** <note>Hebrew: ם (*Mem*)</note> at the end, it will be pronounced **Elohim**. For example, **LA** and **AL** <note>Hebrew: לא (*Lo*, meaning "not") and אל (*El*, meaning "God")</note>, that is, **God** and **not**. Therefore, [even if] they are permuted, they always signify one and the same thing, namely the essence of God, who said, "I am the Tetragrammaton, and I do not change." <note>original Latin: *Ego Tetragrammatus, & nō mutor*; a reference to Malachi 3:6, "I am the Lord, I change not."</note> This will become more manifest to you through use. If the Tetragrammaton is resolved into its twelve variations (for we cannot proceed further), then whatever is arrived at will serve nothing other than the Essence, whose symbols are:
->יהוה יההו יוהה הויה הוהי ההיו ויהה והיה וההי היהו היוה ההוי ;<-
These twelve names, therefore, are reckoned as one name among the Kabbalists <note>Followers of Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition</note>, as signifying a single thing, although there are twelve explanations, for each of which they apply a specific clause from Holy Scripture so that it clearly refers to it through <term>notariacon</term> <note>A Kabbalistic shorthand or acrostic method where the initial or final letters of words form a new word</note>—not for the sake of exposition, but for memory’s sake alone, lest it be forgotten. For instance, if I were to say, "Attend and hear, Israel, today," which is read in Deuteronomy 27:9, in Hebrew it is: שמע ושראל היום <note>original: *Shema v'Yisrael Hayom*</note>. You will note the heads <note>initial letters</note> of these four words, and they make יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-W-H</note>, which is the name of the essence and the resolution of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>; likewise for the others.

But let us remain a little while in the first species of <term>Kabbalah</term> until we have seen certain necessary points of knowledge. For what I have already said had to be taken from the second part. Let us approach this art, if you please, piece by piece and step by step, provided we do not linger too long on each one, so that the day's work passes with the day. Indeed, that which I touched upon before I will now cite again briefly, so that it may stick more firmly: that God before creation was ineffable <note>Beyond description or naming</note>; at creation He was named <term>Elohim</term> <note>The name for God emphasizing His power as Creator and Judge</note>; and after creation, dwelling in the world as if in His temple, He is called אדני <term>Adonai</term> <note>Hebrew: "My Lord"</note>. Hence that is read in <margin>[Psalm] 11</margin>: "The Tetragrammaton is in His holy temple, the Tetragrammaton's throne is in the heavens," as He who rules over His works. For He is, as the Scripture says in Deuteronomy 10: "The God of gods and Lord of lords, the great <term>El</term>." Moreover, "Temple" is a Kabbalistic sign for <term>Adonai</term>, and vice versa through numerical equality <note>This refers to Gematria, where the Hebrew word for Temple (*Heikhal*, היכל) and the name *Adonai* (אדני) both have the numerical value of 65</note>. Just as the ineffable <term>Tetragrammaton</term> is to be venerated in <term>Adonai</term> (אדני) as if in His own temple (היכל), so God is to be loved in God throughout the triple world. In Jeremiah 7: "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord."

There remains another descriptive name, שדי <note>original: *Shadai*</note>, that is, <term>Sadai</term>. In Exodus 6: "I am the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>, and I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob by <term>El Sadai</term>, and my name <term>Tetragrammaton</term> I did not make known to them." Here, only this is called His name which is ineffable, because this title is proper to the Most High God, insofar as He Himself is nothing of those things that exist, but is above all things, having no regard outside of Himself. The rest are descriptive of other properties and relations, such as <term>Sadai</term>, which the Latins were able to translate saying "Almighty," but it is more aptly signified in Hebrew as "Sufficient," "Self-content," and "Needing nothing," which the Greeks more correctly translate as <term>autarkēs</term> <note>Greek: αὐτάρκης, meaning self-sufficient or independent</note>. For *Sha* (ש) means "which" and *Dai* (די) means "suffices" or "is enough," as we say grammatically. Furthermore, if you hear the name <term>Shaddai</term> <note>original: *Sadai*</note> called alone in the sacred texts, let the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> immediately come to your mind, which *pre-eminently* <note>original Greek: κατ’ ἐξοχὴν (*kat’ exochen*)</note> and hyperbolically is called "the Name above every name," however much in speech...

# BOOK III.

[The name is used] for the daily existence of every thing that has being. However, because **Shaddai** <note>original Latin: *Sadai*; the Hebrew name for God usually translated as "Almighty"</note> has no need for the help of another, he appeared to the fathers as **El Shaddai**, that is, in the form of the Strong One who is content in himself. He appeared as the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> as one who is sufficient in himself to perform miracles and wonders. Yet he did not let them know that the name Tetragrammaton is that name in which a man, acting as a co-operator and delegate of God, can perform miracles. Of this, I have written more clearly in **Capnio’s** <note>Johann Reuchlin, the author, often referred to himself by the Grecized name "Capnio"</note> work, *On the Miraculous Word* <note>original: *De Verbo Mirifico*</note>. Furthermore, there is a ministering spirit belonging to Shaddai himself named **Metattron** <note>Metatron, a high-ranking angel in mystical tradition</note>, so named because of an equality of number <note>In Hebrew numerology (Gematria), both "Shaddai" and "Metatron" add up to the value of 314</note>; he is said to be the leader and shower of ways, which we shall discuss more clearly later if you remind me. To this is added another name, **Sabaoth**, which is read in Hebrew as <term>צבאות</term> <note>original: *Tzabaoth*</note>, and thus they are called "hosts" or "armies." Of these, the first rank consists of entirely separate intelligences and angels. The second consists of the movers of the celestial spheres and the assisting powers. The third consists of souls that give form to bodies. This name is not found except following a name of God. Whence it is also read in a threefold way: "Holy, Holy, Holy is the Tetragrammaton Sabaoth," in the sixth chapter of Isaiah and similarly in other places.

You have now heard the status of the entire first part of **Kabbalah** and the instruction by which it proceeds. For since it consists entirely in the changing of sacred words, and any words can be altered in two ways, we must necessarily admit that two species fall under this part: one which is the transposition of syllables or words, and the other which is the equality of numbers.

For example, if I read in Isaiah 40: <term>מי אלה ברא</term> <note>original: *Mi eleh bara*</note>, that is, "Who created these?" and I transponed these two [words] according to Kabbalah, I would turn them into <term>אלהים</term> <note>Elohim (God)</note>. Then the beginning of Genesis would return in action: "God created" <note>original: *Bara Elohim*</note> instead of "Who created these?" so that the meaning stands: "Who created these? God created [them]." And Ezekiel sat by the river **Chebar** <note>original Latin: *Chobar*</note>, that is, by the "influence of the **Cherub**" <note>A type of high-ranking angel</note>, for if <term>כרוב</term> <note>Cherub</note> is transposed, it becomes <term>ברכב</term> <note>meaning "in the chariot" or "by the river Chebar"</note>. And Noah found grace (Genesis 6), for by converting <term>חן</term> <note>*Hen*, meaning grace</note> it becomes <term>נח</term> <note>*Noach*, or Noah</note>. All similar things occur through <term>metathesis</term> <note>The transposition of letters in a word</note> because of the primary confusion of letters that had appeared in the globe of fire; thus it was permitted to draw the letters out as if from chaos and read them here and there, forward and backward. Thus the first species of the first part is completed.

Now I have determined to show something by way of example regarding the approach to the second member of the first part, so that you may understand the matter more clearly and hold it more firmly in memory. One reads of **Isaac** <note>original: *Ishac*</note> and **Rebecca** in Genesis 25: <term>ותהר רבקה אשתו</term> <note>original: *Va-tahar Rivkah ishto*</note>, that is, "and Rebecca his wife conceived." From this, it is granted to us to conveniently divine: what did Rebecca conceive? Surely, as the words indicate, Rebecca conceived <term>אשתו</term> <note>*ishto*, meaning "his wife"</note>. But consider, most learned men, what <term>אשתו</term> might be. In this second species of the first part, through <term>Gematria</term> <note>The Kabbalistic method of interpreting words by the numerical value of their letters</note>, that is, the measurement of numbers, you will find that according to an equality of number, it signifies <term>אש וקש</term> <note>original: *esh v'kash*</note>, that is, "Fire and stubble," for each contains within itself the number 707. Therefore, Rebecca conceived fire and stubble, which the sacred utterances confirm; for the witness is **Obadiah** <note>original: *Abdia*</note>, who says, "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Esau stubble" <note>Obadiah 1:18; Jacob and Esau were the twins Rebecca conceived</note>. Similarly, when we hear that the Law was brought forth in **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: *Hokhmah*</note>, <term>חכמה</term>, let us see what that wisdom is which is suitable for bringing forth the Law. And...

->**KABBALAH**<-

Certainly, there are decrees and prohibitions, commands and forbidden things. However, the symbol is **Wisdom** <note>original Hebrew: חכמה (*Chokhmah*)</note>, which is the Wisdom of all the commandments of God. For when you pronounce the four elements of that word from the proper scriptures, **the spice of life is in it** <note>original Hebrew: חיה בה סם (*chayah bah sam*). Reuchlin is demonstrating a Gematria (numerical) equivalence here.</note>; from these, the number of the six hundred and thirteen commandments of God will be forged together, which our teachers call **Taryag** <note>original Hebrew: תריג; the Hebrew letters Tav, Resh, Yod, and Gimmel sum to 613</note>. 

To summarize this type of speculation: first, it will be worth remembering that the characters, elements, and letters of the Law were stored in a state of confusion and were readable here and there. Second, they were not distinguished by any accents or points <note>referring to vowel markers and cantillation marks, which were added to the Hebrew text later</note>. Third, each primordial letter of the alphabet signifies a specific number, including the five terminal letters <note>the *sofit* forms of Kaph, Mem, Nun, Pe, and Tzadi used at the ends of words</note>, which that wise man **Ezra** invented long afterward along with the points. For there are twenty-two primitive letters, by which alone all scripture was depicted from the beginning; to this day, the Kabbalists locate and dislocate these for the beauty of whatever pleasant contemplation they desire. Finally, we must aim for this universal goal: that although it is the duty of the Kabbalist to read one thing and understand another, everyone must nevertheless inviolably observe this rule—to apply good to good and evil to evil, lest he apply black to white or day to night. 

Then **Marranus** said: "I would think of that kind of art as being no different than if someone called a certain 'Dorotheus' by the name 'Theodorus,' or 'Demonicus' instead of 'Nicodemus,' or 'Philodemus' instead of 'Demophilus.' As the Greeks are accustomed to say, **body-loving and lover of the body**." <note>original Greek: σωματόφιλον καὶ φιλοσώματον (*somatophilon kai philosomaton*). Marranus is suggesting these are just clever linguistic transpositions or anagrams.</note>

To these things **Simon** replied: "Certainly, what you say fits to some extent, but in listing examples you will be exhausted in a very short time because of the poverty of other languages. Compared to Hebrew, which is the fountain of all languages, they are poor and impatient with their own lack, so much so that they must adopt the idioms of other nations. They neither receive the full number of meanings, nor do they allow for useful composition. Therefore, this art cannot be translated into the speech of any other nation at all. If I did not know you were equally skilled in Hebrew, I would have discussed these few things about Kabbalah with you in vain, or would be about to do so now. 

But let us proceed quickly to the second part of this instruction, which is called **Notarikon** <term>Notarikon: a method of shorthand where single letters stand for whole words or phrases</term>, that is, the 'notarial art.' This is a certain convention secretly accepted among Kabbalists so that individual letters, without the joining of syllables, designate certain words, just as is the custom for notaries and clerks. In the past, the secret writings of military commanders, using single letters stored out of order, brought forth the secrets of the mind. There is even a commentary by an honest grammarian, as **Aulus Gellius** writes, quite carefully made regarding the hidden meaning of letters. 

Perhaps the pursuit of this art is no different than if people were to agree among themselves that the letter **Yod** <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often resembling a point</note>, because of the shape of an indivisible point, should denote the ineffable **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, which we commonly interpret as 'Lord.' Just as they are accustomed to mark that very thing with three points because of the three **supernal things** <note>original Hebrew: עליונות (*elyonot*)</note> in the ten numerations <note>The Sephirot, or divine emanations</note>, which are one and the same **Crown** <note>original Hebrew: עטרה (*Atarah*)</note>, symbolized by a single diadem. For the Kabbalists say: **'That for this mystery they write the name with three Yods'** <note>original Hebrew: כי לכוין את כותבו בשלש י וד' אות י; Reuchlin is connecting the three Yods to the concept of the Trinity or the three highest Sephirot</note>..."

### BOOK III.

...as in this <insert>YY</insert> <note>original: יי; a common scribal shorthand for the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> where a single four-letter word is written with three unique letters, which is approved by daily use. There was also once, in the days of Antiochus Eupator, a man named Judas, son of Mattathias—a noble warrior and a leader in the war for the laws, the temple, the city, the fatherland, and the citizens of the Jews. Against them, when Antiochus and his entire army were rushing in, Judas, warned by an angel, gave to his fellow soldiers a "watchword" or military signal. This noble sign was <term>Maccabee</term> <note>original Hebrew: מכבי (M-K-B-I)</note>, so that they might bravely exhort themselves in battle with these four letters. He promised that it would be a sign of God's victory. The Jewish soldiers received this with joyful hearts as a great consolation, and fighting powerfully under that seal, they slew fourteen thousand men in the camp of Antiochus, along with a huge number of elephants and those who had been placed upon them. Thus it happened that the leader of the war, Judas, who was previously called by his own name, was thereafter surnamed "Maccabeus" by everyone, because these four characters sounded syllabically in that way.

And since they believed themselves to have been the victors of so many battles by the power of that sign, the military tribunes and the wise men in Israel wondered, asking Judas in what way so many triumphs had occurred under this sign given to them? Judas Maccabeus responded that in that sign was the presence of the Almighty, Ineffable God. He showed them those words of Moses from Exodus 15, saying: <term>Who is like unto thee among the gods, O Lord?</term> <note>original Hebrew: מי כמוך באלים יהוה (*Mi Kamokha Ba’elim YHWH*). The first letters of these four words—Mem, Kaph, Bet, Yod—spell "Maccabee" (MKBI)</note>. For these four characters designate those words as their initials. In this, the letter *Yod* is clearly understood to signify the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name, YHWH</note>, and <term>Maccabee</term> is truly a memorable symbol for the divine name of 72 letters through numerical equality. Moved by this, those of the army of Judah, fighting again, struck down no fewer than 35,000 men, as the writings indicate; they were wonderfully delighted by the presence of God and blessed the Almighty Lord <term>YHWH</term> in their native tongue.

From this, therefore, you understand that an entire word can be signified by a single letter, whether it stands alone or completes any other word collectively. Just as a whole phrase is said to mark an entire speech equally, as in Daniel 5: <term>Numbered, Weighed, Divided</term> <note>original Aramaic: מנא תקל פרשין (*Mene, Tekel, Pharsin*)</note>. These words represented the following to Nebuchadnezzar <note>Reuchlin attributes this to Nebuchadnezzar, though the biblical account in Daniel 5 identifies the king as Belshazzar</note>: God has **numbered** your kingdom and finished it; it has been **weighed** in the balance and found wanting; your kingdom is **divided** and given to the Medes and Persians.

Either, therefore, one word dispersed through letters creates many words, or many words brought back through certain of their letters collect into one: hence, one from many, and many from one. This is by no means strange, as is shown by the frequent use of two monosyllables; for they say **Maro** <note>The Roman poet Virgil (Publius Vergilius Maro)</note> wrote in his poems: *"Yes and No; all people frequently use these known monosyllables; if these were taken away, there is nothing left of human speech to revolve."* Therefore, almost all conversations of all men signify "Yes" and "No." Why then, in this art, would anyone doubt that an entire word can be noted by one letter, and an extended speech by one word? And vice versa, that some chosen and intended word can be noted by a single speech. From this arises a certain hidden and admirable <term>technology of letters</term> <note>original: *epistolarum techno*, referring to the Kabbalistic method of Notarikon</note>.

-># KABBALAH<-

...logy, which I have often imitated; in times of grave danger and the greatest crisis of affairs, I wrote letters in the German language which I desired to be understood in Tuscany or Etruria by a Latin speaker, and conversely, I spoke in Latin so that a German man, unskilled in the Latin tongue, might not know what I wished. Please accept this, whatever it may be, with a grateful heart and deep feeling; it is no small matter, and you should store it away diligently. It has come to our use, if we operate correctly, that there are four ways of using letters of this kind. 

For they are either taken from the **beginning of a word** to signify something else, as in the opening of Genesis: **"The sixth day. And the heavens were completed"** <note>original Hebrew: יום הששי ויכלו השמים (Yom Ha-Shishi Vayechulu Ha-Shamayim); the initial letters of these four words (Y-H-V-H) spell the Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God</note>, behold the Tetragrammaton. 

Or they are taken from the **end of any word**, such as in Psalm 1: **"Not so the wicked"** <note>original Hebrew: לא כן הרשעים (Lo khen ha-reshaim)</note>, which when put together make **AMEN** <note>original Hebrew: אמן; the final letters of the Hebrew words for "not," "so," and "wicked" are L, N, and M, which Kabbalists rearrange or interpret as Amen</note>. For he wished this to be understood: "Not so the impious," because they will not say "Amen," and for that reason they shall be sent into Gehenna <note>a historical site in Jerusalem used as a metaphor for a place of purification or punishment in the afterlife</note>. 

Or they are **offered individually**, where any single letter represents an entire word, as in Psalm 3: "Many rise up against me." Who are these who rise? The Kabbalists answer: **R, B, I, M** <note>original Hebrew: רב"מי; interpreted as an acronym for the traditional enemies of Israel</note> they are the **Romans, Babylonians, Ionians** <note>Greeks</note>, and **Medes**. 

Or finally, they are used **not in relation to the construction of other words**, but each letter is taken according to the significance of its own property. For example, when mention is made of the two worlds, the **letter Iod** <note>י</note> signifies the world to come, and the **letter He** <note>ה</note> signifies the present world, namely this world. As in Genesis 2: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth **when He created them**" <note>original Hebrew: בה בראם (Be-hibbaram); Kabbalistic tradition notes that the letter 'He' in this word is written smaller in the Torah, suggesting the world was created with the breath of that letter</note>. 

Surely this final consideration of letters pertains to the very substance of the character itself, and not at all to an accidental relationship like the three above. For in this way, by their designation, they signify either things first offered according to Grammatical instruction, or numbers ordered by the discipline of arithmetic <note>referring to Gematria, where letters have numerical values</note>, or certain reasons applied to the words of our masters, or finally, every creature proceeding from the First Cause and reducible back into the First Cause. Regarding the primitive position of the letters, they show it thus:

**Aleph** <note>א</note> is a path or instruction; hence Job 33 says: "I will teach," that is, "I will instruct you in wisdom."
**Beth** <note>ב</note> is a house; Psalm 23: "I will dwell in the house of the Lord."
**Gimel** <note>ג</note> is retribution or reward; Psalm 116: "Because the Lord has rewarded you."
**Daleth** <note>ד</note> is a door, gate, or entrance; Genesis 19: "And they were close to breaking the door."
**He** <note>ה</note> is "behold"; Genesis 47: "Behold, here is seed for you."
**Vau** <note>ו</note> is a hooked peg; Exodus 26: "Their heads shall be hooks."
**Sdain** <note>ז - Zayin</note> is weapons; 3 Kings 22: "And they washed the weapons according to the word of the Lord."
**Heth** <note>ח</note> is terror; Job 7: "You terrify me through dreams."
**Teth** <note>ט</note> is a turning away or declining, by metathesis <note>rearranging letters</note> "thet"; Proverbs 4: "Do not decline to the right or to the left."
**Iod** <note>י</note> is a confession of praise; Genesis 49: "Your brothers shall praise you" <note>The name Judah (Yehudah) begins with Iod</note>.
**Caph** <note>כ</note> is the palm of the hand; Ecclesiastes 4: "Better is a palm full of rest."
**Lamed** <note>ל</note> is doctrine or teaching; Psalm 143: "Teach me to do your will."
**Mem** <note>מ</note> is waters; Isaiah 55: "All who thirst, come to the waters."
**Nun** <note>נ</note> is sonship; Isaiah 24: "Son and grandson."
**Samech** <note>ס</note> is an imposition or placing upon; Deuteronomy 34: "Because he imposed," that is, "placed," Moses laid his hands upon him.
**Ain** <note>ע</note> is the eye; Exodus 21: "An eye for an eye."

Then Philolaus said: "It seems to me that we must become elderly schoolchildren <note>literally "elementary old men"</note> who once again have need of the schoolmaster's rod. For in the meantime, through much study, we have been reduced back to the alphabet."

And Marranus added: "Certainly we are becoming children again; Philolaus, this is that Pythagorean rebirth <term>palingenesia</term> <note>the concept of rebirth or the transmigration of the soul</note> of yours."

To them, Simon replied: "Do not reject it; it is truly a great matter and worthy of philosophers—if you believe your Plato—and not at all ridiculous. As it seemed to Socrates in the *Cratylus*, to know the letters is essential, for he says we have nothing better than this by which we may judge the truth of the first names, <term>since imitation of essence happens to occur through syllables and letters, it is most correct to first distinguish the elements</term> <note>original Greek: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ συλλαβαῖς τε καὶ γράμμασιν μίμησις τυγχάνει οὖσα τῆς οὐσίας, ὀρθότατόν ἐστι διελέσθαι τὰ στοιχεῖα πρῶτον</note>. This is why I think they are called 'elements,' as if they were 'hyle-ments' <note>a pun on the Greek word 'hyle' (ὕλη), meaning matter or substance</note>, which is to say the material things from which the greatest things are made out of the smallest. As Hesiod says: 'If you add a little to a little and put it all together, eventually the heap will become large.'"

"Proceed, Simon," Philolaus said, "for everything you say is true; let us just joke with your permission during this conversation."

Then Simon continued: "Regarding the numbers of the mathematical discipline which are designated by Hebrew letters: there is no other language in the whole world whose letters show any numbers so perfectly. The more recent Greeks tried to imitate the Jews so that they might likewise represent numbers with their alphabet. But it was necessary for them to insert two extra figures for the numbers six and ninety, which are not actually letters from the alphabetic order. For these two signs, ϛ <note>stigma, used for 6</note> and ϟ <note>koppa, used for 90</note>, are inventions of later men led by a desire for imitation, a fact for which the Homeric books stand as witnesses. To be sure, the Romans express only a few numbers with letters; you once read what Priscian of Caesarea <note>a famous 6th-century Latin grammarian</note> wrote on this matter to Symmachus regarding numbers, weights, and measures.

Therefore, let us establish four grades of numbers: the first is of digits (units), the second of tens, the third of hundreds, and the fourth of thousands.

The first grade is noted by the shapes of the alphabet from **Aleph** to **Teth**. There are nine signs, representing the nine numbers individually, as follows:

א ב ג d ה ו ז ח ט
that is: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine.

The second order, that of the tens, also contains nine shapes of the alphabet:
י כ ל מ נ ס ע פ צ
that is: Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy,

# CABALÆ

eighty, ninety. The third level of hundreds contains nine characters: ק ר ש ת ך ם ן ף ץ <note>These are the letters Qoph, Resh, Shin, Tav, and the five final forms: Kaph, Mem, Nun, Pe, and Tzadi.</note> that is: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, seven hundred, eighty, and nine hundred. <note>The text likely contains a typo here; "octoginta" (eighty) should likely be "octingenta" (eight hundred) to match the letter 'Final Pe'.</note> The fourth level is that of the thousands, in which one must return to the shapes of the previous numbers, although they ought to be larger in stature, so that it is called a "Large *Aleph*," as if it were a wide *Aleph*, and they are pronounced with a *pathach* <note>A Hebrew vowel mark indicating an "ah" sound.</note> like an Italian 'a'. Thus, a "Large *Beth*" signifies two thousand. From there it continues up to nine thousand, and finally a "Large *Yod*" signifies ten thousand; in this order, some are accustomed to mark the shapes with points to indicate their stature. Thereafter, they do not use figures but words: *ribbuy ribbot* <note>original Hebrew: רבוי רבבות</note> that is, "thousands of thousands," "twice thousand thousands," and so forth. The Cabalists have most eagerly embraced this path of the numerical alphabet; they say that two thousand years passed before this world was created. This is because before the word *shit* <note>referring to the end of the word 'Bereshit'</note> which is the beginning of the scripture, it places a Large *Beth*, saying: "In the beginning" <note>original Hebrew: בראשית; the 'B' at the start of the Bible is traditionally written larger than other letters.</note>. Thus our wise men explain that passage in Proverbs 8: "The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from that time." Indeed, whatever transcends number is held to be in the place of the infinite. For the limit of numbers in the sacred texts is thousands; as when David wished to show the infinity of a price in Psalm 119, he said: "The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver," which is to say, without number.

We shall now very briefly review the third species of the substance of the letters, which refers to certain intentions of our masters. For instance, **Aleph-Beth** signifies prudence <note>associated with 'Aleph-Binah', or 'Learn Wisdom'</note> to them; **Gimel-Daleth** signifies the rewarding of the poor <note>associated with 'Gemol Dallim'</note>; and **Mem** signifies *Meamar* <note>the Word or Speech</note>, namely, "open speech" and "closed speech" <note>referring to the two forms of the letter Mem: the open 'Mem' used at the start/middle of words and the closed 'Final Mem' used at the end</note>; and so on for the others, which we shall recite a little further below, as they are more frequently used in the Talmudic texts.

The fourth species of these letters consists in all things born and created. This is especially useful for students of Cabala, so that they might more easily lead creations back to the Creator—which is surely the greatest and most singular pursuit in every discipline. I will therefore arrange the letters into several orders, so that each element may be known individually, and thus I begin:

From **Aleph** to **Yod**, the orders or choirs of angels are signified. Philosophers call these "separate intelligences" and "noble, incorporeal, and insensible forms," which proceed and derive from the power of God, who has no form, image, or likeness. For He says in the fortieth chapter of Isaiah: "To whom have you likened me and made me equal?" And a little before: "To whom then have you made God like? Or what image will you set up for him?" Furthermore, this dwelling place is named the "World of Angels" or the "Angelic World" <note>original Hebrew: עולם המלאכים, *Olam Ha-Malachim*</note>.

Then, from the letter **Kaph** to the letter **Tzadi**, the orders of the heavens are designated. These, endowed with power by God the Creator, are administered by the influence of the angels, and this is called the "World of Orbs" or the "World of Spheres" <note>original Hebrew: עולם הגלגלים, *Olam Ha-Galgalim*</note>.

Further, from **Tzadi** to **Tav**, there intervene the four elements with their forms, and all mixed things together, both living and non-living, which depend upon the power of God, and which...

### BOOK III.

[God] flows into existence and life: as it is written in Isaiah, *Creating the heavens and stretching them out, establishing the earth and that which sprouts from it, giving breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those treading or walking upon it.* <note>Reference to Isaiah 42:5. The author is describing how divine energy descends through the levels of reality.</note> These things are directed by the influences of the angels and the celestial spheres; and this whole system is called the **World of Elements** <note>original Hebrew: עולם היסודות, *Olam ha-Yesodot*</note>, and within it is man, who is called the **Small World** <note>original Hebrew: עולם הקטן, *Olam ha-Katan*</note>, which the Greeks call the **microcosm** <note>original Greek: μικρόκοσμος</note>, that is, the "Lesser World"—or more correctly, the "Small World." For within man himself, the properties of all creatures, both the highest and the lowest, are reflected. Perhaps we shall recall these matters more usefully to memory if we demonstrate what the individual letters are held to symbolize; this is indeed a pleasant subject, celebrated by the most ancient authors, lest there should ever be those who mock this art as if it were thin and meager. Therefore:

**א Aleph** is the mark of the highest and loftiest things, which subsist by the first outflow of divine goodness: namely, the angels, who are called the **Holy Living Creatures** <note>original Hebrew: חיות הקדש, *Chayot ha-Kodesh*</note>, that is, the animals of the sanctuary, or rather, lives directly beneath God without an intermediary. These angels, by the power of God, purify, illuminate, and perfect those immediately below them, which in common speech is called their "influence."

**ב Beth**, the second letter, signifies the second grade of angels from God himself, who are called the **Ophanim** <note>original Hebrew: אופנים</note>, that is, "forms" or "wheels"; they are derived in the second place from the power of God through the first intelligence, and they themselves also flow from God into the lower beings. The wise have also said that *Beth* is the mark of **Wisdom** <note>original Latin: *Sapientia*</note>.

**ג Gimel** represents, among the superior essences, the angels who are called **Aralim** <note>original Hebrew: אראלים</note>, that is, great, strong, and robust angels, who descend in the third order from the goodness of the divine majesty. They are illuminated by the power of God through the second intelligence, and they likewise flow into the lower beings.

**ד Daleth** is the symbol of the fourth emanation among the heavenly beings, those who are called the **Hasmalim** <note>original Hebrew: חשמלים</note>; they are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the third intelligence, and by that power, they flow into the lower beings.

**ה He**, this letter designates the superior beings of the fifth emanation from God himself, which are the **Seraphim** <note>original Hebrew: שרפים</note>; they are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the fourth intelligence, and by that same power, they flow into the lower beings.

**ו Vau** marks the essence of the heavenly beings of the sixth emanation, who are called the **Mallachim** <note>original Hebrew: מלאכים</note>, that is, angels; they flow from the power of God through the medium of the fifth intelligence, and by that same power, they flow into the lower beings.

**ז Zain** is the seal of the blessed superior spirits of the seventh emanation who are named **Elohim** <note>original Hebrew: אלהים</note>, that is, "gods"; they are influenced by the power of God through the angels of the sixth order, and by that same power, they flow into the lower beings.

**ח Heth** is the sign of the superior beings of the eighth emanation, and these are the angels called **Bne Elohim** <note>original Hebrew: בני אלהים</note>, that is, the "Sons of the Gods"; they are infused by the power of *El* <note>A Hebrew name for God.</note> through the angels of the seventh order, and they flow into the lower beings by that same divine power.

# THE KABBALA

...eighty, ninety. The third degree, that of the hundreds, contains nine characters: ק, ר, ש, ת, ך, ם, ן, ף, ץ <note>These represent the letters Koph, Resh, Shin, Tav, and the five "final" forms of Caph, Mem, Nun, Pe, and Tzadi.</note>, that is: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred, and nine hundred.

The fourth degree is that of the thousands, in which one returns to the shapes of the first numbers, although they ought to be larger in size; thus, it is called a "Great Aleph" <note>original: *Aleph magnum*</note>, essentially a broad Aleph, and it is pronounced with a *pathach* <note>A Hebrew vowel mark indicating an "ah" sound.</note> like an Italian *a*. Likewise, a "Great Beth" signifies two thousand. This continues up to nine thousand, and finally, a "Great Iod" signifies ten thousand. In this order, some people are accustomed to distinguish the figures by adding marks to the tips of the letters to indicate their size. Beyond this, they do not use specific shapes, but rather words: *rebu rebuaim* <note>original Hebrew: רבו רבואים</note>, which means "thousands of thousands" or "myriads of myriads," and so on.

The Kabbalists have wholeheartedly embraced this system of the numerical alphabet. They say that a span of two thousand years preceded the beginning <note>original: *initium*</note> before this world was made. This is because before the word *shit* <note>original Hebrew: שית, the latter part of the word "Bereshit" (In the beginning).</note>, which is the start of the scripture, it places a "Great Beth," saying *Bereshit* <note>original Hebrew: בראשית, the first word of Genesis.</note>. Thus our sages explain that passage in Proverbs 8: "The Lord possessed me in the beginning of His ways, before He did anything from then." <note>Proverbs 8:22. The author uses this to argue that the letters/wisdom existed before physical creation.</note> Truly, whatever transcends number is considered to be in the place of the infinite. For the limit of numbers in the Holy Scriptures is thousands; for instance, when David wished to show the infinity of value in Psalm 119, he said: "The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver," <note>Psalm 119:72</note> which is to say, it is beyond number.

Now, let us briefly review the third species of the substance of the letters, which refers to certain intentions of our masters. For instance, **Aleph-Beth** <note>א-ב</note> signifies "prudence" or "understanding" to them <note>Likely referencing the Hebrew *Aleph Binah*—"Learn Understanding."</note>, and **Gimel-Daleth** <note>ג-ד</note> signifies "the rewarding of the poor" <note>Referencing *Gomel Dallim*—"One who gives to the poor."</note>. Likewise, **Mem** <note>מ</note>, that is, *Meamar* <note>Word or Speech</note>, represents both "open speech" and "closed speech" <note>Referring to the two forms of the letter Mem: the "open" form used at the start/middle of words and the "closed" form used at the end.</note>, and so on for the others, which we will recite a little further below as they are more frequent in Talmudic usage.

The fourth species of these letters consists in created things and all that is created. This is especially useful for the study of the Kabbala <note>original: *Cabalæ*</note>, so that practitioners may more easily lead creatures back to their Creator—which is indeed the greatest and most singular goal of this discipline. I will therefore arrange the letters into their respective orders so that each individual element may be recognized, and I shall begin thus:

From **Aleph** to **Iod** <note>The first ten letters: א to י</note>, the orders or choirs of angels are signified. The philosophers call these "separated intelligences" and "unbodied, insensible forms," which proceed and derive from the power of God, who has no form, image, or likeness. For He says in the fortieth chapter of Isaiah: "To whom have you likened me or made me equal?" And a little before: "To whom then have you made God similar? Or what image will you set for Him?" <note>Isaiah 40:25 and 40:18.</note> Furthermore, this dwelling-place is named the **World of Angels** <note>original Hebrew: עולם המלאכים, *Olam ha-Malakhim*</note>, that is, the angelic age or world.

Next, from the letter **Caph** to the letter **Zade** <note>כ to צ</note>, the orders of the heavens are designated. These, endowed with the power of the Creator God, are distributed by the influence of the angels, and this is called the **World of Orbs or Spheres** <note>original Hebrew: גלגלים, *Galgalim*</note>.

Furthermore, from **Zade** to **Thau** <note>צ to ת</note>, the four elements intervene with their forms, along with all things—both living and non-living—which depend upon the power of God, by which...
