# KABBALAH

**ט Teth** is the sign of the ninth emanation of angels, who are called <term>Cherubim</term> <note>original Hebrew: כרובים</note>. They receive influence from the power of God through the mediation of the intelligence of the eighth order, and by that same power, they flow into those below.

**י Iod**, the tenth letter, signifies the essence of the tenth emanation of intelligences. These are called <term>Issim</term> <note>original Hebrew: אישים, literally "men" or "individuals"</note>, the noble and patrician ones, who are the lowest of all the hierarchies. They are illuminated by God's power through the ninth choir, and by that same power, they instill in the sons of men cognition, the knowledge of things, and a wonderful industriousness. Hence, those endowed with such a faculty are called "sons of <term>Ish</term>" <note>original Hebrew: איש</note>, that is, men of noble intelligence. Of these, Psalm 49 speaks: *Both the low-born and the sons of men* <note>Psalm 49:2. The author interprets "sons of men" (benei ish) as those of high status or superior intellect</note>, as if to say, both the rustic and the noble. We take our own name from this order of intelligences; for within us, the <term>active intellect</term>—the highest part of the soul, which Aristotle calls the <margin>mind</margin> <note>original Greek: νοῦς</note>—is the only part that comes to us from the outside. From here proceed prophetic visions and all things great and holy. It is called the <term>Active Intellect</term> <note>original Hebrew: שכל הפועל (Sekhel Ha-Poel)</note>, which marks the end of the angelic world. Next follows:

**כ Caph**—this letter designates the <term>Primum Mobile</term> <note>The "First Moved" sphere, the outermost sphere in the medieval geocentric model</note> from <term>El Shaddai</term> <note>God Almighty</note> himself. It is moved by the First Cause immediately, albeit through the spirit of rational life, which is the angel <term>Metatron</term>. He is called the active intellect of the sensible world, providing a path for forms to penetrate all lower things; thus, he flows by divine power into everything that is movable. The **final Caph** <note>The form of the letter used at the end of a word: ך</note> signifies the circuit of the fixed stars, which is called the eighth sphere in relation to us. However, in relation to the higher realms, it is a circle divided into the twelve signs of the Zodiac, which we call <term>Mazalot</term> <note>original Hebrew: מזלות, meaning constellations or signs of fate</note>. It receives influence from the power of God through the medium of the intelligence of Caph itself, and it flows into the lower realms.

**ל Lamed** is the sign of the first sphere of the planets. They are spoken of as if they were "walkers," which the Latins call <term>wanderers</term> <note>original Latin: errones</note>, following the Greeks, for which reason they assert they are <term>planets</term> <note>original Greek: πλανῆτας</note>. It is called the seventh sphere, **Saturn**, a dwelling which we name <term>Shabbatai</term> <note>original Hebrew: שבתאי</note>; it both receives and gives influence.

**מ Mem**, in its open form, denotes the sphere of **Jupiter**, which is called <term>Tzedek</term> <note>original Hebrew: צדק, meaning "Justice"</note> by us. It receives influence from the power of God through the medium of the higher intelligence and flows into the lower things by that same power. The **closed Mem** <note>The final form: ם</note> is the symbol of the sphere of **Mars**, which we call <term>Ma'adim</term> <note>original Hebrew: מאדים</note>, the fifth sphere. It receives God's power through the angel immediately above it and flows into the lower things by that same power.

**נ Nun** signifies the greater luminary, which is called <term>Shemesh</term> <note>original Hebrew: שמש</note>, that is, the **Sun**. Its sphere is called the orb of <term>Chamah</term> <note>original Hebrew: חמה</note>. It receives influence from God through the medium of the sixth intelligence, by which it also flows into lower things. The **final Nun** <note>The form: ן</note> names the sphere of **Venus**, which we call <term>Nogah</term> <note>original Hebrew: נוגה, meaning "Brightness"</note>, and it is illuminated by God's power and flows through the mediation of the seventh intelligence.

**ס Samech** is the symbol of the chancellor <note>Likely referring to the cosmic scribe or messenger</note>, who is called <term>Cochab</term> <note>original Hebrew: כוכב, the planet Mercury</note>...

# BOOK III. 869

In Latin, [this letter represents] **Mercury**; it is influenced by the power of God from the higher realms, and by that same power, it flows into the lower realms.

**ע Ain** is the sign for the sphere of the **Moon**, which we call **Iareah** <note>Hebrew: ירח</note>, and it appears as if it were the left eye of the world. It is the last of the spheres among the stars; and because of its whiteness, it is sometimes named **Lebanah** <note>Hebrew: לבנה, meaning "the white one"</note>. We entrust all these matters to the skill of astrology.

**פ Pe** signifies the intellectual soul, both singular <note>the individual human soul</note> and universal <note>the *Anima Mundi* or World Soul</note>. It is directed by the "separated intelligences" <note>angels or pure spirits existing apart from matter</note> into which it is poured by God, both within the celestial spheres and the stars, as well as in all living things, both superior and inferior, within the spheres and elements. **ף Phe finale** <note>the form of the letter used only at the end of a word</note> denotes the animal spirits <note>the subtle fluids believed to carry sensation and movement through the body</note>, which are directed by the superior intelligences by the power and command of God.

**צ Zade** symbolizes matter, both of the heavens (which is "intelligible" or perceived by the mind) and of the elements (which is "sensible" or perceived by the senses), and of all mysteries. These are directed by divine power through the separated intelligences and through their own specific forms. **ץ Zade finale** shows the forms of the elements, which are fire, air, water, and earth. They are governed by divine power through the angels called **Issim** <note>Hebrew: אישים, the tenth order of angels, often associated with human souls or the "Active Intellect"</note>, and by the power of the heavens, and by the power of **prime matter** <note>the fundamental, formless substance from which all things are made</note>, which is the source and origin of all elements.

**ק Kuph** is the symbol of inanimate things, minerals, and those things called "elementated" <note>physical objects composed of the four elements</note> and mixed. They are directed by divine power through the celestial spheres and the separated intelligences called **Issim**. They flow into the lower things in the region of the four elements.

**ר Res** signifies all vegetation—fruits, crops, and things growing from the earth. They are influenced by the power of God from the celestial bodies and the separated intelligences named **Issim**, and likewise by the complexions <note>the balance of qualities like heat and moisture</note> of the elements.

**ש Sin** designates all sensing creatures, including reptiles of the earth and those that walk, as well as the fish of the waters and the birds of the air together, and whatever irrational beings have vital movement. These are regulated by the power of God through the celestial bodies and the intelligences we call **Issim**, and by the complexions of the elements.

**ת Thau** is the symbol of man and human nature, which is the perfection and end <note>the ultimate goal or purpose</note> of all creatures. Man is directed by God through the complexions and qualities of the elements according to the influences of the heavens and through the specific duties of the separated intelligences, the **Issim**, who are of an angelic condition. And just as the *Issim* are the end and consummation in the world of angels, so man is the end and perfection of creatures in the world of elements—or rather, in the world of all things combined. For he was created from two worlds, as it is written: *The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his face the breath of life* <note>Genesis 2:7</note>.

# KABBALAH

These matters are treated more extensively by our ancestors, whose most burning love for the sacred letters is clearly apparent in their later writings; they even strove to provide a reason for the smallest details. For example, concerning **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet: א</note>, it is written in the book *Ha-Bahir* <note>original: "הבהיר", meaning the "Book of Brightness," one of the earliest and most important Kabbalistic texts</note>, where **Rabbi Amorai** <note>A traditional figure mentioned in the Bahir</note> discussed why **Aleph** is placed at the head of the alphabet. The answer given is that it existed before all things—even before the Law <note>The Torah</note>. **Menahem Recanati** <note>A 13th-century Italian Kabbalist known for his mystical commentary on the Torah</note> mentions this, citing **Rabbi Rahumai**, the author of that book, in his first commentary on Genesis. Furthermore, as to why **Beth** <note>The second letter: ב</note> follows it, it is certainly because it was the beginning of the Law <note>The first word of the Torah, *Bereshit* ("In the beginning"), starts with the letter Beth</note>. And as for why **Gimel** <note>The third letter: ג</note> should not be born from *gidel* <note>Hebrew: גדל, meaning "to grow"</note>, even though in the sacred scriptures "growing" is placed before "weaning" <note>Hebrew: גמל, the root of the letter Gimel</note> in Genesis 21, where it is written: "And the child grew and was weaned" <note>original: "ויגדל הילד ויגמל" (Vayigdal hayeled vayigamel)</note>. Wise men did not consider it beneath them to scrutinize such things and others like them.

However, there are also others in this number who, for the sake of brevity, chose to overlook the explanations for some things and only wrote down what simply pertains to the matter at hand. This is because they always endeavored to hurry toward more sublime things with all diligence and study. Among these is **Rabbi Cohen** <note>Likely referring to Joseph Gikatilla, a famous Kabbalist who wrote on the names of God</note>, in the book titled *The Explanation of the Holy Name* <note>original: "פירוש השם הקדוש" (Perush Ha-Shem Ha-Kadosh)</note>. For concerning the Alphabet, he speaks briefly in this manner:

These things and the rest of their kind which you have heard from the monuments of the fathers, I have gathered as briefly as I could, so that I might offer you at least some taste of the literary profession. For the eminent author **Rabbi Akiba** <note>A leading 1st-century Jewish scholar and a foundational figure in rabbinic Judaism and mystical tradition</note> wrote about these things with great care, and many of our most learned men, whom we deem worthy of much honor, have followed him. For they have said that in the explanation of the Alphabet, many hidden meanings lie concealed. And **Rabbi Abraham Aben Ezra** <note>A celebrated 12th-century Spanish scholar, poet, and philosopher</note>, concerning this in his book entitled *Sod Torah* <note>original: "סוד תורה", meaning "The Mystery of the Law"</note>, that is, *On the Mystery of the Law*, says: "And the truth is that it is good for the intelligent person to learn from this wisdom." <note>original Hebrew: "והאמת כי טוב הוא למשכיל שילמד מזאת החכמה"</note> Yet he also says that we should not labor in the literary art for the whole of our lives, as if we were to be twisted day and night by the volumes of **Rabbi Judah** <note>Likely Judah Hayyuj, considered the father of Hebrew grammar</note>, who is said to be the first grammarian among the Hebrews; or by those twenty books which **Marinus** <note>Jonah ibn Janah, a 11th-century grammarian known in Latin as Marinus</note> composed on the institution of letters; or the twenty-two books which **Samuel Nagid** <note>A 11th-century statesman and scholar in Spain</note> published on the same subject. Thus far Rabbi Abraham Aben Ezra, and this most prudent man, highly skilled in letters, did not feel this way in vain. For we were born for greater and higher things.

I have just spoken of four considerations that pertain to the substance of the letter. Now, in my opinion, we must conclude that which we began a while ago regarding the accidental relation of letters, which is called **Notariacon** <note>original: "נוטריקון", a method of shorthand or forming acronyms</note>. In this part, we consider which letter signifies which word. It has three types. For when it takes a sign from the beginning of a word and (as is customary) is marked with points at the top, it is called *Rashe Tevot* <note>original: "ראש תיבות", meaning "heads of words"</note>, that is, the "head of the expression," and is customarily written thus: ת׳. Likewise, when it is taken from the limit and end of any given word, it is then named *Sof Tevot* <note>original: "סוף תיבות", meaning "ends of words"</note>, that is, the "end of the expression," which they are accustomed to represent in this way: ם׳. But if individual notes are derived from each of the letters of any word, we then call it by the general name **Notariacon**. To these things **Philolaus** <note>A character in the dialogue representing a Pythagorean perspective</note> said: "O our Simon, how secret and recondite these things are to those outside our circle!" Then Simon replied: "Perhaps I shall show you much more hidden things in this third part of the Kabbalah, which is called **Tzeruf** <note>original: "צירוף", meaning "combination" or "permutation"</note>, where there is a mutual substitution of letter for letter, and this occurs as many times as the alphabets are permuted." They are permuted twenty-two times according to the number of letters, because we read twenty-two Hebrew letters. It will always be permitted to take one letter for another by joining any two letters, and that combination is called *Tzeruf*. For example, if from these six letters of the Latin Alphabet, **a b c d e f**, I joined them two by two in succession, so that under the first yoke are **a b**, under the second **c d**, and under the third **e f**, and I wished to urge someone skilled in this art through a letter to fall before the feet of a prince to make a petition. I would write: **d b c f**, which he will understand as **Cade** <note>Latin for "fall" or "yield." By the substitution rule a=b, c=d, e=f, the word "cade" becomes "dbcf"</note>, and so on for others. This whole workmanship arises from the revolution of the alphabet, so that letters mutually succeed one another.

->CABALAH<-

...for a letter combined in its own pair, namely in turn [B] for [A], and [A] for [B], similarly [D] for [C], and [C] for [D], and likewise [F] for [E], and [E] for [F]. This proceeds in the Hebrew language without any obstacle, because the sounds they call vowels are not placed within the sequence of the Jewish Alphabet. <note>In Hebrew, vowels are typically indicated by "points" or marks added to the letters, rather than being letters themselves that occupy a spot in the 22-letter alphabet sequence.</note> Moved by this in an ancient age, our father Abraham said (as is read in the second chapter of the *Book of Creation* <note>original: "Libri Ietzira," referring to the *Sefer Yetzirah*, the oldest known work of Jewish mysticism</note>): "Aleph with all and all with Aleph, and no differently than Beth with all and all with Beth," <note>original: "Aleph cum omnibus & omnia cum [Aleph], haud secus atq; Beth cum omnibus & omnia cum Beth." This refers to the "231 Gates," a Kabbalistic method of pairing every letter of the alphabet with every other letter.</note> and so on for all of them. Therefore, to make this clearer by example, I will bring forward the twenty-two alphabets which Abraham, in that same volume of creation, organized in a proper and useful way.

->### BOOK III<-

This mixture of the twenty-two elements must not be understood in a crude or unlearned way: for all things are spirits. Thus it is written in the *Book of Creation* <note>original: "libro Ietzira," the *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>: "And with that spirit, God carved twenty-two letters: three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples." Each of these is a spirit. These things have been handed down to us to be contemplated spiritually with great joy—not for speaking against or mocking, but for embracing the mysteries of the Scriptures with pious faith. For by believing, we more easily behold higher things through the letters, and we trust that hidden things can be found within them, like the word of God in the midst of the darkness. As He said to Moses: "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you." Furthermore, in **22** <note>original: "כב" (*Kaph-Beth*), the Hebrew numeral for 22</note>, they shall believe forever. For it is necessary for a Kabbalist to believe not like an old woman, but with strength, and to receive the commands of the fathers committed to letters with singular love and a joyful, glad mind—with joy and confidence—as in Psalm 70: "Let them exult and be glad **in You**" <note>original: "בך" (*B-K*). In Hebrew, the word "in You" has the numerical value of 22, creating a mystical pun: "Let them rejoice in the 22 letters."</note>, that is, in the twenty-two, who seek You. 

For you should know that the twenty-two letters are the foundations of the world and of the law, as is treated at length in the second book of the <term>Garden of the Nut</term> <note>original: "Horti nucis," the Latin title for Joseph Gikatilla’s *Ginat Egoz*, a work on the mystical meanings of Hebrew letters</note>, which you have either read or will read. 

Then **Philolaus** said: "Certainly, I have never read nor even seen such books, though I have searched with no small effort until now to find where they might be hidden." 

And **Marranus** said: "I do not know why the Jews are so stingy with books of that kind, such that they will not even freely give them to a friend, or sell them for any price." 

Then **Simon** said: "It is a statute for us that the secrets of the law are not to be given to strangers, but only to a **wise counselor** <note>original: "ליודע חכם" (*le-yodea chakham*)</note>. Not just to a domestic counselor, nor only to a wise man, but to one who is both a wise counselor, who is not an outsider, and who is not unlearned. I beseech you, do not take this poorly. For often, because of imminent danger while we were established in such a long-lasting dispersion, the anxious assembly of the fathers prudently decreed: **'By that law, that he himself might flee from that into which he fell later'** <note>original: "ברה שהוא ברח ממה שגמל בו באחרונה." This refers to a defensive withdrawal or concealment to prevent the misuse of sacred knowledge.</note>. This was on the authority of our Moses the Egyptian <note>original: "Moyse nostro Aegyptio," referring to the philosopher Maimonides</note>, who enumerates the causes and recites the outcomes in chapter 71 of the *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "libri Perplexorum," the *Moreh Nevukhim*</note>. But I hope you will take these and other matters of our people in good part; therefore, leaving aside that dispute, I shall proceed with the third part of the Kabbalistic art."

"You have received, concerning the combinations of letters, two hundred and forty-two permutations and two hundred and thirty-one conjugations, besides the commonly used alphabet; however, they are accustomed to connect each of its two letters in their own order likewise for mutual exchanges. This is a matter commonly considered trivial, and perhaps at first glance despised by the unskilled, but it is one that should nevertheless be highly exalted by men. As is read in Psalm 12: **'Exalting the despised for the sons of men'** <note>original: "כרם זלה לבני אדם." Simon interprets the verse mystically to mean that what seems 'cheap' or 'despised'—like simple letters—is actually of the highest value.</note>. Regarding this, Rabbi Solomon <note>original: "R. Salomon," referring to the commentator Rashi</note> cites there what is said by the Psalmist: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.' I pray you, consider this not carelessly, for it is not written in vain as **Kerem** <note>original: "כרם," meaning 'vineyard' or 'nobility'</note>, for concerning..."

<page-num>874</page-num>
->### KABBALAH<-

<term>Gematria</term> <note>original: "גמטריא," a Kabbalistic method where letters are assigned numerical values to find hidden meanings</note> Kabbalistically signifies two hundred and forty-two; for all the combinations described above are that many, and you should venerate the thirty-one and two hundred variations among them with due honor. For all things that exist and all things that are spoken arise from them. Indeed, concerning those "gates" (as they call them), our father Abraham—as it is written in the <term>Book of Creation</term> <note>original: "Iętzira," or *Sefer Yetzirah*, one of the oldest Jewish mystical texts</note>—said: <insert>Every composition and every creature emerged, and its gift emerged</insert> <note>original Hebrew: "יצא כל חיבור וכל היצור ויצא מתן"</note>. This means that every spoken word and every created thing exists by proceeding from those letters. By their aid, we can easily order ourselves toward our salvation, since we are to be led back, through the contemplation of all created things, to the most immediate and robust knowledge of the one Creator. This is our salvation and eternal life—that is, coming to God through His name, and returning into God.

He Himself is His very name, the four-lettered name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH, often translated as "LORD"</note> blessed forever and ever, which the Psalmist demonstrated when he said: *And they shall know that You are Your name, the Tetragrammaton, You alone supreme over all the earth.* <note>Psalm 83:18</note>. Therefore, this name alone is called the <term>Shem Ha-Mephorash</term> <note>original: "Semhamaphores," the "Explicit Name" or "Explanatory Name"</note>, that is, the name that explains the very essence of God. The proof of this is taken from the first part of this section. 

There is another name of God that takes the place of this one, which is written with twelve letters, and the reasoning for it will be found in the second part. Furthermore, there is another name that is most conveniently treated here in this third part of Kabbalah: the name of forty-two characters. This does not mean that a single pronunciation of one name consists of forty-two letters—for as <term>Rabbi Moses Maimonides</term> <note>original: "Rabi Moyses Mahimoni," the 12th-century philosopher also known as Rambam</note> teaches, no person of understanding would think a single name could be found anywhere written with so many letters. Rather, these are several names complex in themselves and joined together, gathered from many letters. These lead the Kabbalist through certain hidden ratios to the truth of the knowledge of the four-lettered God: *Yod, He, Vav, He* <note>original Hebrew: "יוד הי ואו הי"</note>, which similarly signifies forty-two by arithmetic <note>Reuchlin is referring to a specific way of "filling out" or spelling the names of the letters to reach the number 42</note>. 

These forty-two characters, joined through such names, are called "one name" because ultimately they signify only one thing; just as, conversely, other names composed and collected are often many signifying only one. It could therefore happen at present that the logic by which our intellect is led to God could only be explained with many letters and words. Nor is this surprising, since ingenious craftsmen are accustomed to investigate the source of a spring through many and diverse streams. In the same way, God made all things emanate from the abyss of His fountain and flow back into the infinite vortex. 

<insert>A word went out in a command, and a command in a word, until things were established in the spring of the flame, and the flame in the command in the spring that is beyond searching and beyond number, toward the light hidden in the addition of darkness, concealed within the sum of forty-two letters.</insert> <note>original Hebrew: "יצא דבר במאמר ומיאמר בדבר עד להעמיד הדברים במעין השלהבת והשלהבת במאמר במעין אין חקר ואין מספר ה לאורה המועלמת בתוספת החשוך המוסתרת בכלל ארבעים ושתים אותיות"</note> These are the words of the most contemplative teacher, <term>Hamai</term> <note>Rabbi Hamai Gaon, an early mystical author</note>, in the *Book of Speculation* <note>original: "ספר העיון," *Sefer ha-Iyyun*</note>, to which he usefully cites the *Book of the Fountain of Wisdom* <note>original: "ספר מעין החכמה," *Sefer Ma'ayan ha-Hokhmah*</note>, although a man of such integrity would not have required a witness. Now I shall attempt to see if I am able to interpret these into Latin <note>Reuchlin's original goal, here translated to English</note>, at least so that none of the meaning is lost...

Let it be permitted to the mind. He said: "To produce the thing in the word and the word in the thing, until he might restore all things to the source of brilliance, and the brilliance into the word, as if a source of which there is neither limit nor number, toward the inaccessible light hidden by the increase of darkness in the universe of forty-two letters." <note>This refers to the Kabbalistic concept of the 42-letter Name of God, often associated with the work of creation.</note> Thus far, Hamai. <note>Hamai Gaon is a traditional name associated with early Kabbalistic texts like the *Book of Speculation*.</note> Moreover, the most excellent of the wise (whose memory is a blessing) call this name—so venerable and to be worshipped, designated by forty-two letters—<gloss>Holy and Sanctified</gloss> <note>original: "קדוש ומקודש," *Kadosh u-Mekuddash*</note>.

Therefore, it is hidden from the unrefined and unworthy through the mixing of alphabetical revolution, and was revealed only to the holy who lead a contemplative life, through alphabetical combination, to Jeremiah. He used to read often in the <term>Book of Creation</term> <note>original: "Ietzira," or *Sefer Yetzirah*, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism explaining how the world was created through the Hebrew alphabet</note>, as is found written <gloss>in the Book of Hope</gloss> <note>original: "בספר בטחון," *Sefer Bittachon*</note>, whose author is Rabbi Judah, who composed it. And when Jeremiah studied the *Book of Creation* much and often by night and by day, it is said that a <term>Heavenly Voice</term> <note>original: "בת קול," *Bat Kol*, literally "daughter of a voice," meaning a divine echo or inspiration</note> came to him, ordering him to labor over that same volume for three years. 

After the end of three years, when the conjugation and treatment of the characters finally pleased him, so that he might work with them, a new man was soon created for him and his companions. On the man's forehead was written: <gloss>The Tetragrammaton God is Truth</gloss> <note>original: "יהוה אלהים אמת," *YHWH Elohim Emet*</note>. Then that newly created man, sensing the writing on his forehead, did not delay, but suddenly with a swift hand moved and removed the first letter in <gloss>Truth</gloss> <note>original: "אמת," *Emet*</note>, which is <term>Aleph</term> <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often representing the breath of God or unity</note>. Thus there remained the rest in these words: <gloss>The Tetragrammaton God is dead</gloss> <note>original: "יהוה אלהים מת," *YHWH Elohim Met*. By removing the 'A' from the word for Truth (*Emet*), it becomes the word for Dead (*Met*).</note>. 

At which matter Jeremiah, struck with indignation, tore his garments and said to him: "Why do you take away the Aleph from Truth?" 

He replied: "Because they have everywhere failed in faithfulness to the Creator, who created you in His image and likeness." 

Jeremiah said: "How then shall we apprehend him?" <note>Meaning, how can they return the man to the dust or rectify the situation.</note>

He replied: <gloss>Write the alphabets in reverse in that dust which was scattered, according to the intentions of your hearts</gloss> <note>original: "כתבו אלפאבתיות למפרע באותו העפר הנזרק בכונות לבבכם"</note>. 

And they did so. And that man became dust and ashes in their sight, and so disappeared. Wherefore Jeremiah asserted that he had then received from God Himself the virtues and powers of the Alphabets and the changes of the Elements; for he had known the arrangement of conjugation from the *Book of Creation* before. From there, this Alphabetical <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>original: "Cabala," meaning "Reception" or "Tradition"</note> passed down to posterity, through which the greatest secrets of Divine things are opened. For when we have led that great name (the Tetragrammaton)—which is to be extolled for its greatest powers—around from the last to the first through all combinations of letters, then His Divine knowledge will freely show itself to us. It will offer its powers to our will and mercifully submit them, if He finds us worthy, and with purity of mind, sincerity of faith, [and] of hope...

### ON THE KABBALAH

...provided with the firmness and fortified by the heat of love. For our fathers (as Rabbi Tarphon, Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>original: "Rabi Moyfes Ægyptius," referring to the famous philosopher and jurist Maimonides</note>, and Rabbi Ishmael, and others have written according to the precepts of our Teachers) did not wish to show that name to any mortal, unless he were quite worthy. For they said thus: that it is not handed down except to one who is humble, and who stands in the middle of his days <note>A traditional requirement that a student of Kabbalah be at least forty years old</note>, one who is not prone to anger, nor a drunkard, nor defiled by wicked habits, but a peaceful man, and one who speaks sweetly with fellow creatures, and who guards it with purity; for such a person is beloved above and desired around us below, and the fear of him falls upon all creatures. 

But so that I may reveal that name to you, after the manner of the Kabbalists, I will first divide the forty-two letters into seven words, and then each word into two small sections, each of which contains three letters according to the idiom of the Hebrew language. Therefore, the arithmetic multiplication having been done by saying six times seven, there will be forty-two; namely, the entire collection of letters of that name which I submit to the inspection of your eyes in this script thus:

->צגתבמא שגחחכץ מיחאזב ימיבתא צהגהפץ הגהזמא צאזפפש<-
<note>This Hebrew sequence represents a variation of the Shem Hamuforash, or the 42-letter Name of God, often derived from the prayer "Ana B'Koach."</note>

Indeed, in this verse, while I hasten to include however many letters, the second part of each of the seven words is born as a two-syllable word. For each word of this so precious name is known to consist of six characters, yet only in Hebrew, but not in another language: for in Latin more letters will be needed, such as: **Sagathbama**, **Sagaththecaz**, **Miathazab**, **Iemibatha**, **Zethaghaphaz**, **Thegazama**, **Zazpapas**. These are found in the volumes of the ancients even to this day: nowadays foreign and unknown to the Latin speech <note>original: "Romano sermoni," literally "Roman speech"</note>, but not on that account to be despised because they are harsh and barbarous. 

For let no one use eyes so blurry in the sight of sacred things that he should despise hidden things. Let no one indulge his ears in hearing divine things with such delights that he only honors, praises, and follows those things which are pleasant to the senses, beautiful to the eyes, soft to the touch, and soothing in pronunciation. But let him grasp spiritual things more than physical ones, and constant things more than light ones, and true things more than the superficial. Indeed, often rough and terrifying things precede the presence of God. Remember what happened to Elijah the prophet, when he lay hidden on Horeb, the mountain of God, within caverns and in a cave; was it not said to him thus: "Behold, the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The sacred four-letter Name of God (YHWH), often translated as "The LORD"</note> passes by, and a great and strong wind, subverting mountains and breaking and crushing rocks before the Tetragrammaton; the Tetragrammaton was not in the wind. But after the wind, an earthquake; and the Tetragrammaton was not in the earthquake. But after the earthquake, a fire; the Tetragrammaton was not in the fire. But after the fire, a still, small voice <note>original: "uox submissa tenuis," the famous description of God's presence in 1 Kings 19:12</note>, and in that voice the glory of the Tetragrammaton spoke to him, which is named <term>Glory</term> <note>original: "כבוד," *Kavod*, referring to the Divine Presence or Shekhinah</note>." 

So you, after the desert—harsh and thorny—after the mountain and the rocks, after the wind and the earthquake, after the fire, after the voice in the very vestibule of the caverns and caves, having dismissed the multitude of secular occupations, you shall hear the Glory.

### BOOK III

...of God speaking to you: "What are you doing here? Go further," as it is told in the third book of Kings, chapter 19 <note>In the Latin Vulgate, 3 Kings corresponds to 1 Kings in modern Bibles. This refers to the prophet Elijah at Mount Horeb</note>. Therefore, we must not stand here, but we must return with the prophet Elijah to our own way through the desert—that is, through these bristling revolutions of "barbaric" connections <note>The author refers to the strange-looking letter permutations as "barbaric" because they do not form standard words</note> and tangled briars—into the way of sacred and canonical scripture. This is truly our way, which is the truth of the utterances of God, so that we may anoint the king in Syria who, from his anointing, is called Messiah <note>original: "Messia," from the Hebrew *Mashiach* meaning "Anointed One"</note>. For we shall walk for a while through the combinations of the twenty-two Alphabets until, with vigilant care and tireless diligence, we reach the highest and first Alphabet.

For it is necessary for us to run skillfully through each individual combination until the voice of God lies open, and the text of the most sacred scriptures offers itself openly to us. Indeed, that voice of God rains down its power and value abundantly upon all Alphabets from the first to the last—namely the twenty-second—so that those combinations which are considered "non-signifying" <note>Permutations that do not form recognizable words</note> possess a somewhat greater efficacy than names with primary meanings, just as a ray of the sun burns more strongly than the sun itself from which it flowed. Hence that statement of the Count of Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a famous Renaissance philosopher and pioneer of Christian Kabbalah</note> in his *Conclusions*, where he says: "Every voice has power in Magic insofar as it is formed by the voice of God." 

Therefore, the power, operation, vigor, efficacy, completion, and perfection of this present name of forty-two letters depends on the voice of God, which we intend to hunt through all the connections and nets of all the alphabets, until we are able to find anywhere in sacred scripture the seven names comprised of forty-two letters. For example: If seven words are sought from the first and twentieth Alphabet in the same way, which could be symbols of any verse of divine scripture, let them be set before me just as they were mentioned above. Likewise from the twentieth, and even the nineteenth, and in the same way running through all of them until the first, which received its name from its beginning like the rest, so that it is called אלבת <note>original: "Albath," a cryptographic system where the first letter (Aleph) is paired with the twelfth (Lamed), and the second (Beth) with the thirteenth (Tav)</note>, that is, *Albath*, from whose combination we borrow this example:

For our father Abraham put only permuted and transposed things in that book of creation, since he did not doubt that otherwise the correct order of the common alphabet was known to all. ->אקבהטש אקכבכו טנבשות<-

878 CABALA

The four-letter, ineffable Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> denotes God as He is above all being and represents God as He is in all being; **Adonai** denotes God as the Ruler of all, and **Shaddai** as He who lacks nothing. In like manner, the Name of forty-two letters—whether it is received from transposed or direct combinations—designates God insofar as He is the creator of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. For this reason, both of those three Divine names <note>Refers to the groupings of names just mentioned</note>, each of which is depicted with forty-two figures, are arranged according to the twenty-three Alphabets derived from the first two verses of Holy Scripture: *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and the earth was without form and void.* 

Starting from the first letter **Beth** and ending in the last letter **Beth**, when these are read in Hebrew as they were dictated by the Holy Spirit, they complete the forty-two figures, provided we always place letter for letter under one and the same yoke of combination. There are also other Kabbalists <note>original: "Cabaliſtæ"</note> who, speculating more sublimely, transcend creation and created things to dwell upon the emanation of the Divinity. This they bestow in faithful silence upon worthy men devoted to God through the "Name of the Sanctuary" of characters and through the Name of forty-two letters. This is received and written **in the book of the Epistle of Secrets** <note>original: *Sefer Igeret Ha-Sodot*. This is a pseudo-epigraphical work often cited in Christian Kabbalah to "prove" the Trinity in Hebrew thought</note>, where **Rabbi the Holy** <note>original: *Rab Hakados*, referring to Judah ha-Nasi, the traditional compiler of the Mishnah</note> responded to the question of **Antoninus the Roman** concerning the most holy names. He stated that from the Tetragrammaton flows the name of twelve letters: **Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.** <note>original Hebrew: *Ab, Ben, ve-Ruach Ha-Kodesh*</note>.

From this is derived the name of forty-two letters, which is pronounced thus: **God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, three in one and one in three.** <note>The original Hebrew provided in the text is: *Elohim Ab, Elohim Ben, Elohim Ruach Ha-Kodesh, Elohim Sheloshah be-Echad, Echad be-Sheloshah*</note>. Oh, how great is this height, how great the depth, which is apprehended by faith alone! 

Then **Philolaus** said: "O **Simon**, what great thanks we owe you! You show us everything so lucidly and clearly—if indeed anything in this art can be clear, and if the greater part of these things are not rather locked away in coverings, like 'seeing the sea through the willows' <note>A Latin idiom meaning to see something only partially or obscurely</note>." 

And **Marranus** said: "Be silent, I beg you, **Philolaus**; let him proceed. Do you not see? Evening is drawing near, and he has made this a kind of day-long pact. Therefore, **Simon**, you must speak continually of whatever remains."

Then he [Simon] said: "I have completed the entire art and taught it, unless there are things which you might think remain, little by little, concerning certain names of God, and of angels, powers, and consecrated seals, by whose force and power many have promised to do many things that commonly seem miraculous."

And **Marranus** said: "Perhaps forgetfulness has seized you, for you were also going to speak of the name of twelve letters, even though you affirmed it was the material of the second part, which has now passed." 

Then **Simon** said: "There is little for me to explain about that, except that after the frequent and common [use] by the wicked..."

BOOK III.

...since the name **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Name of God, YHWH</note> was becoming cheapened everywhere through common use. Previously, it had been handed down with such great care and anxiety, with such reverence and such prudent restraint, only to suitable and chosen priests every seven years, so that they might learn to bless the people in the sanctuary through it. At that time, to preserve the majesty of this name, the priests were forbidden from using it in prayers, and its pronunciation was permitted only to the High Priests once a year on the days of fasting and atonement. 

For this reason, they substituted for the others a **Name of twelve letters**, because it was somewhat more sacred than the name **Adonai** <note>My Lord</note>, and yet far less divine than the ineffable Tetragrammaton, which the priests would use in blessings. It was customary for this name to be written in shorthand using these four letters **HKBH** <note>original Hebrew: הקבה</note> with marks on the head of each, and thus it was pronounced: **The Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original Hebrew: הקדוש ברוך הוא, *Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu*</note>. 

Through this substitute, they would later pronounce the blessing over the people from God mandated in the sixth chapter of the book of **Numbers** in place of the Tetragrammaton, like so: "May **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, bless you and keep you. May **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, show His face to you and have mercy on you. May **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, lift His face toward you and grant you peace." 

Regarding this passage, **Solomon of Troyes** <note>Salomon Trecensis, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the most influential medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note>, the regular commentator on Holy Scripture, writes as follows: **Therefore the priests stretch out their hands to say, "The Holy One, Blessed be He, stands behind us," just as it is written: *Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the lattices* <note>Song of Solomon 2:9</note>—that is, from between the fingers of the priests.** 

I hold this written thus on the parchment of an ancient book, although some printed paper volumes lack these words. Our people most firmly believe and in no way doubt that a blessing expressed in this form is the cause of as much prosperity as it would have been if the name **Tetragrammaton** (which they now pronounce as **Adonai**) had remained in those prayers. For this change was made for the honor of the Tetragrammaton, lest by being repeated so often, it should finally fall into neglect—which may God, the Best and Greatest, most especially avert.

You have now the whole **Kabbalistic garden**, that is, the **Pardes** <note>original Hebrew: פרדס, a term for the garden of mystical knowledge, also an acronym for four levels of interpretation</note>, divided into three flowerbeds, which are **Gematria**, **Notarikon**, and **Temurah**; it grows with infinite roots, herbs, and flowers, with all its adornment looking toward one gardener: God, the Best, Greatest, incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnamable. He is the one who waters, plants, and gives growth, and to Him also belongs the incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnamable name, the **Tetragrammaton**, from which flows and derives everything that is holy among holy things. For the remaining symbols, marks, mysteries, and signs of divine things, if any are found, certainly take their origin from this very source. 

For example: **YHWH** <note>יהוה</note> signifies **God is One** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה אחד, *YHWH Echad*</note> by working arithmetically through the first part of this art, **Gematria** <term>Gematria: a method of interpreting Hebrew words by calculating their numerical value</term>, as was explained above; yet that same name **YHWH** symbolically represents...

-># CABALA<-

the **four-letter ineffable name** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> denotes God as He is above all being, and ***El*** <note>original: El</note> represents God as He is in all being, and ***Adonai*** <note>original: Adonai</note> God as the Ruler of all, and ***Shaddai*** <note>original: Sadai</note> as needing nothing. In the same way, the squares of two letters, whether received from transposed or direct combinations, each designate God insofar as He is the creator of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible. For this reason, all those three Divine names—each of which is depicted with forty-two figures—are drawn individually according to the order of the twenty-three alphabets from the first two words of Holy Scripture: ***In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and the earth was without form and void*** <note>Genesis 1:1–2</note>. Starting from the first letter ***Beth*** and ending at the last letter ***Beth***, when these are read in Hebrew as they were dictated by the Holy Spirit, they complete the forty-two figures, provided we always place letter for letter in a swift and uniform yoke of combination. 

Other Kabbalists are found who investigate more closely, transcending creation and creatures and persisting in the very emanation of the Deity. They bestow this most worthily and under a faithful silence to men devoted to God through the holy name of characters and through the **Name of Forty-Two Letters**. This is received and written in the ***Book of the Epistle of Secrets*** <note>original: בספר אגרת הסודות - Sefer Iggeret HaSodot</note>, where ***Rabbi Hakadosh*** <note>original: Rab Hakados; "The Holy Rabbi," usually referring to Judah ha-Nasi</note> replied to the question of ***Antoninus the Roman*** concerning the most holy names, saying that from the **Tetragrammaton** flows the **Name of Twelve Letters**: **Father, Son, and Holy Spirit** <note>original: אב בן ורוח הקדש - Ab, Ben, ve-Ruach Ha-Kodesh</note>. From this is derived the **Name of Forty-Two Letters**, which is pronounced thus: **God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, three in one and one in three** <note>original: אלהים בן אלהים רוח הקדש אלהים שלשה באחד אחד בשלשה - Elohim, Ben Elohim, Ruach Ha-Kodesh Elohim, Sheloshah be-Echad ve-Echad be-Sheloshah</note>. 

Oh, how great is this height, how great the depth, which is apprehended by faith alone! Then ***Philolaus*** said: "How many thanks, indeed, ***Simon***, must be given to you, who show us everything so lucidly and clearly—if indeed anything in this art can be clear, and not rather that the greatest part of these things is shut away in wrappings and seen only by the fortunate." And ***Marranus*** said: "Be silent, I pray, ***Philolaus***; let him proceed further. Do you not see? Evening is pressing in, and this was agreed upon as a daytime task. Furthermore, ***Simon***, speak continuously about whatever the matter shall be."

Then he replied: "I have completed and taught the whole art, unless there are things that you think remain in detail concerning certain names of God, and of angels, and of virtues, and consecrated seals, by whose power and strength many have promised many things that commonly seem marvelous." And ***Marranus*** said: "Perhaps forgetfulness has seized you, for you said you were also going to speak about the **Name of Twelve Letters**, although you claimed it belonged to the material of the second part, which has now passed." Then ***Simon*** said: "There is little that I shall explain about it, except that after the frequent and common use of wicked men—"

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the divine names, specifically how the use of the Tetragrammaton was restricted over time due to its holiness, leading to the use of substitute names and mystical abbreviations in priestly blessings.</meta>

### BOOK III.

Because the name **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton; the four-letter ineffable name of God, YHWH</term> was becoming common and cheapened through everyday use—whereas previously it had been passed down with such care, anxiety, reverence, and prudent restraint only to suitable and chosen priests every seven years, so they might learn to bless the people in the sanctuary through it—it was then forbidden for priests to use it in prayer to preserve the majesty of this name. Its pronunciation was permitted only to the High Priests once a year on the days of fasting and atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>. For this reason, they substituted the "Name of Twelve Letters" in place of the other for everyone else, as it was somewhat more sacred than the name **Adonai** <term>Adonai; "Lord"</term>, yet far less divine than the ineffable **Tetragrammaton**. The priests used this name in their blessings. 

Furthermore, it became customary for these four letters <term>הקבה</term> <note>original: ה"קדוש ב"רוך ה"וא - Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu</note>, marked with shorthand points above each head, to be written and thus pronounced as **The Holy One, blessed be He** <note>original: הקדוש ברוך הוא</note>. Through this, they later performed the blessing over the people commanded by God in the sixth chapter of Numbers in place of the **Tetragrammaton**, speaking thus: "May **the Holy One, blessed be He**, bless you and keep you. May **the Holy One, blessed be He**, make His face shine upon you and be merciful to you. May **the Holy One, blessed be He**, lift up His face toward you and give you peace." 

In this passage, **Solomon of Troyes** <note>Salomon Trecensis, better known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator</note>, the standard commentator on Holy Scripture, writes: <term>The priests spread their hands to say, 'The Holy One, blessed be He, stands behind us, looking through the windows'—this refers to 'Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the lattices' of the priests.</term> <note>original Hebrew: לבד הכהנים פורסים בידיהם לומר הק ב ה עומד אחרינו , מבין החלונות : שנו הנה זה עומד אחר כותלינו משגיח מן החלונות מציץ מן החרכים של כהנים</note>. This means: Therefore the priests stretch out their hands, saying, **The Holy One, blessed be He**, stands behind us, just as it is written: *Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows* <note>Song of Solomon 2:9</note> between the fingers of the priests. I hold this written thus on the parchment of an ancient codex, although certain printed paper volumes lack these words. 

Our people most firmly believe, and in no way doubt, that a blessing expressed in this form is the cause of as much prosperity as it would have been if the name **Tetragrammaton** (which they now pronounce as **Adonai**) had remained in those prayers. For this change was made to honor the **Tetragrammaton**, lest by being repeated so often it should eventually fall into neglect—which may God, the Best and Greatest, most especially avert. 

You have here the entire Kabbalistic garden, that is, **Ginat** <note>Hebrew: גנת (GNT), a garden; also an acronym for the three methods: Gematria, Notarikon, and Temurah</note>, divided into three flowerbeds: **Gematria** <term>Gematria; calculation of the numerical value of letters</term>, **Notarikon** <term>Notarikon; using letters as shorthand for words or acrostics</term>, and **Temurah** <term>Temurah; the permutation or exchange of letters</term>. This garden grows with infinite roots, herbs, and flowers, and with all its adornment looks toward one gardener who waters, plants, and gives increase: God, the Best, the Greatest, the Incomprehensible, the Ineffable, the Unnamable, whose name is also the incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnamable **Tetragrammaton**. From Him flows and derives everything that is sacred among the sacred. For all other symbols of divine things, marks, sacraments, and signs, if any are found, certainly take their origin from this very source. For example, **YHWH** <note>original: יהוה</note> signifies **The LORD is One** <note>original: יהוה אחד</note> by working arithmetically through the first part of this art, **Gematria**, as was explained above; yet that same name **YHWH** symbolically represents...

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the divine names, moving from the restriction of the Tetragrammaton to the Kabbalistic methods of interpreting it through letter permutations and numerical values (Gematria), specifically focusing on the tension between God’s absolute unity and the plural forms used in scripture.</meta>

### KABBALAH

...represents the complete name **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton; the four-letter ineffable name of God, YHWH</term> themselves through the second part of the Kabbalah, as Joseph son of Abraham <note>Joseph Gikatilla (1248–1305), a prominent Spanish Kabbalist</note>, a citizen of the district of Jerusalem, writes in the second volume of the *Garden of the Nut* <note>original: "Ginnat Egoz," a foundational work on the mystical meanings of Hebrew letters and vowels</note> with these words: **Yod He Vav He** <note>original: יוד הי ויו הי; the full spelling or "filling" of the four letters of the Name</note>. That is to say, **Yod** is its replacement... so **He** is its replacement **Vav**, and so **Vav** is its replacement **Zayin** <note>original: "sdain," likely a corruption of Zayin</note>, by which we observe that God is one and most unified in His essence, than which nothing is more "one." Nevertheless, many things are said of Him according to other relationships, because of which He is called **Elohim Kadoshim**, that is, the **Holy Gods** in the book of Joshua <note>Joshua 24:19</note>, and **Elohim Haijm**, that is, the **Living Gods** in Deuteronomy 5. And in Malachi, He speaks of Himself thus: "And if I am **Masters** <note>original: אדונים - Adonim, a plural form of Lord</note>, where is my fear?" In this place, God calls Himself by the plural "Masters." According to His immanence <note>His internal, unchanging nature</note>, therefore, He is one; but according to His outpourings <note>His manifestations or emanations in the world</note>, He is many. It was according to this plurality, therefore, that He spoke when He said, "**Let us make man in our image and likeness**" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. 

This was not merely a custom of the Holy Language <note>Hebrew</note>—that those established in the highest majesty should speak of themselves in the plural—as Rabbi Saadia <note>Saadia Gaon (882–942), a famous Jewish philosopher and scholar</note> writes in the book *Beliefs and Opinions* <note>original: "Emunot ve-Deot"</note>. For that is a weak argument, since shortly afterward God Himself speaks in the singular, saying: "**I will make for him a helper like himself**" <note>Genesis 2:18</note>. 

The Kabbalists do not unwillingly admit this unity and this plurality in divine matters through various reasonings, which is why they assert that the first three Kabbalistic numerations <note>The Sephirot: Keter (Crown), Chochmah (Wisdom), and Binah (Understanding)</note>—**Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding**—are the one crown of the supreme King, as Rabbi Asher <note>original: "Rab Assen," likely referring to Rabbi Asher ben Yehiel or Azriel of Gerona</note> writes in the book *Unity* <note>original: "Yichud"</note>, a singular work on unions or collections.

You see from this example that we use all parts of the Kabbalah back and forth and mixed together: namely, the entire transformation of letters, syllables, and words; then numerical calculation <term>Gematria; the practice of calculating the numerical value of Hebrew words</term>, shorthand notation, and literal mutation with each of the species I placed in my earlier discourse. For we transpose the name **Tetragrammaton** so that it varies. **YHWH** <note>original: יהוה</note> is "Essence," which is the first of all things, from which come all beings that are true and good. Hence, **Ehieh Adonai** <note>original: אהיה אדני - "I am the Lord"</note> signifies numerically exactly as much as **Elohim** <note>original: אלהים - "God"</note>, the sum of which is 86. Just as the word **Kos** <note>original: כוס - "Cup"</note> is also a notation for this **Elohim**, if it is extended thus: **Aleph, Lamed, He, Yod, Mem**, it equals 86. And the name **Tetragrammaton**, because it makes 26—but if it is expanded to **Yod, Vav, He, Vav** <note>original: יו הו - a specific Kabbalistic expansion of the Name</note>—it makes and designates **Tetragrammaton Elohim**, which is **Lord God**. Concerning this, it is first written: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the **Lord God** <note>original: "Tetragrammatus Elohim"</note> made the earth and the heavens."

Furthermore, the beginning of the name **Tetragrammaton** is **Yah** <note>original: יה</note>. And the middle of **Elohim** itself is **Yah**, and the end of **Ehieh** <note>I Am</note> is **Yah**. The whole of this is the perfection of **Yah** itself, which is of "Essence," signifying **Living** <note>original: חי - "Chai"</note>—that is, "Himself"—and **Yah** is the "Divine Being." Indeed, it is common in daily use to say that "Being" itself is something divine, celestial, and incorruptible. For everything that exists, when it exists by limited grace, must necessarily be, nor can it then happen not to be. Therefore, the power of that Essence was led into operation through the Word of God, who said, "**Yehi**" <note>original: יהי - "Let there be"</note>, by which word the universal Ideas and powers were created in the highest...

...most absolute intellectual realities, through the fact that he himself commanded thus, "Let there be light" <note>original: "Fiat lux"</note>, and soon light was made. This universality was followed by the nature of the angels assigned to ministries, when he said **Yehi khen** <term>יהי כן; "Let it be so"</term>, which designates the prince and great priest named Michael, a bright proof of the angelic condition, which is composed of unity and the number one hundred <note>Michael’s name in Gematria is 101, combining 1 (unity) and 100</note>. Hence they believe that on the first day, the Ideas were produced outside the First Cause as most absolute forms, both in terms of being and acting. But on the second day, the angels were created from here. For on the first day He did not say **Vayehi khen** <term>ויהי כן; "And it was so"</term>, but on the second day, when the firmament of heaven was made, according to Rabbi Eliezer <note>Eliezer ben Hurcanus, a 1st-century sage; this refers to a passage in the "Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer"</note>, they were created from the light of His garment. For God was clothed in ten garments when He created the world, as the Kabbalists say, and from the light of His last garment He took and created the heavens—not indeed those perceived by the senses, but those invisible and intellectual **ruchaniyot** <term>רוחניות; spiritual entities</term>, of which the Psalmist says, "The heavens declare the glory of God," where it is not written **shamayim** <term>שמים; heavens</term> (which are the spherical ones, as Rabbi Ama memorably noted in the *Book of Secrets* regarding Psalm 19), but **Ha-shamayim** <term>השמים; "The Heavens"</term>, to which the article *ha* is added, as is read in the summary argument of Genesis: "In the beginning God created **Hasamaim**" <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. That is, those distinguished heavens, those world-renowned ones, those wonderful ones, never seen nor to be seen by mortal eyes. For other heavens, which are not written with the article *ha*, are indeed the firmament, yet they are called by the name "heaven," wherefore it is written, "And God called the firmament heavens." And the firmament of that same invisible heaven is itself invisible, and it is that which is called the "Heavens of heavens." From this follows the phrase: "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven" <note>Genesis 1:14</note>. Surely that extension in the manner of a skin <note>Referring to Psalm 104:2, comparing the sky to a stretched-out tent or hide</note>, as if inscribed with letters by the lights and stars, is called **rakia** <term>rakia; an expanse or firmament</term> because of its local expansion, which we call "firmament" from the word for firmness.

For the invisible heaven did not need lights, since it is spiritually illustrious through itself, and is mentally illuminated by the First Cause. Therefore they are named "separate intelligences" <note>A medieval term for angels as purely intellectual beings without physical bodies</note>, of which the author of *The Book of Causes* says: "Every intelligence is full of forms," which, while it understands, is said to hear and speak. Wherefore Moses says: "Hear, O heavens, what I shall speak" <note>Deuteronomy 32:1</note>. And David: "The heavens declare the glory of God." And God says in Hosea: "I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth" <note>Hosea 2:21</note>. From here descends the prophetic light which is called **ispaklaria ha-me'irah** <term>אספקלריא המאירה; the shining mirror</term>, which was the vision belonging to Moses. For the vision of other prophets was an **ispaklaria she-einah me'irah** <term>אספקלריא שאינה מאירה; a mirror that does not shine</term>, and that is called "earth." Some mention of these was made in the first discourse. Indeed, I seem to believe rightly that for this reason our sages said: "The appearance of Moses was like the appearance of the sun, and the appearance of Joshua was like the appearance of the moon."

In the creation of sensible things, therefore, God uses this symbol of intellectual things, **Yehi khen** <term>יהי כן; "Let it be so"</term>, so that the ministry of angels might be designated as concreated with natural things under the common name of Michael—as if it were a title for the angelic species—which, through that phrase **Yehi khen** repeated in the following five days of works, according to the first part of the Kabbalistic art, equal...

# KABBALAH

...by the plurality <note>original: "litate," likely "pluralitate"</note> of the number it is symbolically signified, through which we are taught that all angels are of the same species. Furthermore, all individual bodies, whether celestial or earthly, have their own governors of virtues and prefects of operations—both those that are rational, such as the heavens, stars, and men, as well as those that are irrational, such as beasts and elements. For it is first proven to the Peripatetic <note>Followers of Aristotle</note> philosophers that every spherical heaven, besides its essential form, has an attendant intelligence which moves its sphere. This is called an "angel," because it is sent for this duty, and being intelligent and volitional, it fulfills the commands of the Creator, acting as a mediating power between God and nature. Through this power, operations occur in things that their own nature either would not perform, or would not perform in that specific way—things which some say arise from a "hidden property" and others simply "because it is so." 

For although the motion of the heavens and stars is naturally circular, to be moved from the east to the west or vice versa is not a matter of nature, but of will. Now, an angel has free will, while nature is confined to a certain instinct alone, so that it always acts in the same way. However, angels do not always move the spheres in the same way. Consequently, changes in these lower things do not always happen in the same way. Indeed, the angelic condition exerts the greatest force and power over corporeal things. For this reason, the "agent intellect" <note>In medieval philosophy, the bridge between the divine mind and human reason</note> from which forms flow is called an "angel," as Rabbi Moses Maimonides <note>The 12th-century philosopher and physician also known as Rambam</note> testifies. It is named **Sar shel Olam** <term>שרי של עולם; "Prince of the World"</term>, as our wise men have said, and is called Metattron <note>Metatron, one of the most significant archangels in Kabbalistic tradition, often described as the celestial scribe or the lesser Yahweh</note>, by whom all individual human, animal, and natural virtues are governed, which are likewise called angels. To us, their multitude is infinite, but to the Creator, it is certain, delimited, and finite. 

The *Bereshit Rabbah* <note>An ancient Jewish commentary on the Book of Genesis</note> mentions this, where it is read that the Creator daily creates a company of angels, whom they call "forms," because they are formal substances with which the entire sphere of things subject to birth and decay is filled without number. Nor does your own Hesiod <note>An early Greek poet</note> differ, for in *Works and Days* he says: "For there are thrice ten thousand upon the much-nourishing earth, immortals from Zeus, guardians of mortal men, who indeed watch over both justice and cruel deeds, clothed in mist, roaming everywhere over the earth" <note>original Greek: "τρὶς γὰρ μύριοί εἰσιν... αἶαν"</note>. 

In a similar fashion, they name two powers of the will in man as two angels: **Yetzer Tov** and **Yetzer Ra** <term>יצר טוב ויצר רע; "the author of good and the author of evil"</term>, as is read in the *Midrash Tanchuma* <note>A collection of homiletic teachings on the Torah</note>, which Rabbi Assé <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama, or perhaps a reference to the collector of these sayings</note> cites in his collection. The Latins call such Hesiodic guardians "spirits" associated with the body. Whosoever of these is destined for the care of lower affairs is called "Mamona" or "Mamon," whom the Greeks call "daemona" or "daemon," though not in a bad sense. Certainly...

### BOOK III.

...there is indeed one thing called a demon, and another a *daemonium* <note>original: *dæmonium*, a Greek diminutive form</note>, which we consider to be a term that diminishes divinity; for this reason, it is excluded from divine things as a lesser term. However, I plainly confess that for *Homer* and the most ancient writers, there was another use for that word. Many of them spoke with praise and veneration regarding the *daemon* of *Socrates* <note>Socrates famously claimed to be guided by a *daimonion*, an inner divine voice</note>, which *Apuleius* interpreted as "the god of Socrates." But what the Latins called "Spirits," in the manner of winds, took its origin from us, who call them *Ruchot* <note>original: רוחות (*ruchot*), the Hebrew word for both "winds" and "spirits"</note>. Regarding these, *Rabbi Todros Levi* <note>original: *Rabi Tedacus Leui*, likely referring to the 13th-century Kabbalist Todros ben Joseph Abulafia</note>, in his book on the *Ten Sephirot* <note>original: *Decem numerationibus*, referring to the ten emanations of God in Kabbalah</note>, after explaining the four winds—north, south, east, and west—finally writes thus: "And for those four winds He created four angels who are appointed over them by day and by night."

Then it follows, by the same author, that *Michael*, who is of the side of clemency and compassion, is established as the *Mammona* <note>In this context, a "steward" or "overseer," from the Aramaic word for wealth/possessions</note>—that is, the prefect—over the eastern wind until the middle of the day, and until the night. And *Raphael* rules the western wind, who is similarly of the side of clemency. Then *Gabriel*, in the power of judgment and severity, is appointed with the northern wind over the middle of the night and two measures of the world; *Noriel* <note>Often identified with Uriel</note>, however, presides over the south. Thus far *Todros Levi*.

Furthermore, those angels have many species under them, which the book *Sodot* <note>original: סודות (*Sodot*), meaning "Secrets"</note> contains. And in the *Gates of Light* <note>original: *Porta lucis*, the Latin title for Joseph Gikatilla’s *Sha'are Orah*</note>, it is read thus: "For from the earth even unto the firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of spiritual forms. Some of them are pure; some are capable of grace and compassion; and there are below many foul, harmful, and accusing creatures, and all of them dwell and fly in the air. And from the earth even unto the firmament there is no empty place, but the whole is filled with multitudes of them: some for peace, some for war, some for good, some for evil, some for life, and some for death. And all this is in the lower habitation in which we exist." These are the words of *Joseph of Castile* <note>referring to Joseph Gikatilla</note>.

But far be it from our holy purpose that we should proceed to dispute much about those filthy and most base demons, those enemies of the human race, who are called "contrary powers." Some are thought to wander through the upper region, being fiery; some wander in the air near to us; some are terrestrial and terrify the earth; some inhabit lakes and rivers and often shake the sea itself. Others are subterranean and sometimes attack those who dig wells and mines; likewise, they provoke chasms in the earth, stir up flame-vomiting winds, and shake the foundations. Finally, there are those who flee all light and splendor—unfathomable and entirely dark spirits—who vex not only the human race, but even the brute animals...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual forces and their influence on the human world. While the previous page categorized spirits according to the four winds and their angelic overseers, this page transitions into "Practical Kabbalah"—the use of sacred names, symbols, and amulets to protect against malevolent forces and human plots.</meta>

### ON THE KABBALAH

...pressing in with a noise. Against their machinations there are some of our people who consider themselves experienced in many things, and they do not hesitate both to draw in good spirits by soothing them, and to repel malignant ones with opposing passions, being duly supported by sacred and divine names and characters. They command a man who is to be exposed to future dangers to take a very thin membrane, which is called "virgin" <note>original: *virginea*; parchment made from the skin of a stillborn or young animal, symbolizing purity</note>, as it is sincere, clean, and immaculate, so that it may portend the purity of the practitioner. Then, they should inscribe these characters thus:

צבורכח <note>original: *Tz-B-V-R-K-Ch*; a Kabbalistic acrostic</note>

But on the outside, on the rougher part of the leaf, these signs also:

בייוי <note>original: *B-Y-Y-V-Y*</note>

by which binding they command that one who hopes most firmly in God, the creator of the universe, should fear no machinations of perverse men. They reveal the mystery in this way: for these are symbols of the first five verses of Genesis, containing both the beginnings and the ends <note>A technique called *Notarikon*, where the first or last letters of words in a verse form a new word or name</note>, according to the second part of the Kabbalistic art. 

*Costa Ben Luca* <note>A 9th-century Syrian Christian physician and scholar known for his works on medicine and talismans</note> once wrote concerning "physical ligatures" <note>original: *ligaturis*; amulets or charms tied to the body</note> things that were not physical, yet were proven by experience (as they believe). He said: "If the little finger of an aborted fetus is hung from a woman's neck, she will not conceive as long as it clings to her neck." But now, would anyone think (they say) that the words by which the Almighty Creator made heaven and earth have no power when bound [as an amulet]? 

Indeed, the men of my sect certainly place much faith in the great master *Rabbi Ashi* <note>original: *R. Assé*; likely referring to the 5th-century scholar and primary editor of the Babylonian Talmud</note>, who wrote in the *Book of Unity* <note>original: *Sefer Ha-Yihud*</note> that one wishing to seek and obtain his desires should turn himself toward the clemency and mercies of God by using these characters: 

אגלאפז פתחם פסטם דיינוסים <note>original: *AGLA-PZ PTChM PSTM DYNVSYM*; these are often derived from the initials of Hebrew prayers or verses</note>

which are found to be worthy memorials of the Holy Scripture; and there are many other such things with which nearly all the books of the Kabbalists are filled. Others also study how to fashion illustrious seals from the divine letters, which, having been proven by long use, might prevail against human infirmities and other troubles. For example, there is that seal which *Rabbi Hama* <note>A legendary figure to whom many early Kabbalistic texts, like the *Sefer ha-Iyun*, were attributed</note> composed in the *Book of Speculation* <note>original: *lib. Speculationis* or *Sefer ha-Iyun*</note> from four names—not magical ones, but solemn and common sacred names—or rather, he received it as composed by the fathers:

יהוה אדני יואו אהיה <note>The names: Y-H-V-H (the Tetragrammaton), Adonai (Lord), Y-V-A-V (a variant of the name of God), and Ehyeh (I Am)</note>

However, in the Kabbalistic way, *Y-V-A-V* <note>original: יואו</note> is the same as *El* <note>original: אל; the Hebrew word for "God"</note>. The craftsmen of this science, therefore, take the first character of the first name, the first of the second, the first of the third, and the first of the fourth, and let the first seal be:

יאיא <note>original: *Y-A-Y-A*</note>

Then they work in a similar way concerning the second letters of the four most sacred names, and there arises:

הדיוא <note>original: *H-D-Y-V*</note>

They fashion the third seal thus: they join each of the third letters, and there is born:

ואאי <note>original: *V-A-A-Y*</note>

Finally, in the same manner, they couple the last letters, and the fourth seal emerges, which is:

היהה <note>original: *H-Y-H-H*</note>

The intention of these four seals is: 

יהוה אלהינו יהוה אחד <note>original: *Adonai Eloheinu Adonai Echad*</note>

that is, "The Lord our God, the Lord is one" <note>The *Shema*, the central declaration of Jewish faith</note>; and let this (they say) be the inscription of the four seals joined together. Finally, on the back of the parchment they depict this:

אראריתא <note>original: *Ararita*</note>

which is interpreted as: 

אחד ראש אחדותו ראש ייחודו תמורתו אחד <note>original: *Echad Rosh Achduto Rosh Yichudo Temurato Echad*</note>

that is: "One, the Principle of His unity, the Principle of His singularity, His Permutation, One." And this literary permutation is understood according to the third part of the Kabbalistic art. And so they stand with the seals...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Practical Kabbalah, shifting from physical amulets to the power of sacred speech, prayers, and the philosophical justification for why certain symbols and names hold power over the physical and spiritual worlds.
