### BOOK III

...and with inscriptions before the Almighty with a soul devoted to God; and whatever blessing they might ask for from those eighteen blessings <note>The *Shemoneh Esreh* or *Amidah*, the central prayer of Jewish liturgy</note>, or those contained in other righteous prayers, they hope to obtain it without fail. They are confident that they can often break every fate looming from heaven, or mitigate *Adrasteia* <note>original: *adrastiam*; a Greek term for the personification of inescapable fate or the "inevitable power" of divine retribution</note>—that is, the inescapable power of divine laws—through the prayers of sacred words. 

For they believe a Kabbalist who is well-initiated not only in characters and figures, but also in words and chants, can perform any number of wonderful things, which some of your own people also admit can be done. For Plotinus, in the thirty-fifth chapter of the second book of *On the Doubts of the Soul*, lists four things in which a miraculous power resides: namely, the occult qualities of species, figures, harmonies <note>original: *concentus*; musical or mathematical proportions</note>, and vows. Porphyry and Iamblichus <note>Influential Neoplatonist philosophers who explored theurgy, or "god-working" rituals</note> also say that through God specifically, and through good angels, we have command over the lower spirits. Nor is there any race of men in the whole circuit of the world who more easily fall into this opinion than the more divine Christians (as the story goes), who cast out demons with names and figures, and lay hands upon the sick and they recover, heal the deadly, and perform similar miracles. 

But (to speak the truth as they assert it), they attribute all these things rather to faith, although they also think some power is inherent in prayers. For they say, and believe, that the "prayer of faith will save the sick" <note>A reference to the New Testament, James 5:15</note>. Nor do skilled Kabbalists feel otherwise; they likewise affirm that miraculous operations depend on God alone and on the faith of the man. Therefore, they declare those to be liars and fools who grant such great force and power of miracles to the figure alone, to the writing alone, to the outlines alone, or to voices alone born of "broken air" <note>original: *aere fracto*; a technical term for sound waves or speech</note>, as Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>The great philosopher Maimonides (1135–1204)</note> testifies in the seventy-second chapter of the first book of the *Guide for the Perplexed*. 

To these things, Philolaus says: "Not only the Kabbalists of the Hebrews, but also the most excellent of the Greeks, attributed much to the tokens and seals of faith." For Antiochus, surnamed Soter <note>Antiochus I Soter (reigned 281–261 BC), a king of the Seleucid Empire</note>, when he was on an expedition against the Galatians—brave men fortified by an innumerable gathering of soldiers—and was about to join a most difficult battle, when, as Lucian writes of him, *he had entirely miserable hopes* <note>original: *πάνυ πονηρὰς εἶχε τὰς ἐλπίδας*</note>, saw in a dream at night Alexander <note>Alexander the Great</note> standing by him, ordering him to proclaim to his soldiers before the fight a certain sign of Health <note>original: *Sanitatis*</note> as a military password, through which he promised victory would fall to him. It was of such a kind that it should be marked on their clothing, as the same man of Samosata <note>Lucian of Samosata, a 2nd-century satirist and rhetorician</note> noted concerning the error in greeting: *a triple triangle intersecting one another, the five-lined figure* <note>original: *τριπλοῦν τρίγωνον δι᾽ ἀλλήλων τὸ πεντάγραμμον*; this describes the pentagram</note>—that is, a triple triangle of five lines between themselves. Antiochus, having raised that sign, obtained a miraculous victory over the Galatians.

I myself have indeed often seen that symbol of the pentagon struck on the silver coinage of Antiochus, which when resolved into lines shows the word *HEALTH* <note>original: *Υ Γ Ι ΕΙ Α* / *ὑγίεια*; Hygieia, the Greek goddess of health and the word for well-being</note>, or (which is exactly the same), health, that...

<summary>This page discusses the power of sacred prayers and symbols, arguing that their efficacy depends on faith and God rather than the mere physical objects themselves. It cites both Neoplatonic philosophers and the historical example of King Antiochus’s use of the pentagram (the "Health" sign) to illustrate the cross-cultural belief in protective seals.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between Marranus (a Christian) and Simon (a Jewish Kabbalist), shifting the focus from the general power of words to specific historical signs and the "Explicit Name" of God. It bridges the gap between the Jewish Tetragrammaton and the Christian name of Jesus through the use of mystical symbols and numerical calculation.</meta>

### OF THE KABBALAH

<image-desc>A rectangular frame containing a five-pointed star (pentagram) with the Greek letters Υ, Γ, Ι, Ε, ΙΑ <note>These letters spell out "Hygeia," the Greek goddess of health</note> placed within the points and center. To the right is the label "The Token of Antiochus."</image-desc>

<image-desc>A rectangular frame containing the Chi-Rho monogram (☧) <note>A Christogram formed by overlapping the first two Greek letters of "Christ" (Χ and Ρ)</note> superimposed on a cross/anchor-like base. To the right is the label "The Token of Constantine the Great."</image-desc>

<margin>This is *hygeia* <note>original: "hygicia"</note> in Greek letters, which in Latin is interpreted as Health or Wholeness.</margin>

"Would it not be relevant," Marranus said, "to consider that which once appeared from above to Constantine the Great as a sign of God (as they then called the Cross) in the very hour of midday? It appeared before his entire army inscribed with Latin letters thus: **IN THIS SIGN, CONQUER.** And indeed, Constantine was victorious by that same sign; he was then chosen and hailed as the Emperor of the Romans by the applause of the people, and was titled the most invincible of all emperors. Therefore, the highest men shall be witnesses to how much power seals and signs possess: for the Jews, it was Maccabaeus; for the Greeks, Antiochus; and for the Romans, Constantine.

Nor does it escape you, Simon, what you spoke of a little earlier regarding the Christians. For among those people, nothing in this age is more admirable in the crafting of signs, characters, and words than those who, by the figure of the Cross and the name of **JESUS**, still the seas, mitigate the winds, and repel lightning. Furthermore, there is nothing stronger than that character and image of the Cross, and nothing more life-saving in dangers—though (to speak freely) for no other reason than that they stand as the symbol of the true Savior, just as the name יהוה <note>The four-letter name of God, Yahweh</note>, that <term>TETRAGRAMMATON</term> <note>The "Four-Lettered Name" of God, considered too holy to pronounce in Jewish tradition</note>, is the symbol of God for you. What the <term>Kabbalists</term> <note>Scholars of Jewish mysticism</note> can achieve through the Ineffable Name, along with the seals and characters you recently demonstrated, the faithful Christians can achieve in a much more powerful way through the pronounceable name of **JESUS**, combined with the specific sign of the cross. They believe they pronounce the name Tetragrammaton far more correctly in the name ישוה <note>Yeheshuah; a Kabbalistic spelling of Jesus's name that inserts the letter 'Shin' into the center of the Tetragrammaton</note>, the name of the true Messiah. To this end, they cite what your own people wrote in the *Midrash Tehillim* <note>A traditional Jewish commentary on the Book of Psalms</note>:

> Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said in the name of Rabbi Phineas ben Yair: For what reason does Israel pray in this world and is not answered? It is because they do not know the *Shem HaMephorash* <note>The "Explicit Name" or "Distinct Name" of God</note>.

That is to say, the Tetragrammaton name. Thus it is written there. Then Simon replied: 'Perhaps you are right. But why waste words? Certainly, the wiser <term>Kabbalists</term> wish to relate this figure of the cross to the wooden pole of the bronze serpent erected in the desert, though they do so very silently and secretly. They do this through <term>GEMATRIA</term> <note>A system of Hebrew numerology where letters have numerical values</note>, that is, by the equality of numbers. For the characters of *Tzelem* <note>צלם — meaning "image" or "form," here used for the cross</note> and those of *Etz* <note>עץ — meaning "wood" or "tree"</note> both symbolize one hundred and fifty <note>The author calculates the value as 150, though standard Gematria for these words sums to 160; he likely uses a variant system or makes a point about their equivalence</note> on both sides. Wherefore the transition from one to the other is easy: from the cross to the wood, and from the wood to the cross. But I press my finger to my lip. Shortness of time constrains me, best of friends, so that I have said less than I wished. And yet I reluctantly deprive myself of that growing joy regarding the ornament...'

<summary>Marranus discusses the historical and mystical power of the Cross and the name of Jesus, comparing them to the Jewish Tetragrammaton. Simon the Kabbalist confirms a secret numerical link (Gematria) between the Cross and the Bronze Serpent of Moses.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the speech of Simon the Kabbalist in response to Marranus. It transitions from a discussion of signs and names to the grave responsibility and danger inherent in the Kabbalistic art, specifically regarding the hierarchy of spiritual beings (angels and demons) and the correspondence between the earthly and heavenly realms.</meta>

### BOOK III.

...by the ornament and dignity of your speech, I might fail in such a dense night when it is time to rest. You do not dispute with me as the Sophists do—with common, trifling, and meager talk—nor with a gladiator-like battle of words or a clash of opinions. Rather, you speak with an accurate and sharp method of reasoning, using insights that are fit and suited to the matter at hand, such that I might wish longer stretches of days were granted to us. For no one can speak sufficiently about the <term>Kabbalistic art<note>The mystical Jewish tradition of interpreting the Bible through secret meanings and spiritual structures.</note></term> in a short moment. These matters are so great, so deep, so numerous, and so fraught with distinction that anyone eager and studious of this cause must strive with the greatest powers of their intellect. 

One must look around not only at the industry with which it must be learned, but also the danger with which it must be moderated and practiced. For since this is a science of spiritual things, and is itself spiritual, a human cannot easily offer judgment concerning spirits—even one to whom the power of judging between angels and demons has been granted. Such judgment requires every bit of discrete weighing, even to the point of a perfectly balanced rule. Truly, this faculty and exercise are not rightly undertaken without much trembling, and unless one’s character has first been purified. This is so that we do not suffer the fate of the prophet Balaam <note>The biblical figure who attempted to curse Israel but was warned by an angel; he is often cited as a cautionary tale of a seer with impure motives.</note>, nor imitate the mother of the living <note>A reference to Eve, specifically regarding the Fall and the pursuit of forbidden knowledge.</note>, nor follow darkness under the appearance of light. 

Fear for yourselves these spirits cast down by lightning, who are our most savage enemies. And believe me, just as the angels do, so the devils carry their own banners among us mortals. In the army of God, there are four standard-bearers: **Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael** <note>original Hebrew: מיכאל גבריאל אוריאל רפאל</note>. They are like the four elements, according to the four positions, or according to the four spiritual enumerations, just as the children of Israel once set out under four banners. <margin>Numbers 2</margin> In the East was Judah, in the South was Reuben, in the West was Ephraim, and Dan was in the North. 

In the same way, in the army of Satan, the avenging standard-bearers carry very wide veils: **Samael, Azazel, Azahel, and Mahazael** <note>original Hebrew: סמאל עזאזל עזאל מחזאל</note>. Regarding these, Menachem Recanati <note>A 13th-century Italian Kabbalist known for his commentary on the Torah.</note> treats the discourse in his commentary on Leviticus 16 and in his first book on the Pentateuch; in that place, even Targum Jonathan <note>An ancient Aramaic translation and interpretation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> himself makes an allegation regarding Genesis. Furthermore, there are still great, increasing crowds of demons and legions, all fugitives and exiles of the abyss, having their portion in the **scapegoat** <note>The "goat for Azazel" mentioned in Leviticus 16, which carried the sins of the people into the wilderness.</note>. I will omit reciting these here because of their foulness and error, although a great part of them are included in Holy Scripture.

But I now make an end of speaking with a proverb of the Kabbalists: **The prudent will understand** <note>original Hebrew: המשכיל יבין</note>. I shall add only this: that just as Michael is **the High Priest** <note>original Hebrew: הוא הכהן הגדול</note>, sacrificing in the upper world, he presents the immaculate souls of men to the Blessed God; however, those that are unclean and burdened with vices, he sends to the devil. In the same way, the High Priest in the lower world, as it is written in Leviticus, is commanded to offer clean and innocent animals to God, but to deliver over to Satan those things burdened by crimes and the weight of guilt. The Kabbalists diligently approve of this, saying: **For all lower things are images of the higher** <note>original Hebrew: כי כל הענינים התחתונים הם דוגמתם לעליונים</note>, and **according to what is done below, so it is done above** <note>original Hebrew: וכפי העשוה למטה כך נעשה למעלה</note>.

<summary>Simon warns that the Kabbalistic study of spirits requires extreme moral purity to avoid demonic deception. He describes the hierarchical organization of both angelic and demonic "armies," concluding with the Kabbalistic principle of correspondence between the earthly priesthood and the heavenly ministry of Michael.</summary>

### THE KABBALAH, BOOK III.

...are representative of higher things, and as it is done below, so it is conducted above. These matters tend toward something owed both to virtues and to vices, so that each person must be careful how they live and in what manner they die. For our entire philosophy is this: that by living well, we may die well; lest perhaps we become the portion of <term>Tartarus<note>In classical mythology, the deep abyss used as a dungeon of torment; here used to represent Hell or a state of spiritual ruin.</note></term> and the avenging furies with all hope frustrated, and then evil befalls the evil man. Now, what greatly pains me, I think, is that we must depart, since from morning until night I have chatted with you more loquaciously than was fitting. For just as I make a kind guess about myself, I judge no differently of you: that sleep invites us to retire for rest.

Then they said: "We are torn away from you so reluctantly, Simon, for we wish to hear you forever; therefore, regarding 'loquacity,' let not even a word be said. But since you so command, we will comply with your wish and depart, intending to return to you tomorrow, unless it is inconvenient for you."

To this Simon said: "I cannot hide from you, my friends, what I have decided. Tomorrow I will travel to distant parts, having been summoned for a wedding, because my uncle has taken a wife in <term>Regensburg<note>Original: "Ratisponte," the Latin name for the city of Regensburg in Bavaria.</note></term>; may the matter turn out well."

Then Philolaus said: "I would urge you with all my strength to stay, were it not unjust; for we are not born for ourselves alone <note>A reference to the famous principle from Cicero and Plato: "Non nobis solum nati sumus."</note> (I confess); we grant a portion of ourselves to our friends by their own right. Therefore, giving you our thanks, we pray for a blessed journey for you and your family."

At this, Marranus, touched by sadness, said: "Go with <term>favorable omens<note>Original: "sinistris auibus," literally "left-hand birds." In Roman augury, omens from the left were considered lucky.</note></term>, prosperously and happily, dearest Simon, best of men. Meanwhile, we are compelled to wait for the end of the <term>Frankfurt fairs<note>The Frankfurt Trade Fair (nundinae Francofordienses) was the most important commercial and intellectual hub in early modern Europe, where books and ideas were exchanged alongside goods.</note></term> so that we might return from this marketplace to our own countries more safely with our local merchants."

Then Simon said, according to the <term>custom of his people<note>Original: "de more Gentilico," referring to Simon's Jewish background. The greeting "Pax uobis" is a translation of "Shalom aleichem" (Peace be unto you).</note></term>: "Peace be unto you." To which both of them replied: "Farewell, our honor,

<meta>This page serves as a formal dedication following the conclusion of the three books of "De Arte Cabalistica." After the dialogue between Simon, Philolaus, and Marranus ends, Johannes Reuchlin (writing under his pen name Capnio) addresses Pope Leo X directly to present his work and defend himself against his theological detractors in Cologne.</meta>

# TO LEO X, FROM CAPNIO.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'H' featuring a figure, likely a scholar, seated in a landscape or study environment within the frame of the letter.</image-desc>

You have here, Most Holy Leo the Tenth, from <term>Capnio<note>The Greek-derived name (meaning "smoky") used by Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and scholar of Greek and Hebrew.</note></term>, your humble servant, the opinions and sentences of the ancients recited in a brief summary concerning the symbolic philosophy of Pythagoras and the wisdom of the Kabbalah. Though these are few in number, they may provide to studious men a much wider handle for reflection and investigation. Regarding these matters, I—a man of modest talent and small prudence—would not dare to judge anything, nor indeed shall I; rather, I submit this entire book to your authority, into whose judgment the censorship of the entire world has been granted. May you reject what is displeasing, and then I shall rejoice that the rest has pleased you. I trust that this effort of mine, which you may consider I have undertaken for the sake of our people and the Republic, will not seem entirely improper to you. This is partly because, through my labor, the works of others are made open to our people, and partly because by reading these during this half-year, I have sought to lighten—if it could not be avoided altogether—that five-year war which my enemies have waged against me with your knowledge. Finally, I desired that there might be something of mine in your possession, so that your memory of us might be more benevolent whenever enemies strive to break or turn away your fatherly mind from me.

For they do not cease, I know, to daily attempt to reach your pious ears with whispers, now through hired agents, now through letters—such as those I recently read, addressed to you on the fourteenth day before the <term>Kalends of October<note>Original: "decimoquarto calend. Octobres," referring to September 18th.</note></term> from <term>Cologne<note>Original: "Agrippina Colonia," the Roman name for the city of Cologne.</note></term>, in which the title lies about the author just as the false accusation does. For it was not that venerable city of Cologne, nor its revered University, but rather a "particularity" and a certain gathering of individual enemies—the smallest and most insane part of the city—that committed this outrage of affirming to your Holiness things that are not true. This they did against apostolic prohibitions and against the peace commanded by the Emperor.

You see also what great audacity is in those same letters, as they presume to prescribe laws to you as if they were <term>Solonian<note>Referring to Solon, the famous lawmaker of ancient Athens; here Reuchlin suggests his enemies are arrogantly trying to dictate the law to the Pope.</note></term>, and to teach you the fountain of the Law. They dictate the path by which the judgment should proceed according to their whim and will, so that they might more easily overwhelm me with filth—as if my innocence were not already held as a certainty by almost the entire world. Hence I cannot be led to suspect that you have faith in those who, having despised the apostolic prohibition and held your censures in contempt, burned my little book while the lawsuit was still pending, observing the path of the Law as little as possible. You will instead believe the more grave men of Upper Germany, who are beyond all exception, that I have placed no scandal and provided no occasion for ruin before any of the German people. These people are joined to me by the fellowship of the same language, in which language—unknown to those <term>Belgians<note>Original: "Belgis." Reuchlin uses this term loosely to refer to the people of the lower Rhine/Cologne region, contrasting them with the "Upper Germans" who supported him.</note></term>—I published that <term>Chamber Counsel<note>Original: "Consilium meum illud Camerarium," referring to his legal defense or possibly his work the *Augenspiegel* (Eye-Glass), written in German to explain his position on Jewish books.</note></term> with its plain declaration in a single context, as was fitting. And you can believe this securely—and all the more firmly because concerning my innocence, piety, faith, and integrity, by many...

<meta>The catchword "à pluribus" (by many) indicates the text continues on the next page with further testimonies of Reuchlin's character.</meta>

<summary>In this dedication to Pope Leo X, Johannes Reuchlin (Capnio) presents his work on Pythagorean and Kabbalistic philosophy while defending himself against the theologians of Cologne. He portrays his enemies as a radical minority who have defied papal and imperial authority by burning his books during an ongoing legal dispute.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Reuchlin’s formal appeal to Pope Leo X. Having presented his book on the Kabbalah, he now transitions into a legal and political defense of his character against the accusations of the Cologne theologians, listing the powerful European figures who support his cause.</meta>

### KABBALAH

...by many most illustrious rulers of the widest lands of our nation, by magistrates, and by the peoples of the Germans, as well as by the most holy Bishops of our dioceses, towns, and cities, you were made certain almost three years ago through sealed and trustworthy letters. There exist in your possession three and four times over the testimonies offered for my innocence by the invincible elected Emperor of the Romans, Maximilian; by Matthew <note>Matthew Lang von Wellenburg (1468–1540), a powerful diplomat and Cardinal of Gurk.</note> to you; and by my lord the most reverend Cardinal of Gurk.

And following the Bishops, the most illustrious governors and Dukes of the provinces, born of the noblest blood, gave their testimony: the Electors of the Empire, Frederick of Saxony <note>Frederick the Wise (1463–1525), later the protector of Martin Luther.</note> and Louis of Bavaria, the Interrex; and the Duke of Württemberg; and the Margrave of Baden, a Prince; and the most strenuous Master of the Teutonic Order. And alongside these are the reverend and God-beloved prelates of Germany: the Bishop of Worms, the Bishop of Strasbourg, the Bishop of Constance (who acknowledges me as a sheep of his own flock), and the Bishop of Speyer—the very judge assigned by your Holiness to this dispute. Exercising your authority and following the counsel of experts, he delivered a definitive sentence in favor of my innocence and that of my writings. 

Equally with them, fifty-three towns of Swabia—all most dutiful, brave, and upright men—gave commendatory letters and documents of right faith as witnesses of my integrity and my freedom from harm. To their testimony, prelates of the Church of distinguished learning and gravity add strength and weight. These men you joined as senatorial assessors and lights of the world to the most reverend judges of our cause, Cardinals Grimani <note>Domenico Grimani (1461–1523), a noted patron of arts and Hebrew studies.</note> and Anconitano <note>Pietro Accolti (1455–1532), the Cardinal of Ancona.</note>, who are columns of the Orthodox faith. 

Archbishops, Bishops, Generals of Orders and their Proctors, magistrates of the Roman Wisdom <term>Sapientiæ Romanæ<note>Likely referring to the Sapienza University of Rome or the Roman Curia's legal experts.</note></term>, Penitentiaries, and other most select Doctors of Theology and Law—each to be named in the history of my times according to their dignities—were present for so many public sessions held in your Majesty’s domestic sanctuary, which they call the Papal Chapel. Throughout these sessions, my advocate, the most learned in law John Vanderbick <note>Johannes von der Wick, Reuchlin’s legal representative in Rome.</note>—a man as noble in his knightly rank as he is a sharp debater in the defense of causes—faithfully acted as my Proctor. 

Finally, in the last session, the cause having been fully examined, they decreed through written sentences that I should be freed from this injurious persecution and acquitted. Nor is there any doubt that the definitive sentence from the same oracle of the most reverend judges would have followed, as it ought to have, had the accusers not then obtained from you a mandate for staying the proceedings <term>supersedendo<note>A legal order to halt or stay a proceeding.</note></term>, as they claimed. 

If you will recall the testimonies and vows of all those whom we have now cited from every side, and if you will take care to read the acts of the judgments in your presence, you will clearly find me to be entirely foreign to every insinuation of my accusers. Almost the entire city of Rome leaps to support this purity of mine, as do all the most learned men of all nations, whose decrees I...

### BOOK III.

Every day I receive letters, even from the ends of the earth, confirming that I have never been a cause of scandal to any person through my writings; on the contrary, that I daily build up and plant the Church for the Holy Spirit <gloss>and</gloss> in various languages—the Spirit who, through the diversity of all tongues, gathered the nations into the unity of faith. For they surely observe that I was the first of all to bring back Greek studies to Germany, and the first of all to grant and hand down the art and study of the Hebrew language <gloss>and</gloss> to the universal Church. Therefore I hope, and I trust I do not hope in vain, that the future of the Church will not be ungrateful for my merits, and that you yourself in the present, most blessed Leo, Supreme Pontiff <note>Pope Leo X (reigned 1513–1521), to whom this defense is addressed.</note>, a judge of deeds rather than words, will justly restore peace and tranquility of mind to me in exchange for so many and such arduous labors contributed as a benefit to the Orthodox <note>original: "Orthodoxam fidem"; in this context, Reuchlin refers to the established, "right-believing" Catholic faith.</note> faith. But if you truly desire me to remain perpetually subject to the persecution of wicked men in this life,

# ON THE CABALA

<note>original: "CABALÆ"; Reuchlin's work *De Arte Cabalistica* was dedicated to Pope Leo X as part of his defense strategy.</note>

You were made certain [of my innocence] nearly three years ago by many most illustrious rulers of the vast lands of our nation, by the magistrates and people of the Germans, and by the most holy Bishops of our Dioceses, through signed letters of reliable credit. There exist in your possession repeated testimonies offered for my innocence from the invincible Maximilian, Emperor-elect of the Romans, addressed to you as "Maximilian the Great Lion" <note>Maximilianus Maximoleoni: a play on the names of Emperor Maximilian I and Pope Leo X.</note>, and from the most reverend Cardinal, my lord of Gurk. After the Bishops, the most illustrious governors of the provinces and Dukes of noble blood also gave [testimonies]: the Electors of the Empire, Frederick of Saxony and Louis of Bavaria (the Regent), the Duke of Württemberg, the Marquis Prince of Baden, and the most valiant Master of the Teutonic Order. 

Alongside these were the reverend and God-beloved German prelates: the Bishop of Worms, the Bishop of Strasbourg, the Bishop of Constance (who acknowledges me as his own sheep <note>Meaning Reuchlin was a resident of the Diocese of Constance.</note>), and the Bishop of Speyer—that judge assigned by your Holiness to this lawsuit, who, acting by your authority and by the advice of experts, delivered a definitive sentence in favor of my innocence and that of my writings. Together with them, fifty-three towns of Swabia—all most dutiful, brave, and upright men—gave letters of recommendation and testimony of my true faith, integrity, and safety from harm. 

To their testimony, strength and weight are added by the prelates of the Church, men of distinguished learning and gravity, whom you joined as Senatorial assessors and lights of the world to the most reverend judges of our cause, Cardinals Grimani and of Ancona <note>Domenico Grimani and Pietro Accolti (Cardinal of Ancona), the high-ranking officials overseeing the case in Rome.</note>—pillars of the Orthodox faith—like a surrounding colonnade. These include Archbishops, Bishops, Generals of Religious Orders, and their Proctors, magistrates of Roman Wisdom, Penitentiaries, and other most choice Doctors of Theology and Law, each to be named in the history of my times according to their dignities. 

In many public sessions held in your Majesty’s domestic sanctuary, which they call the Papal Chapel, my most learned legal advocate Johannes Vanderbicus <note>Jan van der Wyck, a Dutch jurist who served as Reuchlin’s legal representative in Rome.</note>—a man as noble in the equestrian order as he is a fierce debater in legal defenses and also my Procurator—always acted on my behalf (as he does everything faithfully). Finally, in the last session, after the case was fully heard, they decreed through sentences issued in writing that I should be freed and acquitted from this injurious persecution. 

Nor is there any doubt that a definitive sentence from the same oracle of the most reverend judges would have followed, as was proper, had the accusers not then obtained from you a mandate to suspend the proceedings <note>original: "mandatum de supersedendo"; a legal stay or suspension of the trial.</note>, as they claim. If you recall the testimonies and desires of all these whom we have now cited, and if you take care to have the acts of the trials read before you, you will clearly find me to be entirely removed from every accusation of the informers. Nearly the whole city of Rome leaps to support my purity, as do all the most learned men of all nations, whose decrees I [receive] daily...

<header>BOOK III.</header>

<warning>The text on this page is extremely faded, likely due to ink degradation or light printing. Transcription is based on available visual cues.</warning>

...pleasant things, and by that means they are preserved in the remaining ends of the world: so that they may be sacrificed to the good, having established a firm foundation of justice. This is because it is no different than building and planting on solid ground, which in the Hebrew language sounds like **Zion** <note>original: "Sion"; Zion is often used by Reuchlin to symbolize the spiritual foundation or the "citadel" of the faith.</note>, who gathers the Christian nation of Christians from the conscience of the heart.

From this, we must remember that the first Christian church in the regions of Gaul <term>Gaul (Galliis): The Roman name for the region comprising modern-day France, Belgium, and parts of neighboring countries.</term> was established in the city of Lyon <term>Lyon (Lugdunum): A major Roman administrative center in Gaul and the site of the earliest well-documented Christian community in the region.</term>, under the leadership of **Saint Pothinus** <note>Saint Pothinus (c. 87–177 AD) was the first Bishop of Lyon and died as a martyr during the persecutions under Emperor Marcus Aurelius.</note>, to whose faith and devotion the faithfulness of his successor should correspond. And lest you here spend your time on promises rather than being seen to stand firm in the knowledge of the truth, it can be gathered from the *Letter of the People of Lyon* to the brothers who were in Asia and Phrygia: from which it is clear, etc. <note>This refers to a famous 2nd-century primary source preserved by the historian Eusebius, describing the trials of the martyrs of Lyon.</note>

We conclude that the Orthodox faith <note>original: "Orthodoxam fidem"; meaning the "right-believing" or established Christian faith.</note> flourished here in Gaul, and that it, like a precious and delightful flower, seems to have driven away the heresies of pride and the rot of vices together by its scent. Let there be, therefore, types of men worthy of their rank, whom they do not ignore.

<meta>This page serves as the colophon, or concluding statement, of the volume. It follows the extensive scriptural and thematic indices that concluded the previous section. This final leaf provides the publication details and the printer's register, ensuring that the bookbinder has assembled the various sections of Pietro Galatino’s "On the Secrets of Catholic Truth" and Johannes Reuchlin’s "On the Art of the Kabbalah" in the correct sequence.</meta>

# THE END OF THE WORK OF PIETRO GALATINO
## AND OF THE KABBALAH OF REUCHLIN <note>Original: *Cabalæ Revchlini*. This refers to Johannes Reuchlin’s influential work *De Arte Cabalistica* (1517), which was often bound together with Galatino's work in later editions.</note>
## WITH THEIR INDICES.

---

## Printed at Basel by Johannes
## Herwagen, in the Year
## of the Lord 1550.

---

->*The sequence of sheets*<- <note>Original: *Series chartarum*. This is a printer’s register, a list of the "signatures" (the letters printed at the bottom of pages) used to guide the bookbinder in gathering the folded sheets in the correct order.</note>

AA BB a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r s t u x y z
A B C D E F G H I K L M N O P Q R S T
V X Y Z aa bb cc dd ee ff gg hh ii kk ll mm
nn oo pp qq rr ss tt uu xx yy zz

->*All are <term>ternions</term>, except for yy*<- <note>A <term>ternion</term> (Latin: *ternio*) is a gathering of three folded sheets of paper, resulting in six leaves or twelve pages.</note>
->*which is a <term>duernion</term>.*<- <note>A <term>duernion</term> (Latin: *duernio*) is a gathering of two folded sheets of paper, resulting in four leaves or eight pages.</note>

<summary>This is the colophon of the 1550 Basel edition of works by Pietro Galatino and Johannes Reuchlin, providing the printer's name (Johannes Herwagen) and a register for bookbinders.</summary>
